description: UPSC CSE 2026 Mains runs 21 to 30 August for 933 posts. Check the day-wise schedule, which papers actually count, the qualifying language trap and timings.
content:
## UPSC Civil Services 2026: Mains starts 21 August

UPSC Civil Services Examination 2026 is recruiting for 933 posts across the Group A and Group B services, and the Main examination begins on 21 August 2026. If you cleared the Preliminary examination, that is 17 days away at the time of writing.

The cycle so far: UPSC notified the examination on 4 February 2026, applications ran to 27 February, the Preliminary examination was held on 24 May 2026, and the Prelims result was declared on 15 June 2026. The Detailed Application Form I window ran from 19 to 28 June 2026. What remains is the Mains, then the Personality Test.

One thing worth fixing at the outset, because candidates lose marks to it every year. Two of the nine Mains papers do not count towards your rank at all, and two more decide almost everything. Getting that allocation wrong in the final fortnight is expensive, so the paper structure section below is the part of this page to read first.

## The Mains schedule, day by day

The Main examination runs across five days, with two sessions on each day.

| Date | Day |
|---|---|
| 21 August 2026 | Friday |
| 22 August 2026 | Saturday |
| 23 August 2026 | Sunday |
| 29 August 2026 | Friday |
| 30 August 2026 | Saturday |

Session timings are 9:00 am to 12:00 noon for the forenoon paper and 2:30 pm to 5:30 pm for the afternoon paper. Each paper is three hours.

Note the gap. The examination breaks after 23 August and resumes on 29 August, giving five clear days in between. That window usually falls before the optional subject papers, and how you use it matters: candidates who treat it as recovery time and candidates who treat it as revision time end up with noticeably different optional scores.

## Mains paper structure, and what actually counts

This is the table to internalise.

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Counts towards merit? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper A | Indian language | 300 | No, qualifying only |
| Paper B | English | 300 | No, qualifying only |
| Paper I | Essay | 250 | Yes |
| Paper II | General Studies I | 250 | Yes |
| Paper III | General Studies II | 250 | Yes |
| Paper IV | General Studies III | 250 | Yes |
| Paper V | General Studies IV | 250 | Yes |
| Paper VI | Optional Subject Paper I | 250 | Yes |
| Paper VII | Optional Subject Paper II | 250 | Yes |

Seven papers at 250 marks each gives 1,750 marks that count. The Personality Test adds 275. Final merit is therefore out of **2,025 marks**.

Papers A and B carry 600 marks between them and contribute nothing to your rank. They are pass or fail. The qualifying standard is modest, typically set around 25 per cent, but the consequence of failing is absolute: if you do not clear Paper A or Paper B, UPSC does not evaluate your other seven papers at all. A candidate can write an excellent Essay, four strong General Studies papers and two good optional papers, and have none of them read.

Candidates from English-medium backgrounds underestimate Paper A, the Indian language paper. Candidates educated in regional-medium schools sometimes underestimate Paper B. Both mistakes end the attempt in exactly the same way, and both are avoidable with a few hours of practice on the prescribed formats: comprehension, précis, translation, and short composition.

## Where the marks are actually decided

Of the 1,750 counted marks, the optional subject carries 500 across two papers. That is more than any single General Studies paper and more than the Essay. It is also the most controllable component, because it is a defined syllabus you have studied for months rather than an open-ended current affairs canvas.

The four General Studies papers carry 1,000 marks combined. General Studies IV, the ethics paper, is the one candidates most often underprepare and the one where marks move most for modest effort, because a structured approach to case studies produces visible gains.

The Essay at 250 marks is a single paper with two essays of 125 marks each. It rewards structure and breadth of illustration rather than specialised knowledge, and it is frequently the difference between a rank and a near miss.

## Prelims pattern, for the next cycle

If you are targeting CSE 2027, the Preliminary examination is where the funnel narrows hardest.

| Paper | Content | Questions | Marks | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper I | General Studies | 100 | 200 | Decides who reaches Mains |
| Paper II | CSAT (aptitude) | 80 | 200 | Qualifying at 33 per cent |

Both papers are objective with negative marking, and both are two hours. Paper II being qualifying at 33 per cent means you need 66.7 marks out of 200 to pass it, and marks above that add nothing. Paper I alone decides the Prelims cutoff.

Prelims marks do not carry into the Mains or the final merit. They exist only to shortlist. That is worth remembering, because candidates sometimes treat a high Prelims score as a head start, and it is not one.

## Vacancies

CSE 2026 carries 933 vacancies, including 33 reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. These are distributed across the services, and the service-wise split is finalised later in the cycle rather than announced with the notification.

The services filled through this examination include the Indian Administrative Service, the Indian Police Service, the Indian Foreign Service, the Indian Revenue Service in both Income Tax and Customs and Indirect Taxes, the Indian Audit and Accounts Service, the Indian Railway Management Service, the Indian Defence Accounts Service, the Indian Information Service, and several other Group A and Group B services including the DANICS and DANIPS cadres.

Service allocation depends on your final rank and the preferences you submit in the Detailed Application Form, along with category and cadre rules. The top ranks generally clear IAS and IFS; the range of services accessible widens considerably as you move down the list.

## Eligibility

On age, candidates must be between 21 and 32 years as on 1 August 2026, with relaxation of 3 years for OBC candidates, 5 years for SC and ST candidates, and further relaxation for defence service personnel, ex-servicemen and PwBD candidates as specified.

On attempts, general category candidates get 6 attempts, OBC candidates get 9, and SC and ST candidates have no numerical limit but remain bound by the upper age limit. PwBD candidates get 9 attempts in the general and OBC categories. An attempt counts when you appear in at least one paper of the Preliminary examination.

On education, a bachelor's degree from a recognised university is required. Final-year students may apply for the Preliminary examination but must produce proof of passing before the Mains.

The application fee is Rs 100 for general, OBC and EWS male candidates. Female candidates and SC, ST and PwBD candidates pay nothing.

## Salary and what the job pays

An officer entering through this examination begins at Level 10 of the pay matrix with a basic pay of Rs 56,100 a month, plus dearness allowance, house rent allowance by city class, and transport allowance. Gross monthly pay at entry commonly works out well above the basic figure.

Progression runs through defined stages: Junior Time Scale at Level 10, Senior Time Scale at Level 11, Junior Administrative Grade at Level 12, Selection Grade at Level 13, Super Time Scale at Level 14, and upward to Level 15, 16, 17 and finally Level 18 for a Cabinet Secretary at Rs 2,50,000.

The non-cash side is substantial and frequently understated in comparisons: official accommodation, official vehicle and staff at appropriate levels, medical facilities, security of tenure, and pension benefits under the applicable rules. The counterweight is genuine and worth stating too: postings are transferable, early district assignments can be remote, and the working hours in field postings are long.

## Preparing in the final fortnight

With the Mains 17 days out, the useful moves are narrow and specific.

Stop consuming new material. Two weeks before a descriptive examination, the marginal value of a new source is near zero and the cost in revision time is real. Work from notes you already have.

Write full-length papers under the clock. Three hours, 20 questions, by hand. Mains is as much an endurance and time-allocation problem as a knowledge one, and candidates who have not written a full paper in weeks discover on day one that their hand tires and their last five answers suffer.

Confirm your language papers are safe. If Paper A or Paper B is a genuine risk for you, a few hours on the prescribed formats is the highest-return time available anywhere in this fortnight, because it protects all 1,750 of your other marks.

Revise the optional. It carries 500 marks, it is the most controllable component, and the five-day gap from 24 to 28 August exists precisely for this.

Prepare answer structure rather than content for General Studies IV. Ethics case studies reward a consistent framework applied calmly far more than they reward remembering thinkers. Settle on a template you can apply to any dilemma: identify the stakeholders, name the competing values, set out the options with their consequences, then commit to a decision and justify it. Applying one reliable structure under time pressure beats recalling a dozen philosophers you cannot deploy.

## What the four General Studies papers cover

Knowing the boundaries between them matters, because Mains questions are set to a paper's remit and answers that drift into another paper's territory lose marks.

General Studies I covers Indian heritage and culture, modern Indian history and the freedom struggle, post-independence consolidation, world history, Indian society, and physical geography including resource distribution and geophysical phenomena.

General Studies II covers the Constitution, polity, governance, social justice and international relations: the structure and functioning of the executive, legislature and judiciary, devolution of powers, statutory and constitutional bodies, government policies and interventions, welfare schemes, and India's relations with its neighbourhood and the wider world.

General Studies III covers the economy, agriculture, science and technology, environment, internal security and disaster management: growth and development, budgeting, cropping patterns, food processing, land reforms, infrastructure, technology missions, biodiversity, and security challenges including cyber security and money laundering.

General Studies IV covers ethics, integrity and aptitude, tested largely through case studies. It examines attitude, emotional intelligence, public service values, probity in governance, and the application of ethical reasoning to administrative dilemmas.

Current affairs cut across all four rather than sitting in any one of them, which is why a standalone current affairs approach works less well than mapping developments onto the relevant paper as you read them. A single news development on, say, a river-linking project can supply material for geography in Paper I, federal disputes in Paper II, and environmental impact in Paper III, and the candidate who files it three ways has three usable answers rather than one.

## Exam day practicalities

Carry your e-admit card and the photo identity document specified on it. UPSC is strict on both and admits nobody without them.

Reach the centre well before the reporting time. Gates close ahead of the session start and UPSC does not admit latecomers, in either the forenoon or the afternoon session.

Take only permitted items. Mobile phones, smart watches, electronic devices and any communication equipment are barred, and centres do not reliably offer storage. Carry black ballpoint pens, since answer scripts must be written in black ink.

Plan the lunch gap on the three double-paper days. The break between a 12:00 noon finish and a 2:30 pm start is short once you account for exit and re-entry queues, and candidates who skip food entirely tend to fade in the afternoon paper.

## After the Mains

Results follow some weeks after the last paper. Candidates who clear the Mains submit the Detailed Application Form II and are called for the Personality Test, worth 275 marks, held at UPSC's office in New Delhi.

The Personality Test is not a knowledge examination. The board assesses clarity of thought, balance of judgement, depth of interest, and suitability for a career in public service, drawing heavily on your DAF: your home state, your graduation subject, your hobbies, your service preferences and your work experience. Everything you entered there is fair material for questioning, which is why the DAF deserves care when you fill it.

Final merit combines the Mains 1,750 and the Personality Test 275 for a total of 2,025 marks. Service allocation follows from that rank and your stated preferences.

Candidates who do not clear this stage should note that the preparation transfers directly. The [UPSC CDS](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-cds-ii-2026) route into the armed forces, the [UPSC CAPF Assistant Commandant](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-capf-ac-2026) route into the paramilitary, and state public service commission examinations all draw on substantially the same base.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the UPSC Mains 2026 exam?**
The UPSC Civil Services Main examination 2026 is held on 21, 22, 23, 29 and 30 August 2026, across five days with two sessions each day. The forenoon session runs from 9:00 am to 12:00 noon and the afternoon session from 2:30 pm to 5:30 pm, with every paper lasting three hours. Note the five-day gap between 23 and 29 August.

**How many vacancies are in UPSC CSE 2026?**
There are 933 vacancies, including 33 reserved for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. They cover the Indian Administrative Service, Indian Police Service, Indian Foreign Service, Indian Revenue Service and other Group A and Group B services. The service-wise split is finalised later in the cycle rather than announced with the February notification.

**Which UPSC Mains papers count towards the final merit?**
Seven of the nine papers count: the Essay, the four General Studies papers, and the two optional subject papers, at 250 marks each for a total of 1,750. Paper A, the Indian language paper, and Paper B, English, carry 300 marks each but are qualifying only and contribute nothing to your rank. The Personality Test adds 275, making the final merit out of 2,025 marks.

**What happens if I fail the UPSC language papers?**
Your other seven papers are not evaluated at all. Papers A and B are qualifying, typically at around 25 per cent, and failing either means UPSC does not assess your Essay, General Studies or optional papers, however well you wrote them. This is why a few hours of format practice on comprehension, précis and translation is the highest-return preparation available to anyone at risk.

**What is the UPSC CSE 2026 exam schedule so far?**
UPSC notified the examination on 4 February 2026 with applications open to 27 February and a correction window from 28 February to 3 March. The Preliminary examination was held on 24 May 2026 and its result was declared on 15 June 2026. The Detailed Application Form I window ran from 19 to 28 June 2026, and the Main examination runs from 21 to 30 August 2026.

**What is the age limit and attempt limit for UPSC CSE?**
Candidates must be 21 to 32 years as on 1 August 2026, with 3 years relaxation for OBC and 5 years for SC and ST candidates, plus further relaxation for defence personnel, ex-servicemen and PwBD candidates. General category candidates get 6 attempts, OBC candidates 9, and SC and ST candidates have no numerical cap but remain bound by the age limit. An attempt counts once you appear in any Preliminary paper.

**Do UPSC Prelims marks count in the final merit?**
No. The Preliminary examination is only a screening stage and its marks do not carry into the Mains or the final ranking. Paper II, the CSAT, is itself qualifying at 33 per cent, meaning 66.7 marks out of 200, with anything above that adding nothing. Only Paper I decides who reaches the Mains.

**What is the salary of an IAS officer?**
Entry is at Level 10 of the pay matrix with a basic pay of Rs 56,100 a month, plus dearness allowance, house rent allowance by city class and transport allowance. Progression runs through Level 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17, up to Level 18 at Rs 2,50,000 for a Cabinet Secretary. Official accommodation, transport, medical facilities and pension benefits add substantially to the package.

**How much weight does the optional subject carry in UPSC Mains?**
The optional subject carries 500 marks across two papers of 250 each, which is more than any single General Studies paper and more than the Essay. It is also the most controllable component of the Mains, since it follows a defined syllabus rather than an open-ended current affairs range, which makes it the highest-priority revision target in the final weeks.

**What should I carry to the UPSC Mains exam?**
Your e-admit card and the photo identity document specified on it, plus black ballpoint pens, since answer scripts must be written in black ink. Mobile phones, smart watches, electronic devices and communication equipment are prohibited, and centres do not reliably provide storage. Arrive well before the reporting time, as gates close ahead of the session start and latecomers are not admitted.

**What happens after the UPSC Mains examination?**
Results are declared some weeks after the final paper. Candidates who qualify submit the Detailed Application Form II and are called for the Personality Test at UPSC's office in New Delhi, worth 275 marks. The board draws heavily on your DAF, covering your home state, graduation subject, hobbies, work experience and service preferences, so those entries should be filled with care.

**Which services are filled through UPSC CSE?**
The Indian Administrative Service, Indian Police Service, Indian Foreign Service, Indian Revenue Service in both Income Tax and Customs and Indirect Taxes, Indian Audit and Accounts Service, Indian Railway Management Service, Indian Defence Accounts Service, Indian Information Service, and various other Group A and Group B services including DANICS and DANIPS. Allocation depends on your final rank, your stated preferences, and category and cadre rules.

content:
## DRDO DEAL Apprentice 2026: current status

The DRDO DEAL Apprentice 2026-27 recruitment offered 77 apprentice training seats at the Defence Electronics Applications Laboratory (DEAL) in Dehradun, a DRDO laboratory. The notification came out on 23 June 2026, and the application window closed around 22 July 2026. So the DEAL 2026 window is over, and if you missed it, this guide explains how DRDO apprenticeships work, which portal to register on in advance, the other DRDO labs that run apprentice drives, and how an apprenticeship differs from a permanent DRDO job.

One point is worth stating clearly up front, because it is the biggest misconception: a DRDO apprenticeship is a one-year training programme with a monthly stipend, not a permanent job. The DEAL notification itself says no employment, permanent, temporary, or contractual, is offered after the training. So an apprenticeship is a way to gain experience and a stipend at a DRDO lab for a year, and a stepping stone, not a government job in itself. The permanent DRDO jobs come through separate exams like DRDO CEPTAM and the RAC Scientist recruitment, covered below.

## DRDO DEAL Apprentice 2026 at a glance

The 77 seats split across three apprentice categories.

| Category | Seats | Who it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Graduate Apprentice | 19 | Engineering degree holders |
| Diploma Apprentice | 8 | Engineering diploma holders |
| ITI Apprentice (Trade) | 50 | ITI-certified trade holders |
| Total | 77 | |

The Graduate and Diploma seats were in disciplines like Electronics and Communication, Mechanical, Computer Science, and Electrical Engineering, plus Library Science. The ITI seats spanned around 21 trades, such as Electronics Mechanic, Fitter, Library Assistant, and Stenographer, which is why the ITI category carried the largest share of the 77 seats.

## Stipend for DRDO DEAL apprentices

Apprentices receive a monthly stipend, not a salary, and it is shared between DEAL and the government and paid by direct benefit transfer.

| Category | Monthly stipend |
|---|---|
| Graduate Apprentice | Rs 12,300 |
| Diploma Apprentice | Rs 10,900 |
| ITI Apprentice | Rs 10,560 |

Half of the stipend is paid by DEAL and half by the government through the relevant board, credited to the apprentice's bank account by direct benefit transfer. There is no application fee for DRDO apprenticeships. The training runs for one year, and the stipend rates are fixed under the apprenticeship scheme rather than negotiated, so every apprentice in a category receives the same amount. Note that some sites list the diploma stipend as Rs 10,981; the correct figure for this drive is Rs 10,900.

## What a DRDO apprenticeship actually is

This is the section that clears the most confusion. An apprenticeship is a structured training engagement under the Apprentices Act of 1961, in which a lab like DEAL trains a candidate for one year and pays a stipend. It is not employment. When the year ends, the apprentice receives a certificate of training, but the lab does not offer a job, and there is no bond or guarantee of one. The value of the apprenticeship is the hands-on experience at a DRDO lab, the certificate, and the stipend during the year, which many candidates use to strengthen their profile before sitting a permanent recruitment exam or applying elsewhere.

Because it is training rather than a job, the selection is usually merit-based on your qualifying-exam marks, with no written test, followed by document verification. This is very different from a permanent DRDO job, where a competitive exam decides selection.

## Apprentice vs a permanent DRDO job

Candidates often confuse the apprenticeship with permanent DRDO recruitment. They are entirely different. This comparison sets out the difference.

| Factor | DRDO Apprentice | DRDO CEPTAM | RAC Scientist B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nature | One-year training | Permanent job | Permanent job |
| Pay | Stipend (Rs 10,560 to 12,300) | Regular pay scale | Regular pay scale |
| Selection | Merit on qualifying marks | Written exam (CBT) | GATE score plus interview |
| Job at the end | No | Yes | Yes |
| Who it suits | Freshers seeking experience | Technicians and support staff | Engineers and researchers |

If your goal is a permanent DRDO job, the routes are [DRDO CEPTAM](/sarkari-naukri/drdo-ceptam-11-2026) for technician and support posts, decided by a computer-based test, and the RAC Scientist B recruitment for scientist posts, based on the GATE score and an interview. The apprenticeship is best seen as experience-building, not as a back door into these jobs.

## Eligibility for DRDO DEAL apprentice

The DEAL apprenticeship set these conditions, which are typical of DRDO apprentice drives.

- Indian nationals only.
- A regular, not distance or private, qualifying course.
- The qualifying exam passed between 2022 and 2026 only.
- No prior apprenticeship training and not more than one year of post-qualification work experience.
- You cannot apply with a qualification higher than the one prescribed for the category.
- Graduate: a BE or BTech with around 60 percent in the relevant discipline. Diploma: a relevant engineering diploma with around 60 percent. ITI: a National or State Council trade certificate.
- Age: a minimum of 18 years, with the upper age as per the Apprentices Act and the apprenticeship rules.

## NATS versus NAPS: which portal you register on

DRDO apprenticeships run through two national portals, and which one you use depends on your qualification. This trips up many candidates.

Graduate and Diploma apprentices register on the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme portal, NATS, at the education ministry's apprenticeship site. ITI and trade apprentices register on the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme portal, NAPS, at the apprenticeship India site. For a specific drive like DEAL, you also enter the lab's establishment code so your application reaches the right lab. There is no fee on either portal.

Registering on the right portal in advance, even before a notification you are interested in opens, is worth doing, because apprenticeship windows are often short. Having a complete NATS or NAPS profile ready means you can apply quickly when a lab you want opens a drive.

## How to apply for a DRDO apprenticeship

1. Identify your category, that is Graduate, Diploma, or ITI, based on your qualification.
2. Register on the correct portal: NATS for Graduate and Diploma, NAPS for ITI and trade.
3. Complete your profile with your qualification, marks, and bank details for the stipend transfer.
4. Find the lab's advertisement and enter its establishment or DEAL identification code so your application reaches it.
5. Submit before the last date. There is no application fee.
6. Watch for the merit list and document verification call, since selection is usually on qualifying-exam marks.

## Other DRDO labs that run apprentice drives

DEAL is one of many DRDO labs that take apprentices, and drives run through the year across labs, so if you missed DEAL, others open regularly. Recent examples include ACEM in Nashik, which advertised around 41 Graduate and Technician apprentice seats, INMAS in Delhi with around 38 seats, and GTRE in Bengaluru, which ran a large walk-in apprentice drive. The pattern is that DRDO labs across the country recruit apprentices year-round, each through its own short advertisement on NATS or NAPS. The practical way to catch them is to keep your portal profile ready and check the DRDO vacancies page and the apprenticeship portals regularly, rather than waiting for a single lab.

## What to do now that the DEAL 2026 window has closed

If you missed the DEAL 2026 window, there are three useful steps. First, register on NATS or NAPS now and complete your profile, so you are ready the moment another lab opens a drive. Second, watch the DRDO vacancies page and the apprenticeship portals for the next lab advertisement, since drives run through the year. Third, if your real goal is a permanent DRDO job rather than an apprenticeship, shift focus to DRDO CEPTAM for technician posts or the RAC Scientist recruitment for scientist posts, both of which are competitive exams that lead to actual employment. The next DEAL apprentice cycle is likely around mid-2027, following the annual pattern, though the exact timing depends on the lab's requirement and will be announced on the portals when it opens, so keep checking rather than assuming a fixed month.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready on your portal profile so you can apply quickly.

1. Your qualifying certificate and mark sheets, that is your degree, diploma, or ITI certificate.
2. Aadhaar and bank account details for the stipend direct benefit transfer.
3. A recent photograph and signature in the specified format.
4. A category certificate where reservation applies, as per the Apprentices Act.
5. Proof of date of birth, usually your Class 10 certificate.

## What DEAL is and what apprentices work on

The Defence Electronics Applications Laboratory, DEAL, is a DRDO laboratory based in Dehradun that works on communication and related electronics systems for defence. For an apprentice, this means the training is not abstract: you work in an environment focused on real defence electronics, communication systems, and supporting engineering and administrative functions, depending on your category and trade. A Graduate or Diploma apprentice in Electronics and Communication or Computer Science gains exposure to the kind of systems the lab develops, while ITI trade apprentices in fields like Electronics Mechanic, Fitter, or Stenographer support the technical and office functions. That environment, at a national defence research lab, is what makes a DRDO apprenticeship a stronger line on a resume than a generic training stint.

## The Apprentices Act framework behind DRDO drives

DRDO apprenticeships sit within a national framework that is worth understanding, because it explains how the portals and stipends work. The Apprentices Act of 1961 governs apprenticeship training in India, and two schemes run under it. The National Apprenticeship Training Scheme, NATS, covers graduate and diploma apprentices and is run by the Ministry of Education through regional boards. The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme, NAPS, covers trade and ITI apprentices. Under these schemes the government shares the stipend cost, which is why half your DEAL stipend comes from the lab and half from the government, credited by direct benefit transfer to your bank account. The NATS portal was modernised into a NATS 2.0 version to make registration and stipend payment smoother. Knowing this framework helps you see that a DRDO apprenticeship is part of a large, structured national programme, not a one-off arrangement, and that the same portals serve apprenticeships across thousands of establishments beyond DRDO.

## Reservation and the three apprentice categories

Reservation applies to apprenticeship seats as per the Apprentices Act and the applicable rules, so a share of the seats is set aside for reserved categories. The three apprentice categories serve different candidates. The Graduate Apprentice category is for engineering degree holders and offers the highest stipend, reflecting the qualification. The Diploma Apprentice category is for engineering diploma holders. The ITI or Trade Apprentice category, which carried the most seats at DEAL with 50 of the 77, is for candidates with a trade certificate from an Industrial Training Institute, across trades from Electronics Mechanic and Fitter to Library Assistant and Stenographer. You apply in the single category that matches your qualification, and a rule worth noting is that you cannot apply with a qualification higher than the one prescribed, so a degree holder cannot take a diploma or ITI seat. This keeps each category open to the candidates it is meant for.

## How an apprenticeship strengthens your career

Because the apprenticeship is not a job, its value lies in what it does for your career afterwards, and that value is real for the right candidate. A year of hands-on training at a DRDO lab gives you practical experience with the kind of equipment and processes that classroom study does not, a recognised training certificate under a national scheme, and a stipend that supports you through the year. Many candidates use the year to build their profile and prepare in parallel for a permanent recruitment exam, whether DRDO CEPTAM, the RAC Scientist route, a public-sector technician post, or a private-sector job. Employers value the discipline and exposure that an apprenticeship at a national research lab signals. The key is to enter with the right expectation: an apprenticeship is an investment in experience and preparation, and candidates who treat it that way get the most from it, while those who expect it to convert automatically into a DRDO job are disappointed.

## Why do a DRDO apprenticeship at all

Given that it is not a job, it is fair to ask why an apprenticeship is worth doing. The answer is experience and profile. A year of hands-on training at a DRDO laboratory, working alongside engineers and technicians on real defence electronics or research work, is valuable experience that strengthens your resume for later jobs, whether in DRDO through CEPTAM or the Scientist route, in other public-sector organisations, or in the private sector. The stipend, though modest, supports you during the year, and the training certificate is a recognised credential. For a fresh graduate, diploma holder, or ITI candidate deciding what to do in the year after qualifying, a DRDO apprenticeship is a productive use of that time, provided you go in understanding clearly that it is training, not employment.

## How the apprentice year typically runs

Understanding the shape of the year helps you decide whether the apprenticeship fits your plans. After selection on merit and document verification, you join the lab and are engaged as an apprentice under the Apprentices Act for a training period of one year. During that year you are attached to a section or function matching your discipline or trade, where you learn on the job under supervision, and you receive the monthly stipend by direct benefit transfer. There is no examination during the apprenticeship in the way a course has exams; the focus is practical training. At the end of the year, on satisfactory completion, you receive a certificate of apprenticeship training, which is a nationally recognised credential. The lab does not extend the engagement into a job, so the year is bounded and clear from the start. Candidates who plan for this, using the year to gain experience and prepare for their next step, get the most out of it.

## Apprenticeship versus a regular job, in plain terms

It helps to state the difference in plain terms, because so many candidates get it wrong. A regular job pays a salary, continues indefinitely, comes with service benefits and a career ladder, and is won through a competitive process like an exam. An apprenticeship pays a stipend, lasts a fixed one year, comes with a training certificate rather than service benefits, and is usually won on qualifying-exam merit without a separate test. Neither is better in the abstract; they serve different purposes. If you need income and security now, a job is what you want, and the route to a DRDO job is CEPTAM or the Scientist recruitment. If you are a fresh graduate, diploma holder, or ITI candidate who wants a year of quality experience and a credential while you prepare for those exams or other opportunities, the apprenticeship is a productive choice. Going in with this distinction clear is the single most important thing, because it sets the right expectation and prevents the disappointment that comes from treating training as though it were employment.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is the DRDO DEAL Apprentice 2026 still open?**
No. The DRDO DEAL Apprentice 2026-27 application window closed around 22 July 2026. If you missed it, register on the NATS or NAPS portal now so you are ready for the next lab drive, and watch the DRDO vacancies page, since apprentice drives run through the year.

**Does a DRDO apprenticeship lead to a permanent DRDO job?**
No. A DRDO apprenticeship is a one-year training programme with a stipend, and the notification states that no employment is offered afterwards. Permanent DRDO jobs come through separate recruitments like DRDO CEPTAM for technician posts and the RAC Scientist recruitment for scientists.

**What is the stipend for DRDO DEAL apprentices?**
The monthly stipend is Rs 12,300 for Graduate apprentices, Rs 10,900 for Diploma apprentices, and Rs 10,560 for ITI apprentices. Half is paid by DEAL and half by the government through direct benefit transfer, over a one-year training period.

**Is there a written exam for DRDO apprentice selection?**
No. Selection for a DRDO apprenticeship is usually merit-based on your qualifying-exam marks, followed by document verification. There is no written test, which is a key difference from permanent DRDO recruitment through CEPTAM or the Scientist route.

**What is the difference between a DRDO apprentice and DRDO CEPTAM?**
A DRDO apprentice is a one-year trainee paid a stipend, with no job at the end. DRDO CEPTAM is a permanent recruitment for technician and support posts, decided by a computer-based test, that leads to a regular government job with a pay scale.

**Do I apply on NATS or NAPS for a DRDO apprenticeship?**
Graduate and Diploma apprentices register on the NATS portal, the National Apprenticeship Training Scheme. ITI and trade apprentices register on the NAPS portal, the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. You then enter the lab's establishment code so your application reaches the right lab.

**Who is eligible for the DRDO DEAL apprentice 2026?**
Indian nationals who passed a regular qualifying course between 2022 and 2026, with no prior apprenticeship and not more than one year of post-qualification experience, and who hold the prescribed qualification for the Graduate, Diploma, or ITI category, not a higher one.

**Which other DRDO labs offer apprenticeships in 2026?**
Beyond DEAL, DRDO labs like ACEM in Nashik, INMAS in Delhi, and GTRE in Bengaluru have run apprentice drives in 2026. DRDO labs across the country recruit apprentices through the year, each on the NATS or NAPS portal, so keep your profile ready and check the portals regularly.

description: UPPSC PCS 2026 has 500 vacancies including SDM and DSP. Applications closed 3 August 2026. Prelims is on 6 December 2026. Full structure and strategy.
content:
The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission is recruiting 500 posts through the Combined State and Upper Subordinate Services Examination 2026, and the preliminary examination is on 6 December 2026. Applications ran until 3 August 2026 and the correction window closed on 10 August.

This is the exam that produces Uttar Pradesh's Sub Divisional Magistrates, Deputy Superintendents of Police and Block Development Officers. If you applied, you have roughly sixteen weeks to prelims.

## Where this recruitment stands

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Notification | 25 June 2026 |
| Vacancies | 500 |
| Application last date | 3 August 2026, closed |
| Correction window | Closed 10 August 2026 |
| Prelims | 6 December 2026 |
| Mains | Not announced |
| Stages | Prelims, Mains, Interview |
| Portal | uppsc.up.nic.in |

If you saw a figure of 200 posts or a January deadline on this page previously, both were wrong and have been corrected.

## The posts, and what the job actually is

Deputy Collector is the post most candidates are chasing. It places you in the provincial civil service on the track toward Sub Divisional Magistrate and, with promotion, eventually into the Indian Administrative Service through the state quota. The work is district administration: revenue, land, magistracy, elections, disaster response, and whatever else lands on a district officer's desk.

Deputy Superintendent of Police is the provincial police service equivalent, with promotion prospects into the Indian Police Service through the same state quota route.

Block Development Officer sits at the block level running rural development schemes, and it is the post where the largest share of candidates actually land. The work is closer to implementation than to magistracy, and it carries real authority over scheme delivery across a block.

Beyond those, the list covers Assistant Labour Commissioner, Naib Tehsildar, Sub Registrar, District Commandant Home Guard, Assistant Controller of Legal Measurement and a range of other Group A and Group B gazetted posts across departments.

The preference order you submitted matters more than most candidates treat it as mattering. Allocation follows merit rank applied strictly down your list, so ranking a post you do not want above one you do can hand you the former with no recourse.

## Prelims on 6 December

The preliminary examination has two papers, both objective, both two hours.

General Studies Paper I carries 150 questions for 200 marks and decides your cutoff. General Studies Paper II, the aptitude paper, carries 100 questions for 200 marks and is qualifying only at 33 per cent.

Negative marking is one third of a mark for each wrong answer in both papers.

That qualifying paper eliminates a steady number of candidates every cycle, and it does so quietly. Because its marks do not count, candidates from humanities backgrounds sometimes skip preparing it, then miss 33 per cent on comprehension and basic numeracy and are eliminated despite a strong General Studies score. Securing it is cheap. Failing it is total.

Prelims marks do not carry into your final ranking. The paper decides only who sits the Mains, and UPPSC calls forward a multiple of the vacancy count.

## The Mains, and the optional subject that no longer exists

UPPSC removed the optional subject from the PCS Mains and replaced it with additional General Studies papers. Candidates working from older guidance, or from material aimed at other state commissions, frequently prepare for a paper that is not in the exam.

The established structure now runs to 1500 marks:

| Paper | Marks |
|---|---|
| General Hindi | 150 |
| Essay | 150 |
| General Studies I | 200 |
| General Studies II | 200 |
| General Studies III | 200 |
| General Studies IV | 200 |
| General Studies V | 200 |
| General Studies VI | 200 |
| Written total | 1500 |
| Interview | 100 |
| Grand total | 1600 |

Six General Studies papers is a heavier General Studies load than most state commissions impose, and it changes what preparation should look like. There is no subject you can specialise in to carry your score. Breadth is the requirement, and a candidate strong in three areas and weak in three will find the weakness impossible to hide.

Confirm the paper weightings in the notification for this cycle rather than from a summary, because UPPSC has adjusted the structure between cycles and the change described above is recent enough that stale material is still circulating.

## General Hindi and the Essay are not free marks

General Hindi carries 150 marks and Essay carries 150, so together they are 300 of the 1500, which is one and a half General Studies papers.

Candidates fluent in Hindi routinely treat the language paper as guaranteed. It is not a conversation test. It assesses formal written Hindi, including precis writing, letter and official correspondence formats, grammar and vocabulary at a standard that everyday fluency does not cover. It is among the most predictable papers in the examination, which makes it among the cheapest marks available, and it is left on the table every year.

The Essay paper rewards structure far more than content. A well-organised essay on a familiar theme scores better than an unstructured one packed with facts, and the format is learnable in a way that General Studies breadth is not.

## Sixteen weeks to prelims

You have roughly sixteen weeks from mid August to 6 December. Here is how to use them.

Spend the first eight weeks on syllabus coverage with real weight on Uttar Pradesh specific material. UP history, geography, economy, polity, administrative structure, schemes and current affairs form a substantial part of the paper and they are the part with the weakest available resources. National General Studies material is abundant and everyone has it. The UP portion is where the field separates.

Run current affairs daily, split between national and state level. State current affairs deserve their own notes, because national compilations do not cover UP schemes, appointments, budget announcements or district-level developments, and those appear.

Start Mains answer writing now at low volume, perhaps two answers a week. This will feel premature with prelims sixteen weeks away and it is the highest-return thing you can do. Six General Studies papers plus an essay is a large writing load, and the skill takes months rather than weeks.

Move to full prelims mocks from around week nine, scored honestly with the one third penalty applied. Analyse for topics missed rather than for the score.

Secure the aptitude paper early rather than assuming it. A few timed practice sets will tell you whether you are comfortably above 33 per cent or need real work, and finding out in September is very different from finding out in December.

Keep the last two weeks for revision only.

## Eligibility

A bachelor's degree from a recognised university is the general requirement, with certain posts specifying additional qualifications in the notification.

The age band generally runs from 21 to 40 years against the cutoff date stated in the notification, which is a considerably wider window than the UPSC Civil Services Examination allows. Relaxation applies for reserved categories under Uttar Pradesh rules, and Deputy Superintendent of Police carries its own age and physical standards distinct from the administrative posts.

Physical standards apply to the police posts and not to the others. Candidates applying to DSP alongside administrative posts should check those requirements against themselves before counting on the preference.

Domicile is not a bar for most posts, but reservation benefits under Uttar Pradesh rules generally apply to candidates domiciled in the state. A candidate from outside UP can sit the exam and competes in the unreserved pool.

Confirm every one of these against the notification, since UPPSC varies eligibility by post and the version that binds you is the one printed for your post.

## Salary

Deputy Collector and Deputy Superintendent of Police enter at Pay Level 10 on the state pay matrix, comparable to other state civil service Group A entry grades, with gross monthly pay well above the entry basic once dearness allowance, house rent allowance and other allowances are added.

Block Development Officer and the Group B posts enter at lower levels on the same matrix.

Beyond pay, these posts carry pension provision, medical benefits, and in field postings official accommodation or a housing allowance. For most candidates the draw is the authority attached to district administration rather than the salary, which is lower than a comparable private sector role at the same age.

Exact pay levels by post are stated in the notification. Figures on coaching sites are frequently drawn from older pay structures.

## How UPPSC PCS compares with UPSC CSE

Many candidates prepare for both, and the overlap is real but narrower than it looks.

| | UPPSC PCS | UPSC CSE |
|---|---|---|
| Prelims papers | Two, one qualifying | Two, one qualifying |
| Optional subject | None, removed | One, two papers, 500 marks |
| Mains written total | 1500 | 1750 |
| Interview | 100 | 275 |
| Age band | Generally 21 to 40 | 21 to 32 |
| State-specific content | Substantial | Limited |
| Attempt limit | Governed by age | Six for general category |

Two differences matter most. The absence of an optional subject makes UPPSC preparation lighter in one respect and heavier in another, since six General Studies papers demand breadth that a UPSC candidate can partly offset with optional depth. And the age band running to 40 rather than 32 makes UPPSC a viable route for candidates who have exhausted or aged out of UPSC attempts, which is a genuine second chance rather than a consolation.

The shared General Studies foundation means preparing for one substantially prepares you for the other. What does not transfer is the Uttar Pradesh specific material, which earns nothing at UPSC, and the UPSC optional, which earns nothing here.

## Answer writing across six General Studies papers

The Mains asks you to write across six General Studies papers plus an essay plus a language paper, which is a larger volume of writing than most candidates have ever produced under examination conditions.

The constraint is rarely knowledge. It is producing structured, legible answers inside a word limit, repeatedly, across multiple days, without the quality collapsing in the later papers. Candidates who have practised writing at volume hold their standard. Candidates who have read widely and written little do not.

Three habits separate the strong papers. Answering the directive actually asked rather than writing everything known about the topic. Structuring visibly, with an introduction, a body in identifiable parts and a conclusion that returns to the question. And finishing every answer, because an incomplete answer scores as incomplete regardless of how strong its opening was.

Time per question is the binding constraint, and it has to be rehearsed rather than calculated. Work out your realistic pace in practice, then build the paper plan around it.

## A note on the state quota route into the IAS

One thing draws candidates to Deputy Collector above every other consideration, and it is worth being accurate about.

A fixed share of Indian Administrative Service posts is filled by promotion from state civil services rather than by direct recruitment through the UPSC Civil Services Examination. A Deputy Collector who enters through UPPSC is on that track, and the same applies to Deputy Superintendent of Police and the Indian Police Service.

What that route is not is fast. Promotion depends on years of service, on vacancies arising in the state cadre, on your position in the state seniority list, and on clearing the selection process the Union Public Service Commission runs for these promotions. Officers typically reach it well into their careers rather than within a few years, and not every eligible officer is promoted.

It is a genuine route and it should be weighed as one. A candidate who treats UPPSC purely as a slower path to the same destination as UPSC will be disappointed by the timeline. A candidate who wants to work in Uttar Pradesh's district administration, and regards eventual promotion as a possibility rather than a plan, is making a sounder decision.

The provincial civil service is a substantial career in its own right. Sub Divisional Magistrates exercise real authority over revenue, magistracy and administration across a subdivision from relatively early in their service, which is more responsibility than most careers offer at that stage.

## Mistakes that cost candidates this exam

Preparing an optional subject. UPPSC removed it. Candidates working from old material or from other states' patterns still do this.

Treating the aptitude paper as automatic. It is qualifying at 33 per cent and it eliminates people quietly every cycle.

Assuming fluency covers General Hindi. It tests formal written Hindi, precis and official correspondence, and it is worth 150 marks.

Reading only national current affairs. The UP specific portion is where the exam is decided, and national compilations do not cover it.

Postponing answer writing until after the prelims result. Six General Studies papers and an essay is a large writing load to build in ten weeks.

Ranking only the senior posts in the preference order. Block Development Officer accounts for a large share of allocations, and a list that ignores it removes you from much of the cycle.

## Frequently asked questions

**How many vacancies are there in UPPSC PCS 2026?**

500 posts, covering Deputy Collector, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Block Development Officer, Assistant Labour Commissioner, Naib Tehsildar, Sub Registrar and other Group A and Group B gazetted positions. UPPSC publishes the post-wise split in the notification.

**Can I still apply for UPPSC PCS 2026?**

No. The notification was released on 25 June 2026, applications closed on 3 August 2026 and the correction window closed on 10 August 2026. There is no late route. The preliminary examination is on 6 December 2026.

**When is the UPPSC PCS 2026 prelims exam?**

6 December 2026. The Mains date had not been announced as of 15 August 2026. Admit cards are released on uppsc.up.nic.in ahead of the exam.

**Is there an optional subject in the UPPSC PCS Mains?**

No. UPPSC removed the optional subject and replaced it with additional General Studies papers. The Mains now runs General Hindi (150), Essay (150) and six General Studies papers of 200 marks each, totalling 1500. Candidates working from older material or from other state patterns still prepare an optional that is not in the exam.

**Do prelims marks count towards the final merit list?**

No. The preliminary examination decides only who sits the Mains. Final merit comes from the Mains written total of 1500 and the interview worth 100, giving 1600.

**What is the UPPSC PCS prelims exam pattern?**

Two objective papers of two hours each. General Studies Paper I has 150 questions for 200 marks and decides the cutoff. General Studies Paper II has 100 questions for 200 marks and is qualifying only at 33 per cent. Negative marking is one third of a mark per wrong answer in both.

**What is the age limit for UPPSC PCS?**

Generally 21 to 40 years against the notification cutoff date, a wider window than the UPSC Civil Services Examination allows, with relaxation for reserved categories under Uttar Pradesh rules. Deputy Superintendent of Police carries its own age and physical standards distinct from the administrative posts.

**Can candidates from outside Uttar Pradesh apply?**

Yes. Domicile is not a bar for most posts, and a candidate from outside UP competes in the unreserved pool. Reservation benefits under Uttar Pradesh rules generally apply to candidates domiciled in the state.

**How much is General Hindi worth?**

150 marks, with the Essay carrying another 150, so together they are 300 of the 1500 written total. General Hindi tests formal written Hindi including precis, letter and official correspondence formats and grammar, at a standard everyday fluency does not cover, which is why fluent speakers lose marks in it.

**What should I focus on in the months before prelims?**

Uttar Pradesh specific material, which is where the field separates and where resources are weakest. Run state-level current affairs separately from national. Secure the qualifying aptitude paper early rather than assuming it. And start Mains answer writing now at low volume, because six General Studies papers plus an essay is a writing load that takes months to build.

**Is UPPSC PCS easier than UPSC CSE?**

The competition ratio is lower and the age band is wider, running generally to 40 rather than 32, which makes UPPSC a viable route for candidates who have exhausted UPSC attempts or aged out. The Mains is not obviously easier: six General Studies papers demand breadth with no optional subject to offset a weak area, and the Uttar Pradesh specific content is material a UPSC candidate has not prepared.

**Does UPPSC publish previous year cutoffs?**

UPPSC publishes cutoffs after a cycle concludes, varying by category and by post. They move with paper difficulty, applicant volume and the vacancy count, so the 500 vacancies in this cycle are the relevant denominator rather than an earlier year's figure. Treat historical cutoffs as orientation for mock scores, not as targets.

**Can I write the UPPSC Mains in English?**

The Mains may be written in Hindi or English for the General Studies papers and the Essay. General Hindi is a separate compulsory language paper regardless of the medium you choose for the rest. Pick the medium you write faster and more precisely in, then practise consistently in it rather than switching.

**What is the difference between Deputy Collector and BDO?**

Deputy Collector places you in the provincial civil service on the Sub Divisional Magistrate track, doing revenue, magistracy, land and election work, with eventual promotion prospects into the IAS through the state quota. Block Development Officer works at block level running rural development schemes, closer to implementation than magistracy. BDO accounts for a larger share of actual allocations, which is why a preference list ignoring it removes you from much of the cycle.

**How long is the full UPPSC PCS process?**

From the 25 June 2026 notification through prelims on 6 December, a Mains some months later, an interview and final results, the cycle runs well over a year. Candidates should plan on that timeline and continue applying to other recruitments in the interim rather than pausing to wait on a result.

## Official sources

- Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission: https://uppsc.up.nic.in
- The PCS 2026 notification PDF, which is the authority on the post-wise vacancy table, age limits by post, physical standards for police posts and paper weightings

Where a figure on this page conflicts with the notification, the notification is correct. UPPSC issues corrigenda mid-cycle.

content:
## India Post GDS 2026: there is no written exam

India Post Gramin Dak Sevak recruitment 2026 covers 28,636 posts, and it is selected entirely without an examination. Merit is prepared from your Class 10 marks and nothing else.

That single fact separates this from every other recruitment on this site, and it is the thing candidates most often get wrong. There is no GDS exam date, no admit card, no syllabus and no question paper. Searching for a GDS exam pattern returns nothing useful because none exists. What exists is a merit list built from the marks you already earned years ago.

Applications for this cycle ran from 31 January to 14 February 2026 on indiapostgdsonline.gov.in. Merit lists have been released in sequence since then, with the fourth list published on 8 June 2026 and a fifth expected.

## How selection actually works

The process has exactly two stages.

1. A merit list prepared from Class 10 marks, computed to four decimal places.
2. Document verification for candidates on the list.

That is the whole process. No interview, no physical test, no typing test, no written paper.

The four decimal places matter more than they look. India Post converts your Class 10 result to a percentage carried to four places, which means 78.4615 and 78.4600 are different scores and rank differently. Candidates with grades rather than marks have them converted per the prescribed conversion table. Because the field is enormous and the scoring is this granular, selection frequently turns on the third or fourth decimal.

One consequence worth stating plainly: nothing you do now changes your Class 10 marks. If you have already applied, the merit outcome is fixed by a result you received years ago. What you can control is applying to every cycle you are eligible for, applying in the right division, and having documents ready so you clear verification.

## The tie-breaker rules

When two candidates have identical marks to four decimal places, India Post applies a defined tie-breaking order, and it is unusual enough to be worth setting out in full.

First, the older candidate is preferred. Age works in your favour here, which is the opposite of most recruitments.

If a tie still remains after age, candidates are ordered by this sequence:

1. ST female
2. SC female
3. OBC female
4. EWS female
5. UR female
6. ST male
7. SC male
8. OBC male
9. EWS male
10. UR male

Every female category is placed ahead of every male category in the tie-break, which is a deliberate feature of the rules rather than an accident of drafting.

## Why there are multiple merit lists

Candidates routinely assume that missing the first merit list means rejection. It does not.

India Post publishes successive lists because selected candidates drop out. Some do not report for document verification, some fail it, some decline the posting because of its location, and some have already taken another job. Every vacancy created that way is filled from the next candidates in merit order, which produces a second list, then a third, then a fourth.

In this cycle the second list came on 11 April 2026 and the fourth on 8 June 2026, with a fifth expected. So a candidate who was not on the first list may still be selected months later.

The practical advice: keep checking indiapostgdsonline.gov.in through the cycle rather than treating the first list as final, and keep your documents ready throughout, since the window between appearing on a list and reporting for verification is short.

## The three posts

The 28,636 vacancies cover three roles that differ in responsibility and pay.

| Post | What the role involves |
|---|---|
| Branch Postmaster (BPM) | Runs a branch post office: accounts, cash handling, mail, savings schemes and overall responsibility for the branch |
| Assistant Branch Postmaster (ABPM) | Assists the BPM with counter work, delivery, and post office operations |
| Dak Sevak | Mail handling, delivery and operational support, generally attached to departmental post offices |

Branch Postmaster carries the highest pay of the three and the most responsibility, including cash and accounts. It is the post to prefer if your marks give you the choice.

## Pay, and an honest note about service conditions

Gramin Dak Sevaks are paid under Time Related Continuity Allowance, referred to as TRCA, rather than on a regular central government pay matrix level.

| Post | TRCA range |
|---|---|
| Branch Postmaster (BPM) | Rs 12,000 to Rs 29,380 per month |
| Assistant Branch Postmaster and Dak Sevak | Rs 10,000 to Rs 24,470 per month |

Dearness allowance applies on top of TRCA, and GDS are entitled to a defined set of benefits including a limited leave entitlement, a Service Discharge Benefit Scheme, group insurance, and ex gratia gratuity on discharge.

The honest framing, which most pages skip: a Gramin Dak Sevak is not a regular central government employee in the way an SSC or Railways recruit is. GDS engagement carries its own service conditions, a different pay mechanism, and a different benefits structure. The work is often part-time in duration terms at a branch office, and GDS are permitted other employment or occupation alongside, which is why the role suits candidates who want a stable government-linked income in their own village while continuing farming or a small business.

That is not a criticism of the post. For a Class 10 pass candidate in a rural area, a stable posting in or near their own village with a defined income and discharge benefits is a genuinely good outcome. But it should be entered with an accurate picture rather than an assumption that it is equivalent to a Level 3 central government job.

## What the work actually involves

Because there is no examination to research, candidates often reach selection knowing very little about the job itself. It is worth setting out.

A branch post office is the smallest unit of the postal network, typically serving a village or a cluster of villages, and often staffed by just a Branch Postmaster and an Assistant. It is not a large departmental post office with counters and queues.

The work covers booking and delivering mail and parcels, running the post office savings bank, handling recurring deposits, time deposits, the Sukanya Samriddhi and Public Provident Fund accounts, processing money orders, paying out social security pensions and MGNREGA wages where the post office is the disbursing agency, India Post Payments Bank transactions, Aadhaar enrolment and update services at enabled offices, and selling postal life insurance.

That range surprises people. A Branch Postmaster in a village handles cash, maintains accounts, is accountable for balances, and is frequently the only formal financial access point for the households around them. The savings and pension disbursement side of the job is larger in practice than the mail side.

Delivery duties involve covering the village and surrounding habitations, which is why a cycling requirement appears in the eligibility conditions. Branch offices also keep their own working hours, which are shorter than a departmental post office and set according to the workload of the location, and this is the basis on which GDS are permitted to hold other occupations alongside the engagement.

The responsibility that comes with cash handling is real. A Branch Postmaster is accountable for the balances they hold, and the post requires furnishing security as specified in the rules. Candidates weighing BPM against the assistant posts should factor that in alongside the higher pay: the extra money comes with accountability for cash and accounts that the ABPM and Dak Sevak roles do not carry.

## Eligibility

On age, the band is 18 to 40 years, with relaxation for reserved categories as per the rules. The age is reckoned as on the last date of application.

That upper limit of 40 is exceptionally wide. Compare it with SSC GD Constable at 18 to 23, or most SSC and Railway recruitments in the 18 to 30 range. For a candidate in their thirties who has aged out of nearly every other central recruitment, India Post GDS is often the only central government route still open. Combined with a tie-break that favours the older candidate, this recruitment is unusually friendly to late applicants.

On education, Class 10 pass with Mathematics and English as subjects of study is required, from a recognised board.

On additional requirements, candidates need knowledge of the local language of the circle they apply to, having studied it at least up to Class 10. Basic computer knowledge and a cycling ability requirement also apply as specified in the notification, along with an adequate means of livelihood condition for certain posts.

## How to apply in the next cycle

Applications are filed only on indiapostgdsonline.gov.in.

1. Register on the portal with your Class 10 certificate details, a working mobile number and an email address.
2. Pay the application fee online. It is a modest amount, with exemptions for female, SC, ST and PwD candidates.
3. Fill the application with your Class 10 marks exactly as printed on your certificate, since this is the entire basis of selection and an error here is fatal.
4. Choose your divisions and post preferences carefully. Vacancies are notified circle-wise and division-wise, and cutoffs vary sharply between divisions.
5. Upload the required documents and submit.
6. Watch for the merit lists and, if listed, report for document verification within the stated window.

The single highest-value decision in that list is the choice of division. Because merit is computed within each division against its own vacancies, the same Class 10 percentage can be comfortably selected in one division and short in another. Candidates who research division-wise cutoffs from previous cycles before choosing improve their odds without changing a single mark.

## How division choice changes your odds

This deserves its own section, because it is the only real decision in an otherwise fixed process.

India Post notifies vacancies circle-wise and then division-wise within each circle. Merit is computed separately for each division against the vacancies notified there. Two candidates with identical Class 10 percentages applying to different divisions can get completely different outcomes.

The reason is supply and demand at a very local level. A division covering a densely populated area with many Class 10 pass applicants and few vacancies produces a high cutoff. A division in a sparsely populated or remote area with comparable vacancies and far fewer applicants produces a much lower one. Differences of several percentage points between divisions in the same circle are ordinary.

What this means practically: before choosing, look up the division-wise cutoffs published in previous cycles, which are available on the portal and widely reproduced. Compare them against your own percentage. If your marks sit comfortably above a division's historical cutoff, that is a strong choice. If they sit two points below, applying there is close to wasted.

The constraint is that you must have studied the local language of the circle up to Class 10, which limits how far afield you can look. But within the circles where you meet that condition, division choice is entirely yours and it is where the odds are won or lost.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 mark sheet and certificate from a recognised board, showing Mathematics and English.
2. Proof of date of birth.
3. Category certificate in the prescribed format for SC, ST, OBC and EWS claims.
4. Certificate of study of the local language up to at least Class 10.
5. Computer knowledge certificate as specified in the notification.
6. PwD certificate where applicable.
7. Photograph, signature and a photo identity document matching the application.

Document verification is where selections are lost in this recruitment, precisely because there is no examination to fail. A discrepancy between the marks entered in the application and the certificate, a category certificate in the wrong format, or a missing local language certificate will end an otherwise successful candidature.

## What to do if you were not selected

Because merit is fixed by your Class 10 marks, the strategy for the next cycle is different from an exam-based recruitment.

Apply again in the next cycle. India Post runs GDS recruitment periodically, and vacancy positions and division-wise cutoffs change between cycles, so the same marks that fell short this time can succeed in the next one without anything about your certificate changing.

Choose divisions more carefully. This is the one genuine lever available, and most candidates never use it.

Keep an eye on the later merit lists in the current cycle rather than assuming the first list is final.

And consider parallel routes that do use examinations, where preparation can change your outcome rather than your certificate deciding it. [RRB Group D](/sarkari-naukri/rrb-group-d-2026) and [SSC GD Constable](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-gd-constable-2026) both take Class 10 candidates, and unlike GDS, effort in the coming months directly affects your result.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is there an exam for India Post GDS 2026?**
No. There is no written examination, no admit card, no syllabus and no interview. Selection is made purely from a merit list prepared on Class 10 marks, computed to four decimal places, followed by document verification. Searching for a GDS exam date or exam pattern returns nothing useful because no examination exists in this recruitment.

**How is the India Post GDS merit list prepared?**
It is prepared from Class 10 marks alone, converted to a percentage carried to four decimal places, with grades converted per the prescribed conversion table. Because the scoring is that granular and the applicant pool is very large, selection often turns on the third or fourth decimal place. Merit is computed within each division against that division's vacancies.

**What is the tie-breaker rule in India Post GDS?**
When marks are identical to four decimal places, the older candidate is preferred first. If a tie remains, candidates are ordered ST female, SC female, OBC female, EWS female, UR female, then ST male, SC male, OBC male, EWS male, UR male. Every female category ranks ahead of every male category in the tie-break, and age works in your favour, which is unusual among government recruitments.

**How many vacancies are in India Post GDS 2026?**
There are 28,636 vacancies across the posts of Gramin Dak Sevak, Branch Postmaster and Assistant Branch Postmaster, distributed circle-wise and division-wise across the country. Applications ran from 31 January to 14 February 2026 on indiapostgdsonline.gov.in.

**Why does India Post release multiple GDS merit lists?**
Because selected candidates drop out. Some do not report for document verification, some fail it, some decline the posting because of its location, and some have taken other jobs. Each vacancy created that way is filled from the next candidates in merit order, producing successive lists. In this cycle the second list came on 11 April 2026 and the fourth on 8 June 2026, with a fifth expected, so missing the first list is not rejection.

**What is the salary of a Gramin Dak Sevak?**
GDS are paid under Time Related Continuity Allowance rather than a regular pay matrix level. Branch Postmasters receive Rs 12,000 to Rs 29,380 a month and Assistant Branch Postmasters and Dak Sevaks receive Rs 10,000 to Rs 24,470, with dearness allowance on top. Benefits include limited leave, the Service Discharge Benefit Scheme, group insurance and ex gratia gratuity on discharge.

**What is the age limit for India Post GDS?**
18 to 40 years as on the last date of application, with relaxation for reserved categories. That upper limit is exceptionally wide compared with most central recruitments, such as SSC GD Constable at 18 to 23. For candidates in their thirties who have aged out of other central routes, GDS is often the only one still open, and the tie-break rule favouring older candidates adds to that.

**What qualification is needed for India Post GDS?**
Class 10 pass from a recognised board with Mathematics and English as subjects of study. Candidates also need to have studied the local language of the circle up to at least Class 10, along with basic computer knowledge and a cycling ability requirement as specified in the notification.

**Are Gramin Dak Sevaks regular government employees?**
Not in the same sense as an SSC or Railways recruit. GDS are engaged under their own service conditions and paid through Time Related Continuity Allowance rather than a central pay matrix level, with a distinct benefits structure. The role is often part-time in duration at a branch office and GDS are permitted other employment or occupation alongside, which suits candidates wanting a stable government-linked income in their own village while continuing farming or a small business.

**What is the difference between BPM, ABPM and Dak Sevak?**
The Branch Postmaster runs a branch post office and is responsible for accounts, cash handling, mail and savings schemes, carrying the highest pay of the three. The Assistant Branch Postmaster assists with counter work, delivery and operations. Dak Sevaks handle mail, delivery and operational support, generally attached to departmental post offices. BPM is the post to prefer if your marks give you the choice.

**Why do candidates get rejected in India Post GDS?**
Almost entirely at document verification, since there is no examination to fail. The common causes are a mismatch between the marks entered in the application and those on the Class 10 certificate, a category certificate in the wrong format, a missing local language certificate, or an absent computer knowledge certificate. Entering your marks with complete accuracy and assembling documents in advance is what protects the candidature.

**How can I improve my chances in India Post GDS?**
Your Class 10 marks are fixed, so the one real lever is your choice of division. Merit is computed within each division against its own vacancies, and cutoffs vary sharply, so the same percentage can be comfortably selected in one division and short in another. Researching division-wise cutoffs from previous cycles before choosing improves your odds without changing a single mark. Beyond that, apply in every cycle you are eligible for and watch the later merit lists.
