content:
## MPPSC Assistant Professor 2026: where this recruitment stands

MPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 is a recruitment of 949 posts in Madhya Pradesh government colleges and state universities, conducted by the Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission. Applications have closed, and the exam stage is under way: admit cards for the next batch of subjects were released on 29 July 2026 on mppsc.mp.gov.in, with those exams on 30 August 2026.

The thing that confuses almost everyone searching for this recruitment is that the dates appear to contradict each other. One page says the exam was on 12 July 2026, another says 30 August 2026, a third gives an application deadline that has already passed. All of them can be right at once.

MPPSC is not running this as one exam. It is running it as a series of subject groups, each with its own application window, its own admit card release, and its own exam date. Your dates depend entirely on which subject you applied for. Checking a date meant for a different subject group is the single most common mistake candidates make here.

## Exam schedule by subject group

These are the batches confirmed so far. Check the one that matches your subject, and confirm on mppsc.mp.gov.in, since MPPSC has issued corrigenda revising dates more than once in this recruitment.

| Subject group | Admit card | Exam date |
|---|---|---|
| Sanskrit, Geography, Psychology, Law, Geology, Yogic Science | 2 July 2026 | 12 July 2026, at Indore |
| History, Physics, Chemistry, Botany, Mathematics and the subjects grouped with them | 29 July 2026 | 30 August 2026 |

A corrigendum dated 25 June 2026 revised the schedule for History, Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Mathematics, which is why older pages carry different dates for those subjects. If your subject is not listed above, MPPSC publishes the schedule group by group, so watch the commission's notice board rather than relying on aggregator pages.

## Application window, and the late fee structure

Applications are closed. The revised last date to apply online was 9 June 2026, and MPPSC then ran an unusual two-tier late window: applications with a late fee of Rs 3,000 were accepted from 10 to 16 June 2026, and applications with an ultra-late fee of Rs 25,000 were accepted on 17 June 2026.

That Rs 25,000 figure is not a misprint, and it is worth knowing about for the next cycle. MPPSC uses steep late fees rather than simply closing the window, which means a candidate who misses the ordinary deadline still has a route in, at a price that for most people is several months of the salary they are applying for. Apply inside the ordinary window.

The ordinary application fee was Rs 540 for General candidates and candidates from outside Madhya Pradesh, and Rs 290 for SC, ST, OBC and EWS candidates who are residents of Madhya Pradesh.

## Vacancy breakdown

The 949 posts span Arts, Commerce, Social Sciences and Science subjects. The largest allocations reported are as follows.

| Subject | Posts |
|---|---|
| Chemistry | 160 |
| Physics | 145 |
| Commerce | 94 |
| Economics | 84 |
| Geography | 74 |

The remaining posts are distributed across the other subjects, including History, Mathematics, Botany, Zoology, Sanskrit, Psychology, Law, Geology and Yogic Science. Category reservation applies within each subject as per Madhya Pradesh government rules, covering General, SC, ST, OBC and EWS.

Two things follow from that table. Chemistry and Physics together account for over 300 of the 949 posts, so science candidates face a much wider opening than those in smaller subjects. And because reservation is applied within each subject, your real competition is the pool in your subject and category, not the headline figure of 949.

## Eligibility

On education, you need a Master's degree in the relevant subject with at least 55 per cent marks, or an equivalent grade, from a recognised university. Candidates in reserved categories get the usual relaxation to 50 per cent as per UGC norms.

On the eligibility test, you need to have qualified the National Eligibility Test conducted by UGC, or CSIR NET, or the State Level Eligibility Test or State Eligibility Test, including the Madhya Pradesh SLET. Candidates holding a PhD awarded in accordance with the UGC regulations are exempt from the NET requirement.

That exemption is worth reading carefully, because it is conditional rather than automatic. The PhD must have been awarded in compliance with the UGC Regulations on minimum standards and procedure for the award of the degree, which set requirements on coursework, evaluation and viva. A PhD that does not meet those conditions does not carry the exemption, and this is checked at document verification rather than at the application stage.

On age, the band is 21 to 40 years, with relaxation for reserved categories and other specified groups as per Madhya Pradesh rules. The reckoning date is set in the advertisement.

## Exam pattern

The exam is offline and OMR based, with two papers on the same day in separate sessions.

| Paper | Content | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | General Studies | 10:00 am to 11:00 am | 1 hour |
| Paper 2 | Subject specific | 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm | 3 hours |

The structure tells you where the weight sits. Paper 2 runs three times as long as Paper 1, and it is the paper that tests your actual discipline at postgraduate level. Paper 1 is a general studies qualifying-style paper covering the areas common to Madhya Pradesh state exams.

Candidates who come from a research background often make the opposite mistake to the one you would expect: they prepare Paper 2 thoroughly, which they would pass anyway, and neglect Paper 1, which covers material they have not touched since their own competitive exam years.

## Paper 1: what General Studies covers

Paper 1 draws on the standard Madhya Pradesh state exam general studies base: Indian history with emphasis on the freedom movement, Indian and Madhya Pradesh geography, Indian polity and the Constitution, the Indian and state economy, general science and technology, current affairs at national and state level, and Madhya Pradesh specific general knowledge covering the state's districts, rivers, tribes, festivals, historical sites and current schemes.

Higher education policy topics appear as well, including the National Education Policy, UGC regulations, and the structure of higher education administration in the state, which are directly relevant to the post being filled.

For a candidate with a research background and no recent state-exam preparation, this paper needs deliberate work over a few weeks. It is a single hour of the day, but it is the part of the exam where the marginal marks are easiest to gain.

## Paper 2: the subject paper

Paper 2 tests your subject at the level expected of someone about to teach it in an undergraduate and postgraduate setting. In practice the syllabus tracks the UGC NET syllabus for the subject fairly closely, extended in places to reflect the Madhya Pradesh university curriculum.

The most efficient preparation is to work from your own postgraduate syllabus and the UGC NET syllabus for the subject together, since between them they cover almost everything MPPSC asks. Past MPPSC papers for your subject, where available, tell you which areas the commission favours, and those preferences tend to persist across cycles.

## Salary and what the post actually pays

The post is placed at Academic Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission structure for teachers, with a pay range of Rs 57,700 to Rs 1,82,400.

Entry pay is Rs 57,700 a month as basic. Dearness allowance applies at the rate for the state, house rent allowance depends on the classification of the posting city, and transport allowance applies. Gross monthly pay at entry works out substantially above the basic figure, and the position carries the leave, medical and pension entitlements of a Madhya Pradesh government post.

Compared with the constable and clerical recruitments that dominate state hiring, this is a materially different pay bracket: entry basic here is roughly two and a half times that of a state police constable, which reflects the postgraduate and NET or PhD requirement.

## Career progression

Assistant Professor is the entry rung of the academic ladder, and progression runs through the Career Advancement Scheme rather than through a promotion exam.

| Position | Academic level |
|---|---|
| Assistant Professor (entry) | Level 10 |
| Assistant Professor (senior scale) | Level 11 |
| Assistant Professor (selection grade) | Level 12 |
| Associate Professor | Level 13A |
| Professor | Level 14 |

Movement up this ladder depends on years of service, academic performance including publications and research, refresher and orientation courses, and the screening or selection committee process laid down in the UGC regulations. Unlike a departmental promotion in an administrative service, progression here is substantially in your own hands: publication record and qualifications drive it.

## After the written exam: interview and verification

Clearing the written exam does not complete the process. Shortlisted candidates go to an interview, and then to document verification.

The interview for an academic post is not a general personality test in the way a police or administrative interview is. Expect questions on your subject, your postgraduate and doctoral work, your publications if you have any, your teaching approach, and your reasons for wanting a college post in Madhya Pradesh. Candidates who submitted a research background should be ready to defend it in detail, since a panel of subject experts will read what you claimed.

Document verification is where conditional eligibility gets tested properly. The two things that fail candidates here are a Master's percentage that falls below the 55 per cent bar once the university's own conversion formula is applied rather than the candidate's estimate, and a PhD claimed for NET exemption that does not meet the UGC regulation conditions. Both are worth checking against your actual certificates now rather than assuming.

## How this compares with other academic routes

Candidates with a NET or a PhD usually have several options open at once, and they are not equivalent.

| Route | Recruiting body | Pay entry | Selection |
|---|---|---|---|
| MPPSC Assistant Professor | Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission | Academic Level 10 | Written exam, interview, document verification |
| Central university Assistant Professor | Individual university | Academic Level 10 | Application screening and interview, usually no written exam |
| Other state PSC Assistant Professor | State commissions | Academic Level 10 | Varies, many use written plus interview |
| Guest or contract faculty | College or university directly | Fixed monthly rate, much lower | Interview, often local |

The pay is the same across the permanent routes, so the real difference is the selection mechanism. Central universities generally shortlist on academic record and interview, which favours candidates with strong publications. State commissions like MPPSC use a written exam, which favours candidates who prepare systematically and gives a chance to those whose research record is thinner. A candidate with a modest publication list and good exam discipline is often better placed in the MPPSC route than in a central university screening.

Guest faculty work is a different proposition entirely, paid at a fixed monthly rate well below the permanent scale and without the tenure, and it is best treated as a stopgap while pursuing the permanent routes rather than as a career.

## What to carry on exam day

Take the printed admit card and a valid original photo identity document, being an Aadhaar card, voter ID, PAN card or driving licence, along with a black or blue pen. The exam is OMR based, so the pen matters.

Mobile phones, calculators, bags, books, jewellery and electronic devices are not allowed at the centre. Reach the centre well before the reporting time printed on your admit card, and note that the two papers run in separate sessions with a gap in between, so plan for a full day rather than a single sitting.

The gap between the 11:00 am finish of Paper 1 and the 1:00 pm start of Paper 2 is long enough to matter. Centres do not always provide a waiting area, and you cannot carry a bag in, so arrange food and water for the break in advance and avoid travelling back and forth. Candidates who spend that gap anxiously reviewing Paper 1 arrive at the three-hour subject paper already tired, which is the paper that carries the weight.

## Preparing between now and your exam date

If your exam is on 30 August 2026, you have about a month, and the allocation of that month should not be even.

Give the first stretch to Paper 1, since it is the paper you are least likely to have prepared and the one where a few weeks of focused study moves your score most. Work through Madhya Pradesh general knowledge and current affairs of the last year, then Indian polity and economy, then general science.

Keep Paper 2 revision running alongside, working from your postgraduate syllabus and the UGC NET syllabus for your subject, and prioritise the areas that past MPPSC papers in your subject have favoured.

In the final week, shift to full-length practice under exam timing, since the three-hour subject paper is a stamina exercise as much as a knowledge one, and few candidates have written for three hours at a stretch since their own university exams.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is the MPPSC Assistant Professor 2026 application still open?**
No. Applications closed with a revised last date of 9 June 2026. MPPSC then accepted applications with a late fee of Rs 3,000 from 10 to 16 June 2026, and with an ultra-late fee of Rs 25,000 on 17 June 2026. The recruitment is now at the examination stage.

**When is the MPPSC Assistant Professor exam 2026?**
The exam runs in staggered subject groups rather than on a single date. Sanskrit, Geography, Psychology, Law, Geology and Yogic Science were examined on 12 July 2026 at Indore. History, Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Mathematics and the subjects grouped with them are on 30 August 2026, with admit cards released on 29 July 2026. Check mppsc.mp.gov.in for your specific subject.

**When was the MPPSC Assistant Professor admit card 2026 released?**
Admit cards are released group by group, a few weeks before each subject group's exam. The card for the 12 July 2026 batch came out on 2 July 2026, and the card for the 30 August 2026 batch was released on 29 July 2026. Download it from mppsc.mp.gov.in or mponline.gov.in.

**How many vacancies are in MPPSC Assistant Professor 2026?**
There are 949 posts across Arts, Commerce, Social Sciences and Science subjects. The largest reported allocations are Chemistry 160, Physics 145, Commerce 94, Economics 84 and Geography 74, with the rest spread across the other subjects. Reservation is applied within each subject, so your competition is the pool in your subject and category.

**What is the eligibility for MPPSC Assistant Professor?**
A Master's degree in the relevant subject with at least 55 per cent marks, relaxed to 50 per cent for reserved categories as per UGC norms, plus UGC NET, CSIR NET, SET or SLET including the Madhya Pradesh SLET. Candidates holding a PhD awarded in accordance with the UGC regulations are exempt from the NET requirement. The age band is 21 to 40 years with relaxation as per Madhya Pradesh rules.

**Is NET compulsory if I have a PhD?**
No, a PhD awarded in accordance with the UGC regulations exempts you from the NET requirement. The exemption is conditional rather than automatic: the degree must comply with the UGC Regulations on minimum standards and procedure for the award of a PhD, covering coursework, evaluation and viva. Compliance is checked at document verification, not at the application stage.

**What is the exam pattern for MPPSC Assistant Professor?**
Two offline OMR based papers on the same day. Paper 1 is General Studies from 10:00 am to 11:00 am for one hour. Paper 2 is the subject specific paper from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm for three hours. Selection is based on the written examination followed by interview and document verification.

**What is the salary of an MPPSC Assistant Professor?**
The post is at Academic Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission structure for teachers, with a range of Rs 57,700 to Rs 1,82,400. Entry basic pay is Rs 57,700 a month, with dearness allowance, house rent allowance by city class and transport allowance on top, along with the leave, medical and pension entitlements of a Madhya Pradesh government post.

**What is the syllabus for MPPSC Assistant Professor Paper 1?**
Paper 1 covers Indian history with emphasis on the freedom movement, Indian and Madhya Pradesh geography, polity and the Constitution, the Indian and state economy, general science and technology, current affairs, and Madhya Pradesh general knowledge. Higher education topics such as the National Education Policy and UGC regulations also appear, since they are relevant to the post.

**What should I carry to the MPPSC Assistant Professor exam?**
Carry the printed admit card, a valid original photo identity document such as an Aadhaar card, voter ID, PAN card or driving licence, and a black or blue pen, since the exam is OMR based. Mobile phones, calculators, bags, books, jewellery and electronic devices are not permitted at the centre.

**Why do different websites show different MPPSC Assistant Professor exam dates?**
Because MPPSC runs this recruitment in subject groups, each with its own application window, admit card release and exam date, and it has issued corrigenda revising some of them, including one dated 25 June 2026 covering History, Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Mathematics. Pages describing a different subject group, or written before a corrigendum, carry dates that are correct for that group but not for yours.

**What is the career progression after MPPSC Assistant Professor?**
Progression runs through the Career Advancement Scheme rather than a promotion exam: Assistant Professor at Academic Level 10, then senior scale at Level 11, selection grade at Level 12, Associate Professor at Level 13A, and Professor at Level 14. Movement depends on years of service, publications and research output, orientation and refresher courses, and the selection committee process under the UGC regulations.

content:
## CISF ASI Paramedical 2026: where this cycle stands

CISF ASI Paramedical 2026 recruitment is for 24 Assistant Sub-Inspector posts in the Central Industrial Security Force medical cadre, and the application window has closed. Applications ran from 8 June 2026 to 7 July 2026 on cisfrectt.cisf.gov.in, and as of 31 July 2026 CISF has not announced an official written exam date.

That status matters, because most pages covering this recruitment still read as though the form is open. If you applied, the next thing you are waiting for is the admit card, which CISF releases a few days before the written exam on the same portal. If you did not apply, this page is a full guide to what the post involves, what the standards are, and what to prepare for the next cycle.

24 posts across the whole country is a small recruitment. That single number should shape how you approach it, and this guide treats it honestly rather than presenting the recruitment as a wide-open opportunity.

## Important dates for CISF ASI Paramedical 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 8 June 2026 |
| Application window opened | 8 June 2026 |
| Last date to apply | 7 July 2026 (closed) |
| Age reckoned as on | 7 July 2026 |
| Written exam date | Not officially announced as of 31 July 2026 |
| Admit card | A few days before the exam, on cisfrectt.cisf.gov.in |

Several sites carried a "last week of July 2026" exam window, but that was a projection rather than a CISF announcement. Treat any date you see as unconfirmed until it appears on the official recruitment portal.

## Vacancy breakdown

The 24 posts are split across three paramedical trades, and the distribution is heavily weighted towards one of them.

| Post | Vacancies |
|---|---|
| ASI (Pharmacist) | 18 |
| ASI (Lab Technician) | 5 |
| ASI (X-Ray Technician) | 1 |
| Total | 24 |

Pharmacist accounts for three-quarters of the intake. The single X-Ray Technician post means that trade is effectively a one-seat national competition in this cycle. Category-wise reservation applies within each post as per central government rules, covering UR, EWS, OBC, SC, ST, and ex-servicemen quotas, and the exact category split is set out in the notification PDF. Vacancy numbers in CAPF recruitments are described as tentative and CISF can revise them, so the figure that governs your cycle is the one in the final notification.

## What these three posts actually do

CISF guards airports, metro networks, ports, nuclear and space installations, and major public sector plants, and it runs its own medical setup for the force and its families. Paramedical ASIs staff that setup rather than doing security duty.

An ASI Pharmacist dispenses medicines, maintains stock and records at CISF units and hospitals, and supports medical officers. An ASI Lab Technician runs pathology tests, prepares samples, and maintains lab equipment and reports. An ASI X-Ray Technician operates radiography equipment, positions patients, and processes imaging for the unit medical officer.

All three are non-gazetted posts in Group C, and all three carry the ASI rank, which is a supervisory rank above Head Constable in the CAPF hierarchy. Postings follow CISF units across the country, so an all-India transfer liability applies.

## Eligibility for CISF ASI Paramedical 2026

On nationality, you must be an Indian citizen.

On age, the band is 18 to 28 years reckoned as on 7 July 2026, the last date of application. Upper age relaxation follows central government rules.

| Category | Upper age relaxation |
|---|---|
| OBC (non-creamy layer) | 3 years |
| SC and ST | 5 years |
| Ex-servicemen | As per government rules |
| Departmental candidates | As specified in the notification |

On education, the requirement is trade-specific and this is where most rejections come from.

| Post | Qualification required |
|---|---|
| ASI (Pharmacist) | Class 12 pass, plus a Diploma or Degree in Pharmacy recognised by the central or a state government, plus registration as a Pharmacist under the Pharmacy Act, 1948 |
| ASI (Lab Technician) | Class 12 in Science, plus a 2-year Diploma in Medical Laboratory Technology from a recognised institution |
| ASI (X-Ray Technician) | Class 12 pass, plus a 2-year Diploma in Radiography from a recognised institution |

## The registration requirement that disqualifies applicants

For the Pharmacist post, a pharmacy diploma on its own is not enough. You must be registered as a Pharmacist under the Pharmacy Act, 1948, with a State Pharmacy Council, and be able to produce that registration at document verification.

This trips up candidates every cycle. A D.Pharm or B.Pharm graduate who never completed state council registration, or whose registration has lapsed and was not renewed, meets the education line on paper and still fails verification. Registration is a separate process with its own fee and renewal cycle, and it takes weeks rather than days at most state councils.

If you are preparing for a future CISF or CAPF pharmacist recruitment, complete the registration before the notification appears, not after. The same requirement applies across BSF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, and Assam Rifles pharmacist recruitments, so the registration is worth holding regardless of which force you target.

For the Lab Technician and X-Ray Technician posts, the diploma itself must be from a central or state government recognised institution. A certificate course, a short-duration private course, or a diploma from an unrecognised institute does not qualify, however relevant the training was.

## Physical standard test

Paramedical candidates face the same physical standards framework as other CAPF entries, though the role is a medical one. The PST checks height, chest, and weight, and it is qualifying, so it does not add to your merit score.

| Category | Male height | Male chest (unexpanded to expanded) | Female height |
|---|---|---|---|
| General, EWS, OBC, SC | 170 cm | 80 cm to 85 cm | 157 cm |
| Garhwali, Kumaoni, Gorkha, Dogra, Marathas and specified hill categories | 165 cm | 80 cm to 85 cm | 155 cm |
| Scheduled Tribes | 162.5 cm | 77 cm to 82 cm | 154 cm |

Chest measurement does not apply to female candidates. Weight must be proportionate to height and age as per the medical standards. The exact standards for your cycle are in the notification, and CISF applies them at the PST venue with no scope for appeal on measurement grounds beyond the on-spot re-measurement provision.

A practical point: candidates who clear the written exam but have never checked their height against the requirement lose the post at this stage. Measure yourself against the standard before you invest months in the written preparation.

## Selection process: five stages

Selection runs through five stages, and understanding which stage carries merit and which is only qualifying changes how you allocate effort.

1. Written examination. 100 marks, objective, and the only stage that builds your merit score.
2. Physical Standard Test (PST). Height, chest, and weight verification. Qualifying.
3. Documentation. Verification of education, registration, age, category, and identity documents.
4. Basic Vocational Aptitude Test (BVAT). A practical trade assessment. Qualifying.
5. Detailed Medical Examination (DME), with a Review Medical Examination (RME) for candidates declared unfit.

The final merit list is built from the written examination alone, subject to clearing every other stage. So the written exam decides your rank, and PST, BVAT, and the medical decide whether you stay in the process at all.

## Written exam pattern

The written examination is a single objective paper.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total marks | 100 |
| Duration | 2 hours |
| Question type | Objective, multiple choice |
| Language | English and Hindi |
| Negative marking | None |
| Mode | Computer based test or OMR |
| Focus | Trade knowledge for the post applied for |

No negative marking changes strategy completely. With no penalty for a wrong answer, leaving a question blank is a wasted mark, so attempt all 100 questions regardless of confidence. Candidates who carry over the cautious habits of exams like SSC or NDA, where wrong answers cost marks, routinely leave 10 to 15 questions unattempted here and lose ground in a merit list decided on a single paper.

## Syllabus by trade

The paper is weighted towards the professional subject of your post, with general sections alongside.

For ASI Pharmacist: pharmaceutics, pharmacology, pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacognosy, hospital and clinical pharmacy, drug store management, forensic pharmacy and the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, plus first aid and human anatomy. The D.Pharm syllabus is the right base to revise from.

For ASI Lab Technician: clinical pathology, haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, blood banking, histopathology, sample collection and handling, lab instrumentation, and biomedical waste management.

For ASI X-Ray Technician: radiographic anatomy and positioning, radiation physics, radiation protection and safety, X-ray equipment and processing, contrast media, and basic patient care during imaging.

Alongside the trade portion, expect general awareness, elementary reasoning, and basic arithmetic. Since the paper is trade-heavy, a candidate with a solid diploma foundation who revises the professional subject thoroughly is better placed than one who spends the bulk of preparation on general studies.

## What BVAT actually is

The Basic Vocational Aptitude Test is the stage candidates understand least, largely because most pages list the acronym and move on.

BVAT is a practical check of whether you can do the job you are being hired for. For a pharmacist that means handling and identifying drugs, reading and dispensing against a prescription, and maintaining stock records. For a lab technician it means sample handling, using standard lab equipment, and following test procedure. For an X-ray technician it means equipment handling, patient positioning, and radiation safety practice.

It is qualifying in nature, so the marks do not enter the final merit list. That does not make it a formality: a candidate who cannot demonstrate basic trade competence is out, whatever their written score. Revise the practical side of your diploma, not just the theory, before this stage.

## Medical examination

The Detailed Medical Examination applies CAPF medical standards, covering vision, hearing, general physical fitness, and freedom from conditions that would impair field duty. A candidate declared unfit at DME can request a Review Medical Examination within the timeline stated in the communication, which is the only appeal route on medical grounds.

Vision standards, colour perception, knock knee, flat foot, and varicose veins are the common grounds for rejection in CAPF medicals. Since the paramedical cadre is still a uniformed force posting with field liability, the standards are not relaxed for being a medical role.

## Salary of a CISF ASI Paramedical

The post sits at Pay Level 5 of the 7th Central Pay Commission matrix, with a pay band of Rs 29,200 to Rs 92,300.

Here is what that means in practice at entry. Basic pay starts at Rs 29,200 a month. Dearness allowance is paid on top at the prevailing rate, and House Rent Allowance depends on the classification of your posting city, at 30 per cent for X-class cities, 20 per cent for Y-class, and 10 per cent for Z-class, where CISF accommodation is not provided. Transport allowance, ration money, uniform allowance, and risk and hardship allowance apply as per CISF entitlement.

Taking a metro posting as a worked example, basic pay of Rs 29,200 plus dearness allowance at the current rate plus HRA at 30 per cent of basic brings gross monthly pay to roughly Rs 45,000 to Rs 55,000, before deductions. Deductions include the National Pension System contribution at 10 per cent of basic plus DA, the Central Government Health Scheme or equivalent medical contribution, and group insurance. In-hand pay at entry lands in the region of Rs 38,000 to Rs 45,000 depending on posting and current DA.

Recruits joining now come under the National Pension System rather than the old defined-benefit pension, which is a material difference from what older CISF personnel receive and worth factoring into any long-term comparison.

## Career progression in the CISF paramedical cadre

Entry as ASI is a rank above Head Constable, so a paramedical ASI starts higher in the hierarchy than a directly recruited constable.

| Rank | Pay level |
|---|---|
| Assistant Sub-Inspector (entry) | Level 5 |
| Sub-Inspector | Level 6 |
| Inspector | Level 7 |
| Subordinate Officer and above | As per cadre rules |

Promotion within the paramedical cadre runs through departmental promotion committees, based on seniority, service record, and available vacancies in the cadre. Because the paramedical cadre is small compared with the executive cadre, promotion pace depends heavily on vacancy position rather than a fixed timeline. Alongside pay, the post carries central government medical cover, leave entitlement, canteen facilities, group insurance, and CISF accommodation subject to availability.

## CISF ASI Paramedical compared with other CISF entries

Candidates often confuse the paramedical ASI with the executive ASI and with constable-level recruitments, which are different jobs with different entry routes.

| Entry | Role | Entry qualification | Selection focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASI Paramedical | Medical cadre: pharmacy, lab, radiography | Class 12 plus trade diploma, plus registration for pharmacist | Trade written paper, PST, BVAT, medical |
| ASI Executive | Security and supervisory duty | Graduation | Written, physical efficiency test, PST, medical |
| ASI Stenographer | Clerical and steno duty | Class 12 with stenography skill | Written plus skill test |
| Constable and Head Constable trades | Support trades such as cook, cobbler, driver | Class 10 or 12 with trade skill | Physical, trade test, written |

If you hold a paramedical diploma, the paramedical route is the one that values your qualification. The executive route needs a degree and a much heavier physical component, since it leads to security duty rather than medical duty.

## What 24 posts means for your strategy

A 24-post national recruitment draws applications in the tens of thousands, and with a single paper deciding merit, the cutoff sits high. That is the honest position, and it should push you towards two things.

Prepare the trade subject to a depth beyond your diploma exams, because when a merit list rests on one 100-mark paper with no negative marking, the difference between selection and rejection is a handful of marks on professional questions everyone else is also attempting.

Apply broadly across forces rather than waiting for CISF alone. BSF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, Assam Rifles, and the Railway Protection Force all recruit paramedical staff on similar patterns, and state police medical cadres, ESIC, and central hospital recruitments take the same diplomas. Candidates who track only one force wait years between opportunities. Candidates who track the CAPF recruitment portals collectively see several chances a year on largely overlapping preparation.

Defence-adjacent alternatives are worth knowing about too, including the [Indian Army Agniveer](/sarkari-naukri/indian-army-agniveer-2026) technical entries and, for candidates still in Class 12 who meet the age band, the officer route through [NDA and NA](/sarkari-naukri/nda-na-2026).

## How to apply for CISF ASI Paramedical

Applications for the 2026 cycle closed on 7 July 2026. This is the process for the next cycle.

1. Watch cisfrectt.cisf.gov.in for the notification. CISF publishes paramedical vacancies there rather than through a common CAPF portal.
2. Read the notification PDF for the vacancy split, category reservation, and the exact standards for your cycle before starting the form.
3. Register on the portal with a working email and mobile number, both of which CISF uses for admit card and stage communication.
4. Fill in personal, educational, and professional registration details exactly as they appear on your certificates.
5. Upload your photograph and signature in the specified dimensions and file size.
6. Pay the fee of Rs 100 online. Women, SC, ST, and ex-servicemen candidates pay nothing.
7. Submit and save the confirmation page and registration number, then download the admit card when it is released.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready before the form opens, since the window is roughly a month.

1. Class 10 certificate as proof of date of birth.
2. Class 12 mark sheet and certificate, in Science where the post requires it.
3. Your pharmacy, medical laboratory technology, or radiography diploma or degree with mark sheets.
4. State Pharmacy Council registration certificate, valid and current, for the Pharmacist post.
5. Caste or category certificate in the central government format, and an EWS certificate where applicable.
6. Ex-servicemen discharge documents where applicable.
7. Photograph, signature, and a photo identity document matching your application details.

## How to prepare

Preparation for this recruitment is narrower than for a general competitive exam, which works in favour of candidates who use their diploma well.

Start with the professional subject, since it dominates the paper. Work through your diploma syllabus systematically rather than relying on general guides, and pay attention to the areas a government service tests: drug schedules and the Drugs and Cosmetics Act for pharmacists, biomedical waste and safety protocol for lab technicians, and radiation protection for radiographers. These regulatory topics appear often and are the areas diploma students revise least.

Add a lighter layer of general awareness, elementary maths, and reasoning, enough to secure the marks available without displacing trade revision. Practise a full 100-question paper under a 2-hour clock so that attempting every question becomes habit, since there is no negative marking to guard against. Then, before the later stages, refresh the practical side of your trade for the BVAT and check your height and general fitness against the PST and medical standards.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the last date for CISF ASI Paramedical 2026?**
The application window closed on 7 July 2026. Applications opened on 8 June 2026 and ran for one month on cisfrectt.cisf.gov.in. The window is now shut for this cycle, and candidates who applied should watch the same portal for the admit card.

**What is the CISF ASI Paramedical exam date 2026?**
CISF has not announced an official written exam date as of 31 July 2026. Several sites carried a projected window in the last week of July 2026, but that was not a CISF announcement. The admit card, released a few days before the exam on cisfrectt.cisf.gov.in, is the reliable signal.

**How many vacancies are there in CISF ASI Paramedical 2026?**
There are 24 vacancies in total: 18 for ASI Pharmacist, 5 for ASI Lab Technician, and 1 for ASI X-Ray Technician. Category reservation applies within each post as per central government rules, and CISF describes vacancy numbers as tentative.

**What is the salary of a CISF ASI Paramedical?**
The post is at Pay Level 5 of the 7th CPC matrix, with a pay band of Rs 29,200 to Rs 92,300. With dearness allowance, House Rent Allowance, and CISF allowances, gross monthly pay at entry is roughly Rs 45,000 to Rs 55,000, and in-hand pay lands around Rs 38,000 to Rs 45,000 depending on posting city and the current DA rate.

**What is the age limit for CISF ASI Paramedical 2026?**
The age limit is 18 to 28 years, reckoned as on 7 July 2026. Upper age relaxation is 3 years for OBC non-creamy layer candidates and 5 years for SC and ST candidates, with ex-servicemen relaxation as per government rules.

**Is registration under the Pharmacy Act needed for CISF ASI Pharmacist?**
Yes. A pharmacy diploma or degree alone does not qualify you. You must be registered as a Pharmacist under the Pharmacy Act, 1948 with a State Pharmacy Council and produce a valid registration at document verification. Candidates whose registration has lapsed are rejected at that stage.

**Is there negative marking in the CISF ASI Paramedical exam?**
No. The written examination carries 100 marks over 2 hours with no negative marking, so an unattempted question is a lost mark with no offsetting risk. Attempt all questions.

**What is BVAT in CISF recruitment?**
The Basic Vocational Aptitude Test is a practical assessment of trade competence, such as drug handling and dispensing for pharmacists, sample handling and instrumentation for lab technicians, and equipment handling and radiation safety for radiographers. It is qualifying only, so its marks do not enter the final merit list, but failing it removes you from the process.

**What is the height requirement for CISF ASI Paramedical?**
The general standard is 170 cm for male candidates and 157 cm for female candidates, with a chest of 80 cm to 85 cm for males. Relaxed standards apply for Garhwali, Kumaoni, Gorkha, and specified hill categories at 165 cm for males and 155 cm for females, and for Scheduled Tribes at 162.5 cm for males and 154 cm for females.

**Can female candidates apply for CISF ASI Paramedical?**
Yes. Female candidates are eligible for all three paramedical posts, pay no application fee, and are assessed against female physical standards, where chest measurement does not apply. The rest of the process, including the written exam, BVAT, and medical examination, is the same.

**Is CISF ASI Paramedical a gazetted post?**
No. Assistant Sub-Inspector in the paramedical cadre is a non-gazetted Group C post. It is a supervisory rank above Head Constable in the CAPF hierarchy, and promotion runs to Sub-Inspector at Pay Level 6 and Inspector at Pay Level 7 through departmental promotion.

**Which other forces recruit paramedical staff on the same qualification?**
BSF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB, Assam Rifles, and the Railway Protection Force recruit paramedical staff on broadly similar patterns, and state police medical cadres, ESIC, and central government hospitals accept the same diplomas. Since CISF paramedical vacancies are few and irregular, tracking all the CAPF recruitment portals gives several opportunities a year on overlapping preparation.

ASI X-Ray Technician: 10+2 in Science with 2-year Diploma in Radiography from a Central or State Government recognized institution. ASI Lab Technician: 10+2 in Science with Diploma in Medical Lab Technology from a recognized institution.

content:
## IBPS RRB 2026: dates are out, the notification is not

IBPS RRB 2026, formally CRP RRB XV, is the common recruitment process for Regional Rural Banks across India, conducted by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection. The examination dates have been published in the IBPS calendar, but the detailed notification carrying vacancy numbers and eligibility conditions is still awaited, expected in August or September 2026.

That gap between announced dates and an unpublished notification is worth stating plainly, because most pages covering this recruitment present vacancy tables as though they were settled. They are not. Figures circulating in the region of 3,000 to 5,000 posts across 28 Regional Rural Banks are expectations drawn from previous cycles, not published numbers. Uttarakhand Gramin Bank has separately announced 323 posts of its own, which is a real figure but a single bank's rather than the national total.

Everything below distinguishes what is confirmed from what is reported.

Two features of RRB recruitment distinguish it from IBPS PO and IBPS Clerk, and both matter more than candidates expect. There is a local language requirement, which is a genuine eligibility gate. And the Office Assistant post has no interview stage at all, while the Officer Scale posts do.

## Confirmed exam dates

| Post | Prelims | Mains |
|---|---|---|
| Officer Scale I | 21 and 22 November 2026 | 20 December 2026 |
| Office Assistant (Multipurpose) | 6, 12 and 13 December 2026 | As per the notification |

Officer Scale II and III recruitments are conducted through a single examination rather than a prelims and mains structure, as set out in the notification for those posts.

Note the sequence. Officer Scale I prelims fall in late November, ahead of the Office Assistant prelims in December, and the Officer Scale I mains on 20 December sits between the Office Assistant prelims dates. A candidate applying for both posts, which is permitted, needs to plan for a dense five-week period rather than treating them as separate campaigns.

## The posts

| Post | Role |
|---|---|
| Office Assistant (Multipurpose) | Clerical work at branch level: counter operations, cash handling, account opening, passbook and record maintenance, customer service |
| Officer Scale I (Assistant Manager) | Entry-level officer: branch operations, credit appraisal, agricultural and rural lending, supervision of clerical staff |
| Officer Scale II (Manager) | Middle management, including specialist streams such as IT, Chartered Accountant, Law, Treasury, Marketing and Agriculture |
| Officer Scale III (Senior Manager) | Senior branch and regional responsibilities |

Regional Rural Banks operate in rural and semi-urban areas, sponsored by commercial banks and jointly owned by the central government, the sponsoring bank and the state government. The work is therefore weighted towards agricultural credit, rural deposits, government scheme disbursement, and the financial inclusion mandate, more so than at a metropolitan branch of a commercial bank.

## The local language requirement

This is the condition that most distinguishes RRB recruitment, and the one that most often disqualifies otherwise strong candidates.

Regional Rural Banks require proficiency in the local language of the state in which the bank operates. In practice this generally means having studied the local language as a subject at school level, commonly up to Class 10, and being able to read, write and speak it.

The reason is operational rather than bureaucratic. An RRB branch serves rural customers who transact in the local language, and a clerk or officer who cannot read a form filled in that language or explain a scheme to a customer cannot do the job.

Two consequences follow.

First, this is a state-linked recruitment in a way IBPS PO and Clerk are not. You apply to a specific state and bank, and your eligibility depends on the language of that state. A candidate from Bihar cannot casually apply to a Tamil Nadu RRB.

Second, candidates who studied outside their home state, or in a school where the local language was not offered, should check this carefully before applying. Verification typically happens at the document stage, which means discovering the problem after clearing two examinations.

The exact requirement is stated in the notification for each participating bank, and it is the document to check rather than a general assumption.

## Selection process, which differs by post

Candidates routinely assume a single process. There are two.

For Office Assistant (Multipurpose): a preliminary examination, then a main examination, and that is all. **There is no interview.** The final merit rests on the mains score alone.

For Officer Scale I: a preliminary examination, then a main examination, then an interview. The final merit is computed from the mains and the interview together, with the mains carrying the larger weight, commonly in an 80 to 20 ratio.

For Officer Scale II and III: a single examination followed by an interview.

That difference matters when choosing which post to apply for. A candidate who is strong on paper but finds interviews difficult has a cleaner route through Office Assistant. A candidate who interviews well has an advantage at Officer Scale I that does not exist at clerical level.

In both cases the preliminary examination is a screening stage: its marks do not carry into the final merit.

## Exam pattern

The preliminary examinations for both posts are short papers focused on reasoning and numerical ability, without a general awareness or English component.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Sections | Reasoning Ability and Numerical Ability (Quantitative Aptitude) |
| Total questions | 80 |
| Total marks | 80 |
| Duration | 45 minutes, with sectional timing |
| Negative marking | 0.25 marks per wrong answer |

The main examinations are longer, adding General Awareness with an emphasis on banking and rural economy, a language paper, and computer knowledge, for a total in the region of 200 marks. Candidates choose English or Hindi for the language paper.

Because IBPS finalises the section-wise composition of the mains in the notification, and it has varied between cycles, the structure above should be confirmed against the CRP RRB XV notification when it appears rather than assumed from a previous year.

45 minutes for 80 questions in the prelims gives you about 34 seconds per question, which makes the preliminary stage a pure speed test. Sectional timing means you cannot borrow minutes from reasoning to finish numerical ability.

## Eligibility

On age, the bands differ by post and are set in the notification, commonly running from 18 years for Office Assistant and from 18 or 21 for Officer Scale I, with upper limits in the late twenties to early thirties and the usual relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for other specified categories.

On education, a bachelor's degree in any discipline is the general requirement for both Office Assistant and Officer Scale I, with preference in some cases for candidates with degrees in agriculture, horticulture, forestry, animal husbandry, veterinary science, agricultural engineering, pisciculture, information technology, management, law, economics or accountancy. Officer Scale II specialist posts carry their own professional qualification requirements.

On language, proficiency in the local language of the state applied to, as described above.

Computer knowledge is generally required, with the notification specifying the form in which it must be evidenced.

## Salary

Office Assistant pay in Regional Rural Banks broadly tracks the clerical scale in the banking industry, and Officer Scale I broadly tracks the officer scale, both under the industry settlements applicable to RRBs.

Alongside basic pay come dearness allowance, house rent allowance depending on the classification of the branch location, transport allowance, medical benefits and pension provisions as applicable to new recruits.

One practical point specific to RRBs: because branches are in rural and semi-urban areas, house rent allowance and the cost of living are both generally lower than at a metropolitan commercial bank branch. The headline salary comparison with IBPS PO or Clerk therefore understates how far the money goes, while the posting locations are less likely to be in a large city.

Confirm the current pay scales in the notification, since banking pay is revised through periodic industry settlements.

## Career progression

Progression in an RRB runs through the officer scales.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Office Assistant | Direct entry |
| Officer Scale I | Promotion from clerical cadre, and direct recruitment |
| Officer Scale II | Promotion, and direct recruitment for specialist posts |
| Officer Scale III | Promotion |
| Senior management grades | Promotion |

An Office Assistant with a degree can move into the officer cadre through internal promotion, and many do. Alternatively, a serving clerk may sit the direct Officer Scale I recruitment in a later cycle, which is a faster route than waiting for departmental promotion.

## How IBPS RRB compares with IBPS PO and Clerk

| | IBPS RRB | [IBPS PO](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-po-2026) | [IBPS Clerk](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-clerk-2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Banks | 28 Regional Rural Banks | Public sector commercial banks | Public sector commercial banks |
| Local language | Required | Not required in the same way | Not required in the same way |
| Postings | Rural and semi-urban | All India, including metros | All India |
| Interview | Officer Scale I yes, Office Assistant no | Yes | No |
| Transfer liability | Within the bank's operating state | Wider | Wider |

The state-linked nature of RRB service is the substantive difference. An RRB operates within a defined area, so postings stay within that state, which for many candidates is the main attraction: a banking career near home rather than an all-India transfer liability.

Candidates preparing for IBPS PO or Clerk need little additional study for RRB beyond the rural and agricultural banking component of general awareness, so applying to all three in a season is common and sensible.

## What working in a Regional Rural Bank is actually like

Because RRBs are less familiar than the big commercial banks, it is worth describing the job rather than only the recruitment.

An RRB branch is typically small, often a handful of staff serving a cluster of villages or a semi-urban town. That means roles are broader than at a large commercial branch: an Office Assistant may handle counter work, cash, account opening, passbook printing and customer queries in the same day rather than sitting at a specialised desk.

The customer base is largely farmers, agricultural labourers, small traders, self-help groups and rural households. A substantial share of the work involves government schemes, since RRBs are a primary channel for disbursing agricultural credit, pensions, scholarship payments and direct benefit transfers.

Kisan Credit Card processing, crop loan disbursement and recovery, self-help group lending, and financial inclusion account opening are core activities rather than peripheral ones. An Officer Scale I in an RRB will spend more time on agricultural credit appraisal than an equivalent officer at a metropolitan commercial branch will in an entire career.

The character of the work suits some candidates and not others. It offers responsibility early, close contact with the community, and a posting near home. It also means rural living, smaller towns, and less exposure to the corporate banking work that a commercial bank career can offer.

Being clear-eyed about that before applying matters, because the local language requirement makes RRB service a longer-term commitment to a state than commercial banking is.

## Common mistakes in IBPS RRB applications

Assuming the local language condition is a formality. It is a genuine eligibility gate, verified at the document stage, and it has ended candidatures after two cleared examinations.

Treating Office Assistant and Officer Scale I as one process. They differ at the final stage, since one has no interview and the other does, and that should influence which you target.

Preparing prelims at mains pace. At about 34 seconds a question with sectional timing, the preliminary paper is a different exercise from the mains and needs its own timed practice.

Studying only commercial banking awareness. The rural and agricultural component is where RRB-specific marks sit, and it is the section a candidate preparing solely for IBPS PO will have skipped.

Waiting for the notification before starting. The dates are already fixed for late November and December, so preparation time is running now whether or not the vacancy table has been published.

Applying to a state on the strength of vacancy numbers alone. Since postings stay within the bank's operating state and the language condition binds, the choice of state is a long-term one rather than a numbers exercise.

## What to do before the notification

Confirm your local language position now. If you did not study the language of your target state at school, establish what evidence the previous notification accepted before you build a plan around applying there.

Begin prelims practice at speed. At roughly 34 seconds a question with sectional timing, the preliminary paper rewards trained pace more than depth, and that is buildable in the weeks available before late November.

Add rural and agricultural banking to your general awareness preparation: priority sector lending, NABARD's role, Kisan Credit Cards, self-help group linkage, financial inclusion schemes and the structure of Regional Rural Banks themselves. This is the part of the mains syllabus that differs most from commercial bank recruitment.

Decide which post you are targeting, since the absence of an interview for Office Assistant and its presence for Officer Scale I should influence the choice.

Watch ibps.in directly for the notification rather than relying on aggregator pages, since vacancy numbers, age bands and language conditions are all fixed there.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the IBPS RRB 2026 exam?**
The dates are confirmed in the IBPS calendar. Officer Scale I prelims are on 21 and 22 November 2026 with mains on 20 December 2026. Office Assistant prelims are on 6, 12 and 13 December 2026, with the mains date set in the notification. The detailed notification itself is expected in August or September 2026.

**How many vacancies are in IBPS RRB 2026?**
Not yet confirmed. Figures of roughly 3,000 to 5,000 posts across 28 Regional Rural Banks are expectations based on previous cycles rather than published numbers, and the CRP RRB XV notification will fix the actual total. Uttarakhand Gramin Bank has separately announced 323 posts, which is one bank's figure rather than the national one.

**Is a local language requirement compulsory for IBPS RRB?**
Yes, and it is the condition that most distinguishes RRB recruitment. Regional Rural Banks require proficiency in the local language of the state they operate in, generally evidenced by having studied that language at school level and being able to read, write and speak it. Since verification typically happens at the document stage, a candidate who does not meet it can discover the problem only after clearing two examinations.

**Is there an interview in IBPS RRB?**
It depends on the post. Office Assistant (Multipurpose) has no interview at all: the process is prelims then mains, and final merit rests on the mains score alone. Officer Scale I has prelims, mains and an interview, with the mains carrying the larger weight in the final merit. Officer Scale II and III have a single examination followed by an interview.

**What is the IBPS RRB prelims exam pattern?**
A short paper of 80 questions for 80 marks in 45 minutes, covering Reasoning Ability and Numerical Ability only, with sectional timing and 0.25 marks deducted per wrong answer. At about 34 seconds per question it is a pure speed test, and sectional timing means you cannot borrow minutes between sections. Prelims marks do not carry into the final merit.

**Do IBPS RRB prelims marks count in the final merit?**
No. The preliminary examination is a screening stage only. For Office Assistant the final merit is the mains score alone, and for Officer Scale I it is the mains and interview combined, with the mains weighted more heavily.

**What qualification is needed for IBPS RRB?**
Generally a bachelor's degree in any discipline for both Office Assistant and Officer Scale I, with preference in some cases for degrees in agriculture, horticulture, forestry, animal husbandry, veterinary science, agricultural engineering, pisciculture, information technology, management, law, economics or accountancy. Officer Scale II specialist posts carry their own professional requirements. Computer knowledge is generally required, and the local language condition applies.

**How is IBPS RRB different from IBPS PO and Clerk?**
RRB recruits for 28 Regional Rural Banks operating in rural and semi-urban areas, requires local language proficiency, and keeps postings within the bank's operating state rather than carrying an all-India transfer liability. IBPS PO and Clerk recruit for public sector commercial banks with wider postings and no equivalent language gate. For many candidates the attraction of RRB is a banking career close to home.

**Can I apply for both Office Assistant and Officer Scale I?**
Yes, and many candidates do. Note the calendar though: Officer Scale I prelims fall on 21 and 22 November, Office Assistant prelims on 6, 12 and 13 December, and Officer Scale I mains on 20 December, so the two campaigns overlap in a dense five-week period rather than running separately.

**What should I study for IBPS RRB general awareness?**
Beyond standard banking awareness, give specific attention to the rural and agricultural side: priority sector lending, the role of NABARD, Kisan Credit Cards, self-help group linkage, financial inclusion schemes, and the ownership and structure of Regional Rural Banks themselves. This is the portion of the syllabus that differs most from commercial bank recruitment and it is where RRB-specific marks sit.

**What is the salary in a Regional Rural Bank?**
Office Assistant pay broadly tracks the banking clerical scale and Officer Scale I the officer scale, under the industry settlements applicable to RRBs, with dearness allowance, house rent allowance by location, transport allowance, medical benefits and pension provisions on top. Because branches are rural and semi-urban, both house rent allowance and living costs tend to be lower than at metropolitan commercial bank branches. Confirm current scales in the notification, since banking pay is revised through periodic settlements.

**Where do I apply for IBPS RRB 2026?**
On ibps.in, once the CRP RRB XV notification is published. Watch that site directly rather than aggregator pages, since the vacancy numbers, age bands, educational conditions and the local language requirement for each participating bank are all fixed in the notification and vary between banks and states.
