content:
## SSC MTS 2026 at a glance

The Staff Selection Commission released the SSC MTS and Havaldar 2026 notification on 30 June 2026 for 7,948 posts, and the online application window closes on 31 July 2026. If you hold a Class 10 pass certificate and want a permanent central government job with no interview stage, this is one of the few large recruitments open right now.

The recruitment fills two post groups: Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff across central government departments, and Havaldar in the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) and the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN). Of the 7,948 vacancies, roughly 6,810 are MTS posts and 1,138 are Havaldar posts, per the SSC MTS 2026 notification.

One number sets the tone for how competitive this is. In the 2024 cycle SSC received well over 50 lakh applications for a similar vacancy pool, which works out to more than 600 candidates chasing each seat. The exam is Class 10 standard, but the cutoff is high precisely because the paper is easy and the field is enormous.

For candidates who have finished Class 10 and want a stable central government job without a graduation requirement or an interview, SSC MTS is one of the shortest routes in. The trade-off is that the entry pay is modest and the competition is heavy, so the difference between a seat and a near-miss usually comes down to a handful of marks in the second session. The rest of this guide covers every stage in detail, from the vacancy split and eligibility to the exam pattern, the worked in-hand salary, the cutoff trend, and how the job compares with SSC GD and CHSL.

## Important dates for SSC MTS 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 30 June 2026 |
| Online application begins | 30 June 2026 |
| Last date to apply | 31 July 2026 |
| Last date for fee payment | 31 July 2026 (11:00 PM) |
| Application correction window | Early August 2026 (per SSC notice) |
| Computer Based Test (Session I and II) | September to November 2026, per the SSC Exam Calendar |
| Age reckoned as on | 1 August 2026 |

Dates for the correction window and the exact CBT day are announced on ssc.gov.in through separate notices, so keep checking the login dashboard after you submit the form.

## Vacancy details

The 7,948 vacancies split across two age bands and the Havaldar cadre. The two MTS age groups exist because certain user departments set an 18 to 25 band while others use 18 to 27.

| Post | Age group | Approx vacancies |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) | 18 to 25 years | 6,078 |
| Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) | 18 to 27 years | 732 |
| Havaldar (CBIC and CBN) | 18 to 27 years | 1,138 |
| Total | | 7,948 |

For context on the trend, SSC notified 7,948 posts in the 2025 cycle, 11,518 in 2024, and 11,788 in 2023, per successive SSC notifications. The count moves with departmental demand each year, so treat the 2026 figure as the confirmed number and ignore any inflated projections you see on coaching pages.

## Eligibility for SSC MTS 2026

Age limit reads off the age group you apply for. Most MTS posts need 18 to 25 years as on 1 August 2026. Havaldar and some MTS posts allow 18 to 27 years. Category relaxation follows standard government norms.

| Category | Age relaxation |
|---|---|
| OBC (non-creamy layer) | 3 years |
| SC and ST | 5 years |
| PwBD (unreserved) | 10 years |
| PwBD (OBC) | 13 years |
| PwBD (SC and ST) | 15 years |
| Ex-servicemen | As per service rules |

On qualification, the bar is a Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board. A higher degree does not help or hurt your eligibility, and there is no minimum percentage. Nationality rules follow the usual clauses for Indian citizens plus the standard provisions for subjects of Nepal and Bhutan and Tibetan refugees who settled in India before 1962.

## Application fee

The fee is modest and waived for several categories, including all women candidates.

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC, EWS | Rs 100 |
| SC, ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen | Nil |
| All women candidates | Nil |

Pay online through BHIM UPI, net banking, or a debit or credit card. There is no offline challan option in the current cycle.

## Selection process

The MTS and Havaldar selection runs on a Computer Based Test with two sessions on the same day. There is no interview and no descriptive paper.

The stages are:

1. Computer Based Test, Session I and Session II, both compulsory for every candidate.
2. Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test (PET and PST), for Havaldar applicants only. This stage is qualifying.
3. Document verification, for candidates who clear the earlier stages.

Session I carries no negative marking, which makes it a section where you attempt everything. Session II carries a penalty of 1 mark for each wrong answer, so guesswork there costs you. That single design choice decides a lot of strategy, and most candidates who miss the cutoff do so by over-attempting Session II.

## Exam pattern

Both sessions run back to back. The full paper is 90 questions for 270 marks in 90 minutes, offered in English, Hindi, and 13 regional languages.

| Session | Subject | Questions | Marks | Duration | Negative marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | Numerical and mathematical ability | 20 | 60 | 45 min | None |
| I | Reasoning ability and problem solving | 20 | 60 | 45 min | None |
| II | General awareness | 25 | 75 | 45 min | 1 mark per wrong answer |
| II | English language and comprehension | 25 | 75 | 45 min | 1 mark per wrong answer |
| Total | | 90 | 270 | 90 min | Session II only |

Candidates who use a scribe get 60 minutes per session instead of 45. Session I acts as a screening qualifier and Session II decides the merit position within your category and age group.

## Syllabus for SSC MTS 2026

The paper stays at Class 10 standard across all four subjects. Depth matters less than speed and accuracy.

Numerical and mathematical ability covers integers, LCM and HCF, decimals and fractions, BODMAS, percentage, ratio and proportion, profit and loss, simple interest, averages, time and work, time speed and distance, and basic mensuration.

Reasoning ability and problem solving covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, classification, non-verbal patterns, direction sense, and blood relations.

General awareness covers current affairs (usually 7 to 8 questions), biology, history, polity, geography, economics, static general knowledge, sports, and awards. This is the section that separates candidates, since it rewards steady daily reading.

English language and comprehension covers reading comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, spotting errors, sentence structure, and synonyms and antonyms.

## SSC MTS 2026 salary and in-hand pay

MTS and Havaldar posts sit at Pay Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission, with a basic pay of Rs 18,000 and a scale of Rs 18,000 to Rs 56,900. The number that matters to you is the in-hand figure after dearness allowance, house rent allowance, and transport allowance, minus deductions.

Dearness allowance rose to 60 percent of basic pay effective 1 January 2026, per the Finance Ministry order. Many coaching pages still show a stale 17 to 50 percent DA, which understates the salary. Here is the worked in-hand pay at the current 60 percent DA, split by city class (X, Y, Z), for a Level 1 recruit.

| Component | X city (metro) | Y city | Z city |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic pay | Rs 18,000 | Rs 18,000 | Rs 18,000 |
| Dearness allowance (60%) | Rs 10,800 | Rs 10,800 | Rs 10,800 |
| House rent allowance (30 / 20 / 10%) | Rs 5,400 | Rs 3,600 | Rs 1,800 |
| Transport allowance (with DA) | Rs 2,160 | Rs 2,160 | Rs 1,440 |
| Gross | Rs 36,360 | Rs 34,560 | Rs 32,040 |
| Deductions (NPS, CGEGIS, CGHS) | about Rs 3,200 | about Rs 3,200 | about Rs 3,100 |
| Approx in-hand | about Rs 33,200 | about Rs 31,400 | about Rs 28,900 |

So a fresh MTS recruit posted in a metro takes home roughly Rs 33,000 a month, and the figure climbs every time DA is revised. Havaldar pay sits at the same Level 1, with the added duty profile of customs and narcotics field work.

## Havaldar PET and PST standards

Havaldar applicants clear a Physical Efficiency Test and a Physical Standard Test after the CBT. This stage is qualifying, not merit-deciding, but you cannot be appointed without passing it.

| Test | Male | Female |
|---|---|---|
| PET walk | 1,600 m in 15 minutes | 1 km in 20 minutes |
| PST height | 157.5 cm | 152 cm |
| PST chest (male) | 81 cm with 5 cm expansion | Not applicable |

Height relaxations of about 5 cm for men and 2.5 cm for women apply to candidates from hill communities such as Garhwalis, Assamese, and Gorkhas, and to Scheduled Tribe candidates.

## SSC MTS cutoff trend

Cutoffs vary by category, state, and age group, and they run high because the paper is easy. As a reference point, the All India unreserved cutoff for the 18 to 25 group sat near 147.78 marks in a recent cycle, per SSC result data.

| Category | Indicative cutoff (out of 270) |
|---|---|
| Unreserved (UR) | 142 to 152 |
| OBC | 138 to 145 |
| EWS | 134 to 140 |
| SC | 128 to 138 |
| ST | 120 to 132 |

Treat these as a planning band, not a promise. Your state and age group shift the exact figure, and the 18 to 27 pool usually closes at a slightly different mark than the 18 to 25 pool.

## SSC MTS vs SSC GD vs SSC CHSL

Candidates eligible for MTS often weigh it against [SSC GD Constable](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-gd-constable-2026) and [SSC CHSL](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-chsl-2026). This comparison sets out the real differences.

| Factor | SSC MTS | SSC GD Constable | SSC CHSL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum qualification | Class 10 | Class 10 | Class 12 |
| Pay Level | Level 1 (Rs 18,000) | Level 3 (about Rs 21,700) | Level 2 or 4 (Rs 19,900 to Rs 25,500) |
| Approx in-hand | Rs 29,000 to 33,000 | Rs 30,000 to 36,000 | Rs 30,000 to 40,000 |
| Nature of work | Office and support duties | Uniformed CAPF service | Clerical and data entry |
| Physical test | Havaldar posts only | Yes, for all posts | No |
| Promotion path | MTS to LDC to UDC to Section Officer | Constable to Head Constable to ASI | LDC or DEO to UDC to divisional cadre |

MTS suits candidates who want a stable desk job close to home with no physical test. SSC GD suits those ready for uniformed field service, and CHSL fits Class 12 pass candidates who want clerical roles at a slightly higher pay level.

## Career growth and promotions

An MTS recruit does not stay at Level 1. The typical ladder runs from MTS to Lower Division Clerk after about three years of service, then Upper Division Clerk, then Divisional Clerk, and up to Section Officer over a full career, with pay increments at each step. Havaldar recruits in CBIC and CBN handle field duties tied to customs checks and narcotics control, and they follow their own promotion track within those departments.

## Choosing your post and centre preference

The application form asks you to rank your post and department preferences and pick an examination centre. Two things are worth thinking about before you fill this in. First, the two MTS age bands (18 to 25 and 18 to 27) draw from different departmental vacancy pools, so your date of birth decides which posts you compete for. Second, Havaldar carries the physical test, so opt for it only if you can clear the walk and the height and chest standards, since a good CBT score is wasted if you fail the PET or PST. Pick a centre you can reach comfortably on exam day, because SSC rarely changes it once allotted, and a long commute on the morning of a two-session paper works against you.

## How to apply for SSC MTS 2026

1. Register on the SSC OTR (One Time Registration) portal at ssc.gov.in if you have not already.
2. Log in and open the SSC MTS and Havaldar 2026 application link.
3. Fill in personal, educational, and category details, and select your post preference and examination centre.
4. Upload a recent photograph and signature in the specified format.
5. Pay the Rs 100 fee if you fall in the paying category. Women and reserved categories pay nothing.
6. Submit before 31 July 2026 and save the confirmation page for your records.

## Documents required for the application

Keep these ready before you open the form, since the portal times out if you hunt for files midway.

1. A scanned passport-size photograph taken recently, in the size and format SSC specifies.
2. A scanned signature on white paper.
3. Your Class 10 certificate for the date of birth and qualification details.
4. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) if you claim relaxation.
5. Aadhaar or another government photo ID for the One Time Registration.
6. A working email and mobile number, since all admit card and result alerts go there.

## Admit card and exam day

SSC releases the admit card region by region, roughly 7 to 10 days before your CBT date, through the regional SSC website and your login dashboard. Download it, check that your name, photograph, category, and centre are correct, and carry a printout with the same photo ID you used at registration. Reach the centre early, since biometric and frisking checks take time and latecomers are turned away. Rough sheets are provided inside, and you must hand them back before leaving.

## Answer key, normalization, and result

After the CBT, SSC publishes a provisional answer key with an objection window, where you can challenge a wrong key for a small per-question fee that is refunded if your objection is upheld. Because the exam runs across many shifts and days, SSC applies normalization: your raw score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of your shift, so two candidates with the same raw marks in different shifts can end with different normalized scores. The merit list uses these normalized Session II scores within your category and age group. Keep an eye on the SSC website for the result, the marks release, and the document verification schedule, since each is announced through a separate notice.

## Building a study plan

Treat the last eight to ten weeks as a rehearsal, not a first read. Give the first half of that window to finishing every topic once and building speed on maths and reasoning, where Session I has no negative marking and rewards a full attempt. Give the second half to full-length mock tests taken at the same time of day as your slot, followed by a careful review of every wrong answer. For general awareness, a single daily current affairs source plus a static general knowledge booklet covers most of what the paper asks. English improves fastest through daily reading and a fixed set of grammar rules rather than memorising word lists. The candidates who convert this exam are rarely the ones who studied the most. They are the ones who made the fewest careless errors in Session II.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the last date to apply for SSC MTS 2026?**
The last date to apply for SSC MTS 2026 is 31 July 2026, with fee payment also closing on the same day at 11:00 PM. The notification was released on 30 June 2026.

**How many vacancies are there in SSC MTS 2026?**
SSC MTS 2026 has 7,948 vacancies, split into roughly 6,810 Multi-Tasking Staff posts and 1,138 Havaldar posts in CBIC and CBN, per the SSC MTS 2026 notification.

**Is there negative marking in SSC MTS 2026?**
Yes, but only in Session II. General awareness and English carry a penalty of 1 mark per wrong answer, while Session I (maths and reasoning) has no negative marking, so you can attempt every question there.

**What is the in-hand salary of SSC MTS in 2026?**
A Level 1 MTS recruit takes home about Rs 33,000 a month in a metro (X city) at the 60 percent dearness allowance effective 1 January 2026, and about Rs 29,000 in a Z-class city, after standard deductions.

**What is the qualification needed for SSC MTS?**
A Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board is the only qualification needed for SSC MTS. There is no minimum percentage and no upper degree requirement.

**Who has to appear for the PET and PST in SSC MTS?**
Only Havaldar applicants appear for the Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test. Multi-Tasking Staff posts have no physical test, and the Havaldar PET and PST are qualifying rather than merit-deciding.

**How is the SSC MTS age limit calculated?**
Age is reckoned as on 1 August 2026. Most MTS posts need 18 to 25 years, while Havaldar and some MTS posts allow 18 to 27 years, with category relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and up to 15 years for PwBD.

**What is the difference between MTS and Havaldar?**
MTS involves office and support duties across central government departments at Pay Level 1, while Havaldar is a field role in customs (CBIC) and narcotics control (CBN) at the same pay level, with an added physical test at selection.

content:
## UPSC ESE 2026 at a glance

The UPSC Engineering Services Examination 2026, still widely called IES, recruits 474 engineers into Group A officer posts across the government, and the cycle is well advanced. The notification came out on 26 September 2025, the Prelims were held on 8 February 2026, and the Mains were held on 21 June 2026. As of late July 2026, the Mains result and the Personality Test are awaited.

ESE is the most prestigious route into government engineering, because it leads to gazetted officer posts in services like the Railways, CPWD, and the Military Engineer Services, with real decision-making authority rather than a technician's role. The exam is open to four engineering disciplines and runs a demanding three-stage process. This guide covers the disciplines, the cadres you can join, the salary in detail, and how ESE compares with the GATE and SSC JE routes.

Here is where the 2026 cycle stands as of late July 2026: applications closed on 16 October 2025, the Prelims and Mains are done, and candidates are waiting on the Mains result and interview call letters. The ESE 2027 notification is expected around September 2026. So this page is a full guide for the exam stages and for candidates planning the next cycle, not an apply-now listing.

## Important dates for UPSC ESE 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 26 September 2025 |
| Application window | 26 September to 16 October 2025 |
| Prelims (Stage 1) | 8 February 2026 |
| Prelims result | 26 February 2026 |
| Mains (Stage 2) | 21 June 2026 |
| Mains result and Personality Test | Awaited (as of late July 2026) |

## Vacancy details by discipline

The 474 posts split across four engineering disciplines.

| Discipline | Vacancies |
|---|---|
| Civil Engineering | 199 |
| Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering | 118 |
| Mechanical Engineering | 85 |
| Electrical Engineering | 72 |
| Total | 474 |

Reservation applies service-wise across the posts as per government norms. Civil carries the largest share because the Railways, CPWD, and the water and roads services draw heavily from it, while Electrical has the fewest seats in this cycle.

## What ESE is and the services it recruits into

ESE feeds Group A gazetted officer posts, and a few Group B posts, across the central engineering services. The service you land depends on your discipline and your rank. The mapping below shows which disciplines typically feed which services, though the exact service list and seat split come from the notification.

| Discipline | Services it typically feeds |
|---|---|
| Civil | Indian Railway Service of Engineers, CPWD, Central Water Engineering Service, Border Roads Engineering Service, Military Engineer Services |
| Mechanical | Indian Railway cadres, Military Engineer Services, Indian Ordnance Factories, Central Power and Mechanical services |
| Electrical | Railway electrical cadres, Central Electrical and Mechanical Engineering Service, power services |
| Electronics and Telecommunication | Indian Telecommunication Service, Railway signal and telecom cadres, Indian Ordnance Factories |

An officer selected through ESE joins as an Assistant Executive Engineer or an equivalent, a Class-I gazetted post with responsibility for planning, execution, and supervision from early in the career.

## Eligibility for UPSC ESE 2026

On age, you must be between 21 and 30 years as on 1 January 2026, meaning born between 2 January 1995 and 1 January 2004. Relaxation applies: 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates, with further relaxation for ex-servicemen per the rules.

On qualification, you need a degree in engineering, that is a BE or BTech or an equivalent, in the relevant discipline, and some posts accept an MSc or specified degrees. On attempts, there is no cap: you may sit the exam as many times as you like within the age limit.

On nationality, you must be an Indian citizen, with the standard provisions for subjects of Nepal and Bhutan, Tibetan refugees, and persons of Indian origin from specified countries.

## Application fee

The fee is Rs 200 for General and OBC candidates. All female candidates and SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempt. Payment is online through net banking, a card, or UPI, or through an SBI challan. The fee once paid is not refunded, so confirm your discipline eligibility and age before you complete the payment step, since ESE eligibility is checked strictly at each stage.

## Selection process

ESE runs through three stages for a total of 1300 marks, and the final merit rests on the last two.

1. Stage 1, Preliminary Examination: two objective papers, 500 marks. This is a screening stage.
2. Stage 2, Mains Examination: two conventional, that is descriptive, papers, 600 marks.
3. Stage 3, Personality Test: an interview of 200 marks.

Prelims marks do not carry into the final merit. The merit is built from the Mains and the Personality Test, out of 800.

## Prelims exam pattern

The Prelims has two objective papers with a penalty of one-third mark for each wrong answer.

| Paper | Content | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | General Studies and Engineering Aptitude | 200 | 2 hours |
| Paper 2 | Engineering Discipline (your chosen branch) | 300 | 3 hours |

Paper 1 is common to all four disciplines, while Paper 2 is discipline-specific. Because both papers carry negative marking, judging which questions to leave is a scoring skill in itself.

## Mains exam pattern

The Mains has two conventional papers in your discipline, each of 300 marks and three hours, with no negative marking since the answers are written rather than multiple choice.

| Paper | Content | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | Discipline-specific (conventional) | 300 | 3 hours |
| Paper 2 | Discipline-specific (conventional) | 300 | 3 hours |

The Mains is where selection is decided, alongside the interview, so depth in your engineering subjects and the ability to write structured, well-presented answers under time both matter.

## Syllabus

Paper 1 of the Prelims covers General Studies and Engineering Aptitude, spanning current affairs, general principles of design and safety, standards and quality, basics of energy and environment, project management, and general engineering aptitude, alongside reasoning and numerical ability. Paper 2 of the Prelims and both Mains papers cover the full technical syllabus of your discipline at degree level. For Civil that spans structural engineering, geotechnical and foundation engineering, water resources, environmental engineering, transportation, and surveying. For Mechanical it spans thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, theory of machines, machine design, and manufacturing. For Electrical it spans circuits, machines, power systems, control systems, and power electronics. For Electronics and Telecommunication it spans electronic devices, signals and systems, communication, control, and networks.

## UPSC ESE 2026 salary

An ESE officer enters at Pay Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission as an Assistant Executive Engineer, with a basic pay of Rs 56,100. With dearness allowance at 60 percent effective 1 January 2026, per the Finance Ministry order, the in-hand works out well above the basic.

Here is a worked in-hand estimate in a metro (X-class city). On a basic of Rs 56,100, dearness allowance at 60 percent adds Rs 33,660. House rent allowance at the metro rate of 30 percent adds Rs 16,830, and transport allowance with DA adds about Rs 11,520. That is a gross near Rs 1,18,000 a month. After the National Pension System contribution and other deductions the in-hand lands close to Rs 1.05 to 1.08 lakh a month in a metro. Officers posted in the field or on special duty receive additional allowances on top. The pay grows through the officer grades over a career, and the pay range for the entry level runs from Rs 56,100 to Rs 1,77,500.

## UPSC ESE vs GATE vs SSC JE

Engineering graduates often weigh ESE against the GATE route into PSUs and against [SSC JE](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-je-2026). They lead to very different careers.

| Factor | UPSC ESE (IES) | GATE to PSU | SSC JE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conducting body | UPSC | IIT and IISc consortium | Staff Selection Commission |
| Qualification | Engineering degree | Engineering degree, final year allowed | Diploma or degree |
| Age limit | 21 to 30 (as on 1 Jan) | No age limit | Post-specific |
| Post level | Group A gazetted officer | PSU executive (E1) | Group B, Junior Engineer |
| Entry pay | Level 10, Rs 56,100 basic | About Rs 50,000 to 60,000 basic in a PSU | Level 6, Rs 35,400 basic |
| Selection | Three stages (Prelims, Mains, interview) | One exam plus a PSU interview | Prelims and Mains |
| Growth ceiling | Chief Engineer and above | General Manager or Director in a PSU | Executive Engineer, slower |

ESE gives officer authority and the widest promotion ceiling but demands the hardest, longest exam. The GATE route into a PSU offers strong pay with a single exam and no age bar. SSC JE is the most accessible, at Group B level, for diploma and degree holders. The right target depends on whether you want officer authority, PSU pay, or a quicker entry.

## Career growth as an ESE officer

ESE is an entry into a long officer career. An Assistant Executive Engineer rises through Executive Engineer, Superintending Engineer, and Chief Engineer over a career, and the most senior officers can reach the top technical and administrative posts in their service, up to secretary-level roles. Alongside pay progression come the security, allowances, and pension provisions of a central government officer post, plus the authority to lead major public infrastructure and engineering projects. That combination of authority and stability is why ESE remains the most sought engineering exam despite its difficulty.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the later stages.

1. Your engineering degree and mark sheets, or a final-year provisional proof where allowed.
2. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) where you claim relaxation.
3. Proof of date of birth, usually your Class 10 certificate.
4. A recent photograph, signature, and a valid photo ID matching your application.

## A preparation plan that fits ESE

ESE rewards a long, structured build rather than a sprint, because the technical syllabus is deep and the three stages test both objective speed and descriptive depth. Give the early months to building your discipline fundamentals to the level the Mains demands, since the same subjects power Prelims Paper 2 and both Mains papers. Add General Studies and Engineering Aptitude preparation for Prelims Paper 1, which many technical candidates underrate. As the Prelims nears, shift to timed objective practice and previous years' papers, and after clearing it, move to writing full-length conventional answers under time, since presentation and structure carry real weight in the Mains. Keep a short interview preparation going in parallel near the end. The candidates who convert ESE are usually those who treated the Mains and interview as seriously as the objective screen and who built depth steadily over many months.

## What an ESE officer actually does

The work varies by service, but the common thread is engineering leadership rather than routine execution. A Civil officer in the Railways or CPWD plans and supervises the construction and maintenance of railway infrastructure, government buildings, and public works, managing budgets, contractors, and subordinate technical staff. A Mechanical or Electrical officer in the Railways or the Military Engineer Services handles rolling stock, power, workshops, and installations. An Electronics and Telecommunication officer in the telecom services or railway signalling handles communication and signalling systems. From early in the career an ESE officer carries decision-making authority over projects and people, which is the core difference from a Junior Engineer role, where the work is more execution than planning. This authority, and the scale of the projects involved, is a large part of the appeal.

## Competition and cut-off context

ESE draws a very large field of engineering graduates for its few hundred posts, so the cut-off runs high and the three stages together filter hard. The Prelims shortlists candidates for the Mains at several times the number of final vacancies, the Mains narrows the field to those called for interview, and the final merit combines the Mains and the interview out of 800 marks. UPSC publishes category-wise and discipline-wise cut-offs with each cycle's result, and they vary year to year with the difficulty of the papers and the number of posts in each discipline. Because Civil carries the most seats and Electrical the fewest in this cycle, the effective competition differs by discipline, which is worth keeping in mind when you gauge your chances.

## Probation and cadre training

Selected officers undergo a period of probation and foundation and departmental training before and during their early posting, where they learn the specific procedures, codes, and responsibilities of their service. This structured induction is part of what makes ESE an officer entry rather than a direct technical hire: the training prepares candidates to take charge of projects and teams. The exact training pattern depends on the service you join, since the Railways, CPWD, and the Military Engineer Services each run their own induction.

## How to write the Mains conventional papers

The Mains is where many technically strong candidates lose ground, because it rewards presentation as much as knowledge. Each answer should open with the core concept, then work through the solution or explanation in clear steps, with neat diagrams, correct units, and labelled sketches where relevant. Managing time across the paper matters, since attempting every question briefly usually scores better than answering a few at great length and leaving others blank. Practising full-length conventional papers under the three-hour limit, then comparing your answers against model solutions, builds both speed and the habit of structured presentation. Because there is no negative marking in the Mains, attempt as much as you reasonably can, but never at the cost of legibility and structure, which the examiner rewards.

## Common mistakes candidates make

The first mistake is preparing only for the objective Prelims and leaving the descriptive Mains until after the result, when the Mains and interview decide selection. The second is neglecting General Studies and Engineering Aptitude in Prelims Paper 1, which is scoring and separates candidates. The third is over-attempting under the one-third negative marking in the Prelims. The fourth is underrating answer presentation in the Mains, where clear, structured, well-diagrammed answers score better than dense text. Avoiding these four puts a technically strong candidate in a much better position.

## Where ESE stands among engineering careers

For an engineering graduate weighing options, ESE occupies a distinct place. It is not the highest-paying entry, since some public-sector and private roles start higher, but it offers something they do not: the authority, security, and prestige of a Group A gazetted government officer, with charge of national infrastructure and a promotion ceiling that reaches the top of the technical services. The trade-off is the exam itself, one of the toughest and longest in the country, spanning an objective screen, a descriptive Mains, and an interview across several months. Candidates who value officer authority and long-term stability over the fastest or highest starting pay are the ones for whom ESE is the right target, and they are the ones who sustain the years of preparation it often takes. Understanding this trade-off honestly, before committing, is the first step in deciding whether ESE fits your goals or whether the GATE-to-PSU or Junior Engineer route suits you better.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is the UPSC ESE 2026 notification out?**
Yes. The UPSC ESE 2026 notification was released on 26 September 2025 for 474 vacancies. The Prelims were held on 8 February 2026 and the Mains on 21 June 2026, and the Mains result and Personality Test are awaited as of late July 2026.

**How many vacancies are there in UPSC ESE 2026?**
UPSC ESE 2026 has 474 vacancies: 199 in Civil Engineering, 118 in Electronics and Telecommunication, 85 in Mechanical, and 72 in Electrical Engineering.

**What is the age limit for UPSC ESE 2026?**
The age limit is 21 to 30 years as on 1 January 2026, meaning candidates born between 2 January 1995 and 1 January 2004, with relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD. There is no cap on the number of attempts within the age limit.

**Is there negative marking in UPSC ESE?**
Yes, in the Prelims. Both objective Prelims papers deduct one-third of a mark for each wrong answer. The Mains papers are conventional, that is descriptive, and carry no negative marking.

**What is the salary of an IES officer?**
An ESE officer enters at Pay Level 10 with a basic of Rs 56,100. At 60 percent dearness allowance effective 1 January 2026, the in-hand works out to about Rs 1.05 to 1.08 lakh a month in a metro, before field and special-duty allowances.

**Which engineering branches can apply for ESE?**
UPSC ESE is open to four disciplines: Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, and Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering. You compete within your discipline for the posts allotted to it.

**How many stages are there in UPSC ESE?**
UPSC ESE has three stages: a Preliminary objective exam of 500 marks, a Mains conventional exam of 600 marks, and a Personality Test of 200 marks. The final merit is built from the Mains and the Personality Test, out of 800.

**Is ESE better than the GATE route?**
They lead to different careers. ESE gives a Group A gazetted officer post with wide authority and the highest promotion ceiling but a harder three-stage exam. The GATE route into a PSU offers strong pay with a single exam and no age limit. The choice depends on whether you want officer authority or PSU pay and flexibility.

content:
## Bihar Police Constable 2026: what CSBC is actually running

Bihar Police constable recruitment is handled by the Central Selection Board of Constables, CSBC, through csbc.bihar.gov.in, and in 2026 it is not one recruitment but ten, covering a combined 31,603 posts. Searching for "Bihar Police Constable 2026" returns pages covering whichever batch that site happened to write about, which is why candidates end up confused about dates that seem to contradict each other.

They do not contradict each other. They belong to different recruitments running in parallel, each with its own written exam date and its own physical test window.

The other thing worth knowing before anything else: Bihar's selection works the opposite way round from Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. In those states the written exam decides merit and the physical test only qualifies you. In Bihar the written exam only qualifies you, at 30 per cent, and the Physical Efficiency Test is scored out of 100 marks. Your running, shot put and high jump performance is what builds your rank.

## The full CSBC 2026 calendar

This is every recruitment CSBC has scheduled, with post counts and stage timing as published in its exam calendar. Figures are tentative and CSBC revises them.

| Recruitment | Posts | Written exam | Physical test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constable (main Bihar Police batch) | 19,838 | Completed | 15 December 2025 to 11 March 2026 |
| Driver Constable | 4,361 | Completed | 12 March 2026 to 25 March 2026 |
| Warder | 2,417 | June 2026 | October to November 2026 |
| Forest Guard | 1,816 | September 2026 | December 2026 |
| Prohibition Constable | 1,685 | June 2026 | October to November 2026 |
| Radio Operator Constable | 993 | June 2026 | November to December 2026 |
| Forester | 188 | September 2026 | December 2026 |
| Mobile Squad Constable | 108 | June 2026 | October to November 2026 |
| Special Branch Constable | 83 | June 2026 | November 2026 |
| Jail Driver | 81 | September 2026 | December 2026 |
| Total | 31,603 | | |

The main constable batch of 19,838 posts is the one most candidates mean. Its written exam is complete, the result was declared on 26 September 2025, the physical efficiency test ran from 15 December 2025 to 11 March 2026, and the final result was expected around June 2026.

For the batches with written exams held in June 2026, covering Warder, Prohibition Constable, Radio Operator, Mobile Squad and Special Branch, the physical tests fall between October and December 2026. That gap is the training window, and candidates who treat it as a waiting period rather than a training period lose marks they cannot recover, because in Bihar those marks are the merit list.

## Why the Bihar structure changes your strategy

Get this the wrong way round and you prepare for the wrong exam.

| | Bihar Police | UP Police | MP Police |
|---|---|---|---|
| Written exam role | Qualifying only, 30 per cent needed | Decides merit | Decides merit |
| Physical test role | Scored out of 100, drives merit | Qualifying only | Qualifying only |
| What to optimise | Physical performance, once you clear 30 per cent | Written score | Written score |

In Bihar, once you have crossed 30 marks out of 100 in the written exam, extra written marks do nothing for your rank. A candidate scoring 85 in the written exam and a candidate scoring 32 arrive at the physical test on equal footing. From there, the person who runs 1.6 km faster and throws the shot further gets the job.

That is unusual, and it means the sensible allocation of effort for a Bihar aspirant is: secure the written comfortably above the 30 per cent bar, then put the bulk of your remaining months into physical training. Candidates who study for another six months to push a qualifying paper from 60 to 80 marks have gained nothing.

## What these ten posts actually are

CSBC advertises under names that mean little from outside the department, and candidates regularly apply to the wrong one.

Constable is the main District Police post: patrolling, station duty, law and order. Driver Constable is a constable who drives departmental vehicles and needs a valid heavy or light vehicle licence with the experience set in the advertisement. Warder is a Prison Department post guarding inmates inside jails rather than doing street policing. Prohibition Constable, or Madh Nishedh Sipahi, belongs to the Prohibition, Excise and Registration Department and enforces Bihar's liquor prohibition law, which in practice means raids, checkpoints and seizure work.

Mobile Squad Constable serves in mobile enforcement units. Special Branch Constable works in the intelligence wing, which is plain-clothes work rather than uniformed patrolling. Radio Operator Constable handles police wireless communication and carries a technical qualification requirement beyond the general Class 10 bar. Forest Guard and Forester belong to the Environment, Forest and Climate Change Department, protecting forest areas and wildlife, with Forester the senior of the two. Jail Driver drives for the Prison Department.

The written exam and physical standards are broadly common across them, so a candidate can prepare once and apply to several batches. Since each has its own advertisement, exam date and physical test window, applying to more than one is a straightforward way to raise your odds, and the CSBC calendar above shows which windows overlap.

## Eligibility

On age, the band for the constable posts runs from 18 years, with the upper limit varying by category: commonly 25 years for general male candidates, with relaxation for backward classes, women and reserved categories as set in each advertisement. Since CSBC fixes the reckoning date per recruitment, check the advertisement rather than assuming last cycle's dates.

On education, Class 10 pass from a recognised board is the requirement for the constable posts. Radio Operator Constable and the forest posts carry additional or higher requirements set out in their advertisements.

On domicile, a Bihar residence certificate is needed for reservation and relaxation benefits, and category certificates must be in the Bihar format. Candidates from other states may apply but are treated as unreserved.

## Written exam pattern

The written paper is common in structure across the CSBC constable recruitments.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total questions | 100 |
| Total marks | 100 |
| Marks per question | 1 |
| Duration | 2 hours |
| Negative marking | None |
| Minimum qualifying | 30 per cent, meaning 30 marks |
| Level | Class 10 |

With no negative marking and a pass bar at 30 marks, the paper is designed to filter rather than to rank. Attempt every question, since a blank is a certain zero and a guess costs nothing.

## Syllabus

The paper covers Hindi, English, Mathematics, Social Science across history, geography, civics and economics, and Science across physics, chemistry, zoology and botany, all at Class 10 level. Current affairs and Bihar-specific general knowledge appear as well, covering the state's districts, rivers, historical sites, agriculture and current schemes.

Because the bar is 30 marks out of 100, a candidate who is solid in two or three of these areas can clear it without mastering all of them. That is a genuine relief for candidates who have been out of school for some years, and it is the reason the physical test is where the competition actually happens.

## Physical measurement standards

The Physical Standard Test checks height and chest for men, and height and weight for women.

| Category | Male height | Male chest (unexpanded to expanded) |
|---|---|---|
| General and OBC | 165 cm | 81 cm to 86 cm |
| SC and ST | 160 cm | 79 cm to 84 cm |

Female candidates of all categories need a minimum height of 155 cm and a minimum weight of 48 kg. Chest measurement does not apply to women.

Note that the Bihar male height requirement of 165 cm is lower than Uttar Pradesh at 168 cm and Madhya Pradesh at 168 cm, which matters to candidates who fall between those figures and are choosing which state recruitments to target.

## The Physical Efficiency Test, scored out of 100

This is the stage that decides selection, so it deserves detail that most pages skip.

| Event | Maximum marks | Male standard | Female standard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Running | 50 | 1.6 km in under 6 minutes | 1 km in under 5 minutes |
| Shot put | 25 | 16 pound shot, minimum 16 feet | 12 pound shot, minimum 12 feet |
| High jump | 25 | Minimum 4 feet | Minimum 3 feet |

The figures in the last two columns are the minimums needed to score at all. Marks within each event are awarded on a sliding scale, so a faster run or a longer throw earns more, up to the maximum for that event. Failing to meet a minimum in any event means no marks from it, which in a merit list built on 100 PET marks is close to fatal.

Running carries half the total, so it is where preparation pays most. 1.6 km in under 6 minutes is a pace of about 3 minutes 45 seconds per kilometre, which is a hard middle-distance effort rather than a jog, and the faster you go under that ceiling the more of the 50 marks you take.

Shot put and high jump together carry the other half, and they are the events candidates neglect. Both reward technique heavily. A candidate with no coaching typically throws well short of their strength because of poor release angle and footwork, and the same is true of high jump approach and takeoff. A few sessions with someone who knows the technique often adds more distance than months of untargeted gym work, and 25 marks is a large share of a 100-mark merit list.

## Building a training plan

Given the structure, here is where the effort belongs once your written paper is secure.

For running, build an aerobic base of 20 to 30 km a week, then add one weekly interval session of repeated 400 metre efforts at faster than target pace with short recoveries, and one weekly time trial over the full 1.6 km so you know your real number rather than an estimate.

For shot put, work on the glide or standing throw technique first and strength second, and practise with a shot of the correct weight rather than a substitute, since the timing differs.

For high jump, practise the approach run and takeoff, since clearing 4 feet is a technique problem for most candidates rather than a power problem.

Start at least four to six months before your physical test date. Looking at the CSBC calendar above, candidates whose written exams were held in June 2026 have physical tests in October to December 2026, which is exactly that window.

## Salary of a Bihar Police Constable

The post sits at Pay Level 3 with a pay matrix range of Rs 21,700 to Rs 69,100.

Entry basic pay is Rs 21,700 a month, with dearness allowance at the prevailing rate, house rent allowance depending on the classification of the posting city, and police allowances covering uniform and kit. In-hand pay at entry works out in the region of Rs 30,000 to Rs 37,000 a month depending on posting and current DA, before deductions. Accommodation in police lines is available at many postings, and the post carries state medical facilities, leave entitlement, and pension benefits under the rules applicable to new recruits.

## Career progression

| Rank | Route |
|---|---|
| Constable | Direct entry |
| Head Constable | Departmental promotion and departmental exam |
| Assistant Sub-Inspector | Promotion on seniority and departmental exam |
| Sub-Inspector | Promotion, and separately through direct BPSSC Sub-Inspector recruitment |
| Inspector and above | Promotion on seniority and service record |

A serving constable who is a graduate and within the age band can appear for the Bihar Police Subordinate Services Commission Sub-Inspector recruitment, which moves you up several rungs at once rather than waiting on departmental seniority.

## How to apply

Applications for CSBC recruitments are filed only on csbc.bihar.gov.in.

1. Watch csbc.bihar.gov.in for the advertisement for the specific batch you want, since each recruitment has its own advertisement number and window.
2. Register with a working mobile number and email, which CSBC uses for admit card and stage communication.
3. Fill the form with details exactly as on your Class 10 certificate, which also proves date of birth.
4. Enter domicile and category details accurately, since reservation and relaxation depend on them.
5. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format.
6. Pay the fee online and save the confirmation.
7. Download the admit card when released, and check the physical test schedule separately, since it is published well after the written result.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 certificate and mark sheet, serving as proof of date of birth.
2. Bihar residence or domicile certificate.
3. Caste certificate in the Bihar format for SC, ST, EBC and BC candidates, with a current non-creamy layer certificate where applicable.
4. EWS certificate where claimed.
5. Documents for horizontal reservation such as ex-servicemen, home guard or sports certificates.
6. Photograph, signature, and a photo identity document matching the application.

## Frequently asked questions

**How many vacancies has CSBC announced for Bihar Police in 2026?**
CSBC's 2026 exam calendar covers 31,603 posts across ten recruitments: 19,838 Constable, 4,361 Driver Constable, 2,417 Warder, 1,816 Forest Guard, 1,685 Prohibition Constable, 993 Radio Operator Constable, 188 Forester, 108 Mobile Squad Constable, 83 Special Branch Constable and 81 Jail Driver. The figures are tentative and CSBC revises them.

**Is the Bihar Police Constable written exam merit based?**
No. The written exam is qualifying only, and you need 30 per cent, meaning 30 marks out of 100, to move ahead. Merit is built from the Physical Efficiency Test, which is scored out of 100 marks. This is the opposite of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, where the written score decides merit and the physical test only qualifies. Confirm the merit basis in the advertisement for your batch.

**How are Bihar Police PET marks calculated?**
The PET carries 100 marks: 50 for running, 25 for shot put and 25 for high jump, awarded on a sliding scale by performance. Male candidates must run 1.6 km in under 6 minutes, throw a 16 pound shot at least 16 feet, and clear a 4 foot high jump. Female candidates must run 1 km in under 5 minutes, throw a 12 pound shot at least 12 feet, and clear 3 feet. Those are minimums to score at all, and better performance earns more marks.

**Is there negative marking in the Bihar Police Constable exam?**
No. The written exam has 100 questions of 1 mark each over 2 hours with no deduction for wrong answers, so every question should be attempted. The qualifying bar is 30 marks out of 100.

**What is the height requirement for Bihar Police Constable?**
Male candidates in the General and OBC categories need 165 cm with a chest of 81 cm to 86 cm, and SC and ST male candidates need 160 cm with a chest of 79 cm to 84 cm. Female candidates of all categories need 155 cm and a minimum weight of 48 kg. The Bihar male requirement of 165 cm is lower than Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, which both ask for 168 cm.

**What is the salary of a Bihar Police Constable?**
The post is at Pay Level 3 with a range of Rs 21,700 to Rs 69,100. Entry basic pay is Rs 21,700, and with dearness allowance, house rent allowance and police allowances, in-hand pay at entry is roughly Rs 30,000 to Rs 37,000 a month depending on posting city and the current DA rate, with police line accommodation available at many postings.

**What is the status of the 19,838 post Bihar Police Constable recruitment?**
The written exam is complete and its result was declared on 26 September 2025. The Physical Efficiency Test ran from 15 December 2025 to 11 March 2026, and the final result was expected around June 2026. Candidates should check csbc.bihar.gov.in for the current position on the final result and appointment.

**Which Bihar Police recruitments have physical tests later in 2026?**
Warder, Prohibition Constable and Mobile Squad Constable have physical tests scheduled for October to November 2026, Special Branch Constable in November 2026, Radio Operator Constable in November to December 2026, and Forest Guard, Forester and Jail Driver in December 2026. Candidates who cleared the June or September 2026 written exams have that period as their training window.

**What is the syllabus for the Bihar Police Constable exam?**
The paper covers Hindi, English, Mathematics, Social Science across history, geography, civics and economics, and Science across physics, chemistry, zoology and botany, all at Class 10 level, along with current affairs and Bihar general knowledge. Since the bar is 30 marks out of 100, strength in a few of these areas is enough to qualify.

**Should I focus on the written exam or the physical test for Bihar Police?**
Secure the written exam above the 30 per cent bar, then put the bulk of your effort into physical training. Marks above the qualifying bar add nothing to your rank, so a candidate scoring 85 and one scoring 32 reach the physical test on equal terms, and the merit list is decided entirely by PET performance out of 100.

**What is the official website for Bihar Police Constable recruitment?**
Applications, admit cards, results and physical test schedules are published on csbc.bihar.gov.in, the Central Selection Board of Constables portal. Each recruitment has its own advertisement number, so check that you are reading the advertisement for the batch you applied to.

content:
## UP Police Constable 2026: where the recruitment stands

UP Police Constable 2026 is a recruitment of 32,679 posts by the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board, and the written exam is done. UPPRPB notified the vacancies on 31 December 2025, applications ran to 30 January 2026, and the written exam was held on 8, 9 and 10 June 2026 in two shifts a day across 1,180 centres in all 75 districts. As of 31 July 2026, candidates are waiting on the result.

At 32,679 posts this is one of the largest single recruitments in the country, and what follows the result is a sequence rather than a single event: document verification, then the Physical Standard Test, then the Physical Efficiency Test. Candidates who scored well and stopped training after the exam are the ones who struggle at that last stage, because the running standard is not casual.

One rule change deserves the top of this page, because a large share of pages covering this exam still get it wrong. There is no negative marking in the UP Police Constable written exam. The Uttar Pradesh government abolished it through a Cabinet decision in December 2025, given effect by the UP Police Constable and Head Constable Service (Fourth Amendment) Rules 2025. Pages telling you that half a mark is deducted per wrong answer are describing the old rules.

## Timeline of the 2026 cycle

| Stage | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 31 December 2025 |
| Applications open | 31 December 2025 |
| Last date to apply | 30 January 2026 |
| Admit card released | 5 June 2026 |
| Written exam | 8, 9 and 10 June 2026, two shifts daily |
| Result | Awaited as of 31 July 2026 |
| Document verification, PST and PET | After the result, dates to be announced |

The exam ran in shifts from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm and from 3:00 pm to 5:00 pm. Because the paper was held across six shifts over three days, UPPRPB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is not simply your raw score. Two candidates with the same raw marks in different shifts can end up with different normalised scores depending on the relative difficulty of their papers.

## Vacancy breakdown

The 32,679 posts cover several wings of the Uttar Pradesh Police rather than a single role.

| Post | What the role involves |
|---|---|
| Constable Civil Police | District policing, patrolling, law and order, station duty |
| Constable PAC (Provincial Armed Constabulary) | Armed reserve battalions, deployed for law and order and security duty |
| Constable Special Security Force | Protection of specified installations and establishments |
| Constable Mounted Police | Horse-mounted policing duty |
| Jail Warden | Prison department duty |

Allocation across wings happens after selection, based on merit, preference and vacancy position. Category reservation applies as per Uttar Pradesh government rules, with horizontal reservation for women, ex-servicemen, dependants of freedom fighters, and sportspersons on top of the vertical category split.

## Eligibility

On domicile, candidates from outside Uttar Pradesh may apply, but reservation benefits and the associated relaxations apply only to candidates holding a UP category certificate. Outside candidates are treated as unreserved.

On age, the band for the last cycle was 18 to 25 years for male candidates and 18 to 28 years for female candidates, with relaxation of 5 years for SC, ST and OBC candidates of Uttar Pradesh, and further relaxation for other specified categories. The reckoning date is set in the notification.

On education, Class 12 pass from a recognised board is the requirement, which is a higher bar than the Class 10 required for constable posts in several other states.

## Exam pattern

The written exam is a single objective paper.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total questions | 150 |
| Total marks | 300 |
| Marks per question | 2 |
| Negative marking | None, abolished from the 2026 cycle |
| Duration | 120 minutes |
| Mode | Offline pen and paper, OMR based |
| Medium | Hindi and English |

The four sections are General Knowledge, General Hindi, Numerical and Mental Ability, and Mental Aptitude with reasoning and IQ, carrying broadly equal weight at around 37 or 38 questions each in recent cycles.

With no negative marking, leaving anything blank is a straightforward loss. 150 questions in 120 minutes gives you 48 seconds per question, so the sensible approach is to move fast through what you know, mark the rest, and reserve the final five minutes for filling every remaining bubble. Under the old rules that behaviour would have cost you marks. Under the current rules it can only help.

## What the rule change means

The removal of negative marking is not a small administrative tweak, and it is worth understanding what it changes.

Under the old pattern, a wrong answer cost half a mark, so a candidate answering 30 uncertain questions and getting 10 right gained 20 marks and lost 10, netting 10. Under the current rules the same candidate gains 20 and loses nothing. Across a full paper this shifts scores upward for everyone who attempts fully, which in turn pushes the cutoff up. So the change does not make selection easier. It makes it harder for anyone who still attempts cautiously, because they are competing against a field that is now answering everything.

The rule change came through a Cabinet decision in December 2025 and was given effect by the UP Police Constable and Head Constable Service (Fourth Amendment) Rules 2025, which covered the Jail Warder recruitment as well.

## Syllabus

The paper sits at Class 12 level across four sections, and the Uttar Pradesh portion of the general knowledge is where the marks are most reliably available.

General knowledge covers Indian history, the freedom movement, geography, polity and the Constitution, economy, general science, and current affairs of the past year, with a distinct Uttar Pradesh component: the state's districts and divisions, rivers, agriculture, industries, historical sites, tribes and festivals, police organisation, and current state schemes. UP-specific questions appear in every cycle and are the section a candidate can study to near-certainty.

General Hindi covers grammar, sandhi and samas, tatsam and tadbhav, synonyms and antonyms, idioms and proverbs, error correction, and comprehension of a passage. Candidates who studied in English medium routinely underestimate this section, and it carries the same weight as the others.

Numerical ability covers arithmetic at Class 10 level: number system, percentage, ratio and proportion, average, profit and loss, simple and compound interest, time and work, time and distance, mensuration, and elementary data interpretation through tables and graphs.

Mental ability, mental aptitude, IQ and reasoning cover logical reasoning, analogies, series, coding and decoding, blood relations, direction sense, ranking, syllogism, Venn diagrams, alphabet and word formation, and non-verbal reasoning through figure series and mirror images. This section also carries questions on public interest, law and order sensitivity, and communal harmony, which are specific to police recruitment and rarely covered in general competitive material.

## Physical Standard Test

The PST checks height, chest for men, and weight for women. It is qualifying only.

| Category | Male height | Male chest (unexpanded to expanded) | Female height | Female minimum weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General, OBC and SC | 168 cm | 79 cm to 84 cm | 152 cm | 40 kg |
| Scheduled Tribe | 160 cm | 77 cm to 82 cm | 147 cm | 40 kg |

Every male candidate must show a chest expansion of at least 5 cm. A candidate who meets the 79 cm unexpanded figure but cannot expand to 84 cm fails the stage, so expansion is measured on its own terms and not treated as a formality.

## Physical Efficiency Test

The PET is a single running event, and it is the one that eliminates the most people.

| Candidates | Distance | Time limit |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 4.8 km | 25 minutes |
| Female | 2.4 km | 14 minutes |

Work out what the male standard demands. 4.8 km in 25 minutes is a pace of about 5 minutes 12 seconds per kilometre, held for nearly five kilometres. That is not a sprint, but it is a sustained running pace that a person who does not run cannot produce on the day, whatever their general fitness. The female standard of 2.4 km in 14 minutes works out to about 5 minutes 50 seconds per kilometre over a shorter distance.

Both are pass or fail with no partial credit and no marks carried into the merit list. Candidates who fail to finish within the time are out of the recruitment regardless of their written score.

Training for a 4.8 km time trial means building an aerobic base of 25 to 40 km a week over three to four months, with one weekly interval session at target pace and one longer run. A candidate starting from no running background needs months, not weeks, which is why the gap between the written exam and the PET is the window to use rather than to rest in.

## Selection process

| Stage | What it decides |
|---|---|
| Written examination | Merit. This is the only stage that scores you |
| Document verification | Eligibility, category, domicile and education |
| Physical Standard Test | Qualifying, on height, chest and weight |
| Physical Efficiency Test | Qualifying, on the run |

Final merit rests on the normalised written score alone. The physical stages are gates, not scoring events. That structure rewards a candidate who prepares the paper seriously and clears the physical standards comfortably, rather than one who is exceptionally fit and average on paper.

## Salary of a UP Police Constable

The post sits at Pay Level 3 of the pay matrix, with a range of Rs 21,700 to Rs 69,100. Under the older pay band structure this corresponded to Rs 5,200 to Rs 20,200 with grade pay.

At entry, basic pay is Rs 21,700 a month. Dearness allowance applies at the prevailing rate, house rent allowance depends on the classification of the posting city, and there are police allowances covering uniform and kit, alongside travel allowance. Accommodation in police lines is available at many postings.

In practice, in-hand pay for a new constable lands in the region of Rs 30,000 to Rs 38,000 a month depending on posting and the current DA rate, before deductions for pension contribution and insurance. Pay rises with annual increments and each DA revision, and promotion to Head Constable moves you to the next level.

Beyond cash, the post carries medical facilities, leave entitlement, and pension benefits under the rules applicable to new recruits.

## Career progression

| Rank | Route |
|---|---|
| Constable | Direct entry |
| Head Constable | Departmental promotion and departmental exam |
| Sub-Inspector | Promotion, and separately through direct UPPRPB Sub-Inspector recruitment |
| Inspector | Promotion on seniority and service record |
| Deputy Superintendent of Police | Promotion, and through the UPPSC state services exam |

A serving constable who holds a graduate degree and remains within the age band can appear for the direct Sub-Inspector recruitment, which is a faster route up than waiting for departmental promotion. Constables planning a long career often work towards that exam in their early years of service.

## What to do while the result is awaited

The gap between a written exam and the physical stages is the most wasted period in police recruitment, and using it well is the cheapest advantage available.

Start running now if you have not been. The PET follows document verification, and once the result lands the timeline moves quickly. Build to a comfortable 4.8 km well under 25 minutes so that a bad day still clears the bar.

Get your documents in order. Domicile certificate, category certificate in the UP format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, Class 10 and 12 certificates, and any horizontal reservation proof. Document verification rejections on paperwork are common and entirely avoidable.

Check your height and chest against the standard honestly, since finding out at the PST venue that you fall a centimetre short is the worst possible time.

If the result does not go your way, the preparation transfers. The written syllabus overlaps heavily with other state police recruitments, including [MP Police Constable](/sarkari-naukri/mp-police-constable-2026) and [Bihar Police Constable](/sarkari-naukri/bihar-police-constable-2026), where only the state-specific general knowledge changes.

## How to apply in the next cycle

Applications are filed only on uppbpb.gov.in.

1. Register with a valid mobile number and email, both of which UPPRPB uses for admit card and stage communication.
2. Fill in personal, educational, and category details exactly as they appear on your certificates.
3. Upload photograph and signature in the specified dimensions and file size.
4. Pay the application fee online.
5. Submit and save the registration number and the application PDF.
6. Use the correction window if one is provided, then download the admit card when released.

Note that the last window ran for a month from 31 December 2025 to 30 January 2026, so it is not a window that rewards waiting.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 certificate as proof of date of birth.
2. Class 12 mark sheet and certificate.
3. Uttar Pradesh domicile certificate.
4. Category certificate in the UP format, with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates.
5. Horizontal reservation documents for women, ex-servicemen, sportspersons, or dependants of freedom fighters where claimed.
6. Photograph, signature, and a photo identity document matching the application.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is there negative marking in the UP Police Constable exam 2026?**
No. The Uttar Pradesh government abolished negative marking through a Cabinet decision in December 2025, given effect by the UP Police Constable and Head Constable Service (Fourth Amendment) Rules 2025, which also covered Jail Warder recruitment. Each of the 150 questions carries 2 marks and nothing is deducted for a wrong answer, so every question should be attempted. Pages still showing a 0.5 mark penalty describe the old rules.

**When will the UP Police Constable result 2026 be declared?**
UPPRPB had not declared the result as of 31 July 2026. The written exam was held on 8, 9 and 10 June 2026 and the result will be published on uppbpb.gov.in, after which document verification, the Physical Standard Test and the Physical Efficiency Test follow. Because the exam ran across six shifts, scores are normalised before the result.

**How many vacancies are in UP Police Constable 2026?**
There are 32,679 posts, covering Constable Civil Police, PAC, Special Security Force, Mounted Police and Jail Warden. UPPRPB notified them on 31 December 2025. Allocation across wings happens after selection on the basis of merit, preference and vacancy position.

**What is the PET running standard for UP Police Constable?**
Male candidates must run 4.8 km in 25 minutes and female candidates 2.4 km in 14 minutes. The male standard is a pace of roughly 5 minutes 12 seconds per kilometre sustained for nearly five kilometres. The PET is qualifying, so it adds no marks, but failing to finish within the time removes you from the recruitment regardless of your written score.

**What is the height requirement for UP Police Constable?**
Male candidates in the General, OBC and SC categories need 168 cm with a chest of 79 cm unexpanded and 84 cm expanded, while Scheduled Tribe male candidates need 160 cm with a chest of 77 cm to 82 cm. Female candidates need 152 cm in the General, OBC and SC categories and 147 cm for Scheduled Tribes, with a minimum weight of 40 kg. Every male candidate must show a chest expansion of at least 5 cm.

**What is the salary of a UP Police Constable?**
The post is at Pay Level 3 with a pay matrix range of Rs 21,700 to Rs 69,100. Entry basic pay is Rs 21,700, and with dearness allowance, house rent allowance and police allowances the in-hand figure is roughly Rs 30,000 to Rs 38,000 a month depending on posting city and the current DA rate, with police line accommodation available at many postings.

**What is the exam pattern for UP Police Constable 2026?**
The written exam has 150 objective questions for 300 marks in 120 minutes, offline on OMR, in Hindi and English, with 2 marks per correct answer and no negative marking. The four sections are General Knowledge, General Hindi, Numerical and Mental Ability, and Mental Aptitude with reasoning and IQ, at broadly equal weight.

**What is the educational qualification for UP Police Constable?**
Class 12 pass from a recognised board is required. This is a higher bar than several other state police constable recruitments, which accept Class 10, so candidates comparing options across states should check this before applying.

**What is normalisation in the UP Police Constable exam?**
The exam ran in two shifts a day across three days, so six different question papers were used. UPPRPB applies a normalisation formula to adjust for differences in difficulty between shifts, which means your final score can differ from your raw score. Two candidates with identical raw marks in different shifts may receive different normalised scores.

**Can candidates from other states apply for UP Police Constable?**
Yes, candidates from outside Uttar Pradesh can apply, but they are treated as unreserved and receive no reservation benefit or associated age relaxation, since those require a Uttar Pradesh category certificate. The written syllabus also carries substantial Uttar Pradesh general knowledge, which favours candidates from the state.

**What happens after the UP Police Constable written result?**
Shortlisted candidates go to document verification, where domicile, category, education and date of birth documents are checked, then to the Physical Standard Test for height, chest and weight, then to the Physical Efficiency Test for the run. All three stages are qualifying. The final merit list is prepared from the normalised written exam score alone.
