## SBI PO 2026 at a glance

State Bank of India is recruiting 1,500 Probationary Officers under advertisement CRPD/PO/2026-27/09, notified on 18 June 2026. This is the single most chased banking job in India, and the numbers show why: SBI PO draws several lakh applicants for a fixed intake, so the real contest is not eligibility but clearing a high cut-off across three demanding stages.

Here is where the cycle stands as of 28 July 2026. Applications opened on 18 June and closed on 8 July 2026, so the form is no longer live. The preliminary exam is scheduled for 1 and 2 August 2026, and the prelims call letter is already available for download on the SBI careers portal. If you applied, your task now is the prelims; if you are researching for the next cycle, this page lays out exactly what the exam demands.

Of the 1,500 posts, 1,446 are regular vacancies and 54 are backlog vacancies. The recruitment is for Junior Management Grade Scale I officers, a permanent SBI officer-cadre role with a fast promotion track and a starting in-hand pay that clears most other clerical and officer bank jobs.

## Important dates for SBI PO 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 18 June 2026 |
| Online application begins | 18 June 2026 |
| Last date to apply | 8 July 2026 |
| Prelims call letter | Available (July 2026) |
| Preliminary exam | 1 and 2 August 2026 |
| Mains exam | September 2026 (expected) |
| Phase III (Psychometric, Group Exercise, Interview) | After mains result |

The mains date is not yet officially fixed, so treat September 2026 as expected until SBI confirms it on the careers portal. SBI usually announces the mains date and releases the mains call letter only after the prelims result, so keep checking your login dashboard through August 2026.

## Vacancy details

The 1,500 posts split into 1,446 regular and 54 backlog vacancies. The category-wise breakup of the regular posts is below.

| Category | Vacancies |
|---|---|
| Unreserved (UR) | 588 |
| OBC | 390 |
| SC | 234 |
| ST | 144 |
| EWS | 144 |
| Total (regular) | 1,500 |

## Eligibility for SBI PO 2026

Age and qualification are the two gates, and both are checked as on 1 April 2026.

On age, you must be between 21 and 30 years, that is, born between 2 April 1996 and 1 April 2005, both inclusive. Category relaxation applies over the upper limit: 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

On qualification, you need a graduation in any discipline from a recognised university, with no minimum percentage. Final-year students can apply provisionally but must produce proof of graduation before the interview stage. If your marks are in CGPA, convert them to a percentage using your college formula for the form.

On attempts, SBI limits the number of times General and EWS candidates can appear, while OBC and reserved candidates get more or no cap. The exact attempt limits change between cycles, so confirm the figure in the CRPD/PO/2026-27/09 notification rather than assuming a past cycle's rule.

## Application fee

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC, EWS | Rs 750 |
| SC, ST, PwBD | Nil |

Payment is online through debit card, credit card, or net banking. The fee is not refundable once paid, so confirm your eligibility on age, qualification, and category before you complete the payment step.

## Selection process

SBI PO runs through three phases, and unlike most bank exams it adds a psychometric test and a group exercise on top of the interview.

1. Preliminary examination: a qualifying screen. Its marks do not count toward the final merit.
2. Main examination: objective plus descriptive. This decides your position going into the final phase.
3. Phase III: a psychometric test, a group exercise, and a personal interview.

The final merit is built from the mains score and the Phase III score. Prelims only decides who moves to the mains.

## Preliminary exam pattern

The prelims is a 100-mark test of 100 questions in one hour, with 20-minute sectional timing and a penalty of 0.25 marks per wrong answer.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| English Language | 30 | 30 | 20 min |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Reasoning Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Total | 100 | 100 | 60 min |

The sectional timing is the catch: you cannot carry saved minutes from one section into another, so pace within each 20-minute block decides your score as much as accuracy.

## Main exam pattern

The mains has an objective paper of 200 marks and a descriptive paper of 30 marks, with sectional timing throughout and the same 0.25 penalty on objective questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reasoning and Computer Aptitude | 40 | 60 | 50 min |
| Data Analysis and Interpretation | 30 | 60 | 45 min |
| General, Economy and Banking Awareness | 60 | 60 | 45 min |
| English Language | 40 | 20 | 40 min |
| Objective total | 170 | 200 | 3 hr |
| Descriptive (letter and essay) | 2 | 30 | 30 min |

The descriptive paper tests a letter and an essay, and it is evaluated only if you clear the objective cut-off. General and banking awareness carries the most weight relative to preparation time, so a daily current affairs and banking-news habit pays off directly here.

## Syllabus

Quantitative Aptitude and Data Interpretation cover simplification, number series, quadratic equations, arithmetic (percentage, ratio, time and work, profit and loss), and data interpretation sets. Reasoning covers puzzles, seating arrangement, syllogism, coding and decoding, inequalities, and data sufficiency, with computer aptitude in the mains. English covers reading comprehension, cloze test, error spotting, sentence rearrangement, and vocabulary. General, Economy and Banking Awareness covers current affairs of the last six months, banking and financial terms, RBI and monetary policy basics, and static general knowledge.

## SBI PO 2026 salary and in-hand pay

SBI PO is a Junior Management Grade Scale I officer post on SBI's own pay scale, not the central government pay scale, so its dearness allowance follows SBI's bipartite settlement rather than the 7th Pay Commission. The starting basic is Rs 48,480, and a graduate entrant gets four advance increments of Rs 2,000, which lifts the effective starting basic to about Rs 56,480 a month.

Here is a worked in-hand estimate at the SBI bipartite scale. On an effective basic near Rs 56,480, dearness allowance under the SBI settlement adds roughly Rs 15,300, house rent allowance adds about Rs 4,500, and a special allowance plus city and other allowances add close to Rs 16,000. That is a gross near Rs 93,000 to Rs 98,000 a month. After deductions for provident fund, the pension contribution, and professional tax (together around Rs 13,000), the in-hand lands at about Rs 80,000 to Rs 82,000 a month in a metro. The annual cost to company works out near Rs 22 lakh in a metro posting. In-hand varies with the posting city because house rent allowance changes by location.

## SBI PO cut-off trend

Cut-offs move year to year with the difficulty of the paper. As a reference, the 2025 cycle closed near these marks.

| Stage | General | OBC | SC | ST | EWS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prelims (out of 100) | 66.75 | 65.50 | 59.25 | 51.50 | 64.50 |
| Mains (out of 250) | 75 | 69.50 | 62.75 | 62.51 | 75 |

The general-category mains cut-off has swung from about 94.85 in 2021 to 70 in 2023, 87.50 in 2024, and 75 in 2025, per SBI result data, which is why comparing your target with a single past year is misleading. Remember that prelims marks do not carry into the final merit; the mains and Phase III decide selection.

## SBI PO vs IBPS PO

Candidates preparing for SBI PO usually also weigh [IBPS PO](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-po-2026). This comparison sets out the real differences.

| Factor | SBI PO | IBPS PO |
|---|---|---|
| Recruiter | State Bank of India only | 11 or more public-sector banks |
| Recent vacancies | 1,500 (2026) | Several thousand (varies by year) |
| Starting basic | Rs 48,480 (about Rs 56,480 with increments) | Rs 36,000 |
| Final stage | Psychometric, group exercise, and interview | Interview |
| Descriptive test | Yes, in the mains | No |
| Difficulty | Higher, tougher reasoning and a descriptive paper | Moderate |

SBI PO pays more from day one and promotes fast, but its exam is tougher and its intake is a fraction of IBPS PO. IBPS PO spreads your chance across many banks with a slightly gentler paper. Most serious aspirants prepare for both, since the syllabi overlap heavily.

## What a bank PO actually does

A Probationary Officer starts as a scale I officer and, after a probation and training period, handles branch operations, customer relationships, loan processing, and supervision of clerical staff. The role carries decision-making responsibility from early on, which is why the selection tests aptitude, communication, and a group exercise rather than rote knowledge alone. Postings are all India at the bank's discretion, so a willingness to relocate is part of the job. Early years often mean a rural or semi-urban branch, which builds the ground-level banking experience that later officer roles are built on, and the exposure counts toward faster promotion.

## Career growth at SBI

SBI PO is one of the fastest promotion tracks in Indian banking. An officer moves from Junior Management Grade Scale I to Middle Management Grade Scale II and III, then into Senior Management and Top Executive grades over a career, through a mix of promotion exams and performance. The bank also offers postings abroad and specialised roles in treasury, credit, and risk as you rise. This mobility, combined with the pay that starts higher than most other bank jobs, is why SBI PO stays the most competitive banking exam year after year.

## Phase III explained: psychometric, group exercise, and interview

The final phase is where SBI PO differs most from other bank exams, and candidates who prepare only for the written stages often stumble here. The psychometric test profiles your personality traits and behaviour tendencies, and its output is used as an input to the interview rather than as a separate scored round. The group exercise puts you in a small group to discuss or solve a given situation, and the panel watches how you contribute, listen, and lead without dominating. The personal interview then probes your background, banking awareness, and reasoning under questioning. Together the group exercise and interview carry the Phase III marks that combine with your mains score for the final merit. The practical lesson is that strong communication and composure matter as much as your written score, so mock interviews and group discussions in the weeks before the final phase are time well spent.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the later stages, since the process pauses if you cannot produce them on time.

1. A recent passport-size photograph and a scanned signature in the SBI-specified format.
2. Your graduation degree and mark sheets, or a final-year provisional proof.
3. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) where you claim relaxation.
4. A valid photo ID that matches your registration details.
5. An active email and mobile number, since every call letter and result alert goes there.

## Admit card and exam day

SBI releases the call letter stage by stage, roughly a week before each exam, on the careers portal. Download it, check that your name, photograph, and centre are correct, and carry a printout with the same photo ID you used at registration. Reach the centre early, because biometric verification and document checks take time and latecomers are refused entry. The exam is computer based, so no rough paper of your own is allowed; the centre provides sheets that you return before leaving. Electronic devices, smart watches, and written material lead to disqualification, so leave them out.

## How to score the descriptive paper

The mains descriptive paper of 30 marks is small but decisive, because many candidates cluster within a few marks in the objective section and the descriptive score breaks the tie. It tests a letter and an essay, usually on a banking, economy, or general social topic. For the letter, follow the standard format, keep the tone appropriate to the recipient, and stay within the word limit. For the essay, spend the first few minutes planning a clear structure of introduction, two or three body points with an example each, and a short conclusion, rather than writing whatever comes first. Correct grammar and a clean structure score better than long, unfocused writing. Because it is typed on screen, practising a few timed essays and letters on a keyboard before the exam removes a real disadvantage on the day.

## How to prepare for SBI PO

With prelims on 1 and 2 August 2026, the near-term task for applicants is speed under sectional timing, so daily timed drills in all three sections beat long untimed study. For the mains, data interpretation, general and banking awareness, and the descriptive paper carry the weight, so build a six-month current-affairs base and practise letter and essay writing under time. Because the syllabus overlaps with IBPS PO and other bank exams, one strong preparation base serves several applications at once, which is the efficient way to work through a bank-exam season.

## Common mistakes candidates make

The first mistake is over-attempting the prelims. Because it is only a screen, the goal is to clear the cut-off comfortably, not to answer every question, and the 0.25 penalty means a string of guesses can pull a strong candidate below the line. The second is treating general and banking awareness as something to cram at the end, when it rewards a daily habit built over months and carries heavy weight in the mains. The third is ignoring the descriptive paper and Phase III until the mains is done, when both need their own practice, especially typing speed for the descriptive and mock group discussions for the final phase. The fourth is comparing your target with a single past cut-off, when the general mains cut-off has moved between 70 and 95 across recent years. Avoiding these four puts you ahead of a large part of the field before the paper even begins.

## A realistic study timeline

If you are preparing for the next cycle rather than this one, a six to eight month runway works well. Spend the first half building fundamentals across quantitative aptitude, reasoning, and English, and starting a daily current-affairs habit that you never break. Use the second half for full-length mock tests of both prelims and mains, taken at the same time of day as the real slot, followed by a careful review of every wrong answer to find your recurring error patterns. Add descriptive writing practice and a few mock interviews in the final two months. The candidates who convert SBI PO are rarely the ones who studied the most hours; they are the ones who made the fewest careless errors under time and who prepared for the final phase as seriously as the written stages.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the SBI PO 2026 exam date?**
The SBI PO 2026 preliminary exam is scheduled for 1 and 2 August 2026, and the prelims call letter is already available on the SBI careers portal. The mains is expected in September 2026, with the exact date to be confirmed by SBI.

**How many vacancies are there in SBI PO 2026?**
SBI PO 2026 has 1,500 vacancies under advertisement CRPD/PO/2026-27/09, made up of 1,446 regular and 54 backlog posts, for Junior Management Grade Scale I Probationary Officers.

**What is the SBI PO in-hand salary in 2026?**
An SBI PO takes home about Rs 80,000 to Rs 82,000 a month in a metro, on an effective starting basic of Rs 56,480 (Rs 48,480 plus four increments) at the SBI bipartite scale, after allowances and deductions. The annual cost to company is near Rs 22 lakh.

**Is there negative marking in SBI PO?**
Yes. Both the prelims and the mains objective papers deduct 0.25 marks for each wrong answer. There is no penalty for unattempted questions, and no negative marking in the descriptive paper or Phase III.

**What is the age limit for SBI PO 2026?**
The age limit is 21 to 30 years as on 1 April 2026, meaning candidates born between 2 April 1996 and 1 April 2005. Relaxation is 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

**Is SBI PO tougher than IBPS PO?**
SBI PO is generally considered tougher, with harder reasoning and data interpretation, a descriptive paper in the mains, and a group exercise and psychometric test in the final phase that IBPS PO does not have. SBI PO also has a much smaller intake relative to applicants.

**Is there a minimum percentage for graduation in SBI PO?**
No. SBI PO requires a graduation in any discipline from a recognised university with no minimum percentage. Final-year students may apply provisionally but must produce proof of graduation before the interview.

**Do prelims marks count in the final SBI PO merit?**
No. The preliminary exam is only a qualifying screen to shortlist candidates for the mains. The final merit is built from the mains score and the Phase III score of psychometric test, group exercise, and interview.

content:
## SEBI Grade A 2026: recruitment for Assistant Manager posts

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) conducts the Grade A Officer (Assistant Manager) exam once every year to recruit officers into India's securities market regulator. The 2026 cycle is expected to be notified in August 2026, with Phase 1 in October 2026. Total vacancies are typically 100 to 200 per cycle, split across streams (General, Legal, Information Technology, Engineering, Research, Rajbhasha, Official Language). Entry-level compensation is Rs. 1.35 to Rs. 1.45 lakh per month including all allowances. That puts SEBI Grade A and RBI Grade B in the same salary bracket, the two top-paying entry-level roles at central financial regulators.

## Important dates for SEBI Grade A 2026

| Event | Date (expected) |
|---|---|
| Official notification | August 2026 |
| Registration opens | **August 2026** |
| Last date to apply | September 2026 |
| Phase 1 (Prelims) exam | **October 2026** |
| Phase 1 result | November 2026 |
| Phase 2 (Mains) exam | November to December 2026 |
| Phase 2 result | January 2027 |
| Interview | February to March 2027 |
| Final result | March to April 2027 |

Confirm every date against the official notification at sebi.gov.in when it is released. Dates above reflect the typical SEBI Grade A cycle timing based on 2023, 2024, and 2025 recruitments.

## SEBI Grade A 2026 streams and vacancies

Recruitment happens across the following streams. Vacancy distribution varies by cycle but the 2024 pattern is the useful reference (97 total posts):

| Stream | Typical share | 2024 vacancies (reference) |
|---|---|---|
| General | Largest allocation | 30 to 40 |
| Legal | Small allocation | 5 to 10 |
| Information Technology | Medium allocation | 10 to 20 |
| Research | Small allocation | 5 to 10 |
| Engineering (Civil, Electrical) | Small allocation | 3 to 5 |
| Rajbhasha (Official Language) | 1 to 2 posts | 1 to 2 |
| Official Language | 1 to 2 posts | 1 to 2 |

The General stream is the most competitive (about 70,000 applicants for 30 to 40 posts, giving a selection ratio of roughly 1:2,000). Niche streams like Legal, IT, and Research have selection ratios closer to 1:500, which is why candidates with degree matches for those streams should target them directly instead of applying through the General stream.

## Eligibility for SEBI Grade A 2026

Eligibility is stream-specific. All streams share the same age criteria.

**Age (as on the reference date in notification, typically August 1 of the notification year):**

- General: 30 years maximum
- Relaxations: OBC NCL up to 33, SC/ST up to 35, PwBD up to 40, Ex-servicemen 5 years additional per rules

**Educational qualification by stream:**

| Stream | Required qualification |
|---|---|
| General | Bachelor's degree from a recognised university with 60% marks (55% for SC/ST/PwBD) |
| Legal | Bachelor's degree in Law (LLB) with 60% marks, or 5-year integrated law degree |
| Information Technology | BE/BTech/BSc in Computer Science, IT, Electronics, Software Engineering, or MCA/MSc in IT with 60% marks |
| Engineering (Civil) | BE/BTech in Civil Engineering with 60% marks |
| Engineering (Electrical) | BE/BTech in Electrical Engineering with 60% marks |
| Research | Master's degree in Statistics, Economics, Finance, Business Administration (Finance), or Commerce with 55% marks |
| Rajbhasha | Master's in Hindi with English as a subject at graduation, or Master's in English with Hindi as a subject |
| Official Language | Master's degree in Hindi with English as a subject at Bachelor's, or Master's in Sanskrit/English/Economics/Commerce with Hindi as a subject |

Final-year candidates can apply provisionally but must submit their degree certificate before the deadline specified in the notification.

## Application fee for SEBI Grade A 2026

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General / OBC / EWS | Rs. 1,000 |
| SC / ST / PwBD | Rs. 100 |
| Women | Rs. 100 |
| Ex-servicemen | Nil |

Fees are non-refundable and payable online during the application window only.

## How to apply for SEBI Grade A 2026 step by step

Applications are accepted only through the SEBI recruitment portal at sebi.gov.in. Offline applications are not accepted.

1. Visit sebi.gov.in and navigate to the Careers section, then Recruitment.
2. Click on the SEBI Grade A 2026 notification link and register with your name, email, mobile number, and date of birth. You receive a registration ID and password by email.
3. Log in with the registration ID and complete the detailed application form: personal, educational, work experience, and stream preference.
4. Upload photograph (200 KB max, JPG), signature (100 KB max, JPG), and category or PwBD certificate if applicable.
5. Pay the application fee online via UPI, net banking, debit card, or credit card.
6. Submit and download the final application form. Print at least two copies for interview and future reference.

Save your registration ID and password securely; they are needed at every subsequent stage (admit card download, result check, interview call).

## SEBI Grade A 2026 selection process

Selection has three stages: Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and Interview. All three must be cleared to receive a final offer.

### Phase 1: online screening (200 marks, 60 minutes total)

Phase 1 is a qualifying stage. Marks do not count in the final merit but you must clear the sectional and total cutoffs to progress to Phase 2.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Awareness | 40 | 40 | 25 mins |
| English Language | 40 | 40 | 25 mins |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 40 | 40 | 25 mins |
| Reasoning | 40 | 40 | 25 mins |
| Awareness of Securities Market | 40 | 40 | 25 mins |

Note: sectional timings are individually allotted; you cannot borrow time across sections. Negative marking is one-fourth of the marks awarded for a correct answer.

### Phase 2: online descriptive and objective (300 marks, 3 papers)

Phase 2 marks are used for the final merit. There are three papers.

#### Paper 1: English (descriptive), 100 marks, 60 minutes

Essay, precis, comprehension. Same for all streams.

#### Paper 2: stream-specific (objective), 100 marks, 60 minutes

For General stream: Commerce, Accountancy, Management, Finance, Costing, Companies Act, Economics.
For Legal: General Legal Knowledge including Constitution, Contract Act, Company Law, Securities Laws.
For IT: Data structures, Programming, DBMS, Operating Systems, Networks, Web Technology.
For Research: Statistics, Econometrics, Economics, Business Analysis.

#### Paper 3: stream-specific advanced (100 marks, 60 minutes)

Case studies and applied analysis in your chosen stream. Some streams include a mix of objective and short-descriptive questions.

### Interview (100 marks)

Candidates who clear Phase 2 are called for a personal interview at SEBI Mumbai headquarters (or via video conferencing for some cycles). Interview weightage is 100 marks. Final merit is computed on Phase 2 marks plus Interview marks; the ratio is typically 85 percent Phase 2 plus 15 percent Interview.

## Salary and allowances for SEBI Grade A officer

SEBI Officer Grade A (Assistant Manager) starting pay structure at Mumbai posting:

| Component | Approximate value |
|---|---|
| Basic pay | Rs. 44,500 per month |
| Dearness Allowance (DA) | Rs. 45,000 to Rs. 55,000 (revised quarterly) |
| House Rent Allowance (HRA) or leased accommodation | Rs. 22,000 to Rs. 35,000 or Bank quarters |
| Grade Allowance | Rs. 6,800 |
| Family Allowance | Rs. 2,000 |
| Local Allowance | Rs. 1,500 |
| Special Allowance | Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 12,000 |
| **Gross monthly (Mumbai)** | **Rs. 1.35 lakh to Rs. 1.45 lakh** |

Net in-hand after NPS, tax, and other deductions is approximately Rs. 1.05 lakh to Rs. 1.15 lakh at entry level.

Beyond the monthly package, SEBI officers get:

- Leased accommodation in Mumbai (Rs. 1.5 lakh per month rental value for a 2 or 3 BHK), or HRA if you opt for self-arranged housing
- Medical coverage for self and dependents including dental and vision
- Newspaper allowance, book allowance, briefcase allowance
- Concessional loans for housing, vehicle, and education (interest rates 4 to 6 percent)
- Leave Fare Concession (LFC) once every 2 years for the officer and family
- Contribution to National Pension System (NPS)

Total cost to organisation (CTC) at Grade A level is approximately Rs. 20 to Rs. 24 lakh per year, which places SEBI Grade A at the top of central government financial regulator compensation alongside RBI Grade B.

## SEBI Grade A career progression

Direct-recruit officers move up the SEBI hierarchy in this order:

Grade A (Assistant Manager) then Grade B (Manager), Grade C (Assistant General Manager), Grade D (Deputy General Manager), Grade E (General Manager), Chief General Manager, Executive Director, and finally Whole-Time Member.

Typical progression timeline: Grade A to Grade B in 4 to 5 years, Grade B to Grade C in 4 to 6 years. Compensation at Grade D level crosses Rs. 3 lakh per month. Senior positions (Chief General Manager and above) are largely by selection and cross Rs. 4 lakh per month with executive perks.

## Preparation strategy for SEBI Grade A 2026

### Phase 1: 2 to 3 months focused prep

- General Awareness and Securities Market: read The Hindu Business Line and Economic Times daily. Cover NCFM modules for basics of securities market. Time: 45 minutes per day.
- English: focus on error spotting, cloze, and reading comprehension. Practice 5 sets a week.
- Quantitative Aptitude: standard bank PO prep applies. Focus on data interpretation and arithmetic.
- Reasoning: high-level puzzles and seating arrangements dominate SEBI Phase 1.

Target: 65 percent aggregate in Phase 1.

### Phase 2: 1 to 2 months after Phase 1 result

- For General stream: revise your commerce and finance basics deeply. Companies Act 2013, SEBI Act, LODR Regulations, ICDR Regulations are the most cited in past papers.
- For Legal stream: focus on Constitution, Contract Act, Companies Act, Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, SEBI Act, and case law of the last 3 years.
- For IT stream: DBMS, Data Structures, and Networking are heavy. Do not neglect Web Technology.
- For Research stream: Statistics inference, Time Series, and Financial Econometrics are the scoring topics.

### Interview

- Deep knowledge of one specialist area is often more valuable than shallow coverage of many.
- Be honest about the reasons for your interest in a regulator role over a private-sector finance role. Interviewers ask this in almost every SEBI panel.
- Follow SEBI's recent orders, circulars, and consultation papers for 3 months before the interview.

## SEBI Grade A vs RBI Grade B: which one to target

Both are top central financial regulator postings. Choose based on stream fit and interest:

| Feature | SEBI Grade A | RBI Grade B |
|---|---|---|
| Location | Mumbai (headquarters) with pan-India offices | Mumbai + all Indian states (rotation) |
| Streams | General, Legal, IT, Research, Engineering, Rajbhasha | General, DEPR, DSIM |
| Application fee (General) | Rs. 1,000 | Rs. 850 |
| Phase 1 marks | 200 (5 sections, 60 mins) | 200 (4 sections, 120 mins) |
| Phase 2 marks | 300 (3 papers) | 300 (3 papers) |
| Interview weightage | 15 percent | 15 percent |
| Entry salary in-hand | Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.15 lakh | Rs. 1.15 to Rs. 1.25 lakh |
| Notification cycle | August | July to August |
| Vacancies (typical) | 100 to 200 | 250 to 400 |

Most serious candidates attempt both. Prep is 80 percent overlapping for the General stream. The differentiator is the Awareness of Securities Market section in SEBI Phase 1 and the Finance & Management paper in RBI Phase 2.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Applying in the wrong stream. Once submitted, stream cannot be changed. If you have an IT or Legal degree, apply through that stream (selection ratio is much better than General).
- Ignoring Securities Market awareness. This is a full 40-mark section in Phase 1 and is heavily weighted in Phase 2 for General stream. Do not treat it as add-on.
- Skipping the descriptive English paper prep. Many candidates score well in objective sections but underperform in Paper 1 of Phase 2, losing 20 to 30 marks that decide the final merit.
- Interview underprep. SEBI interviews are notoriously conceptual. Vague answers do not survive follow-up questions.
- Waiting for the "official" cutoff. SEBI does not release Phase 1 cutoffs officially. Target 130 out of 200 to be safe for General; 110 to 120 for reserved categories.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the SEBI Grade A 2026 notification date?**
The SEBI Grade A 2026 notification is expected in August 2026, with Phase 1 exam in October 2026. Confirm dates on sebi.gov.in when the notification is released. The last three cycles have followed similar timing.

**What is the age limit for SEBI Grade A 2026?**
The maximum age for General category candidates is 30 years as on the reference date in the notification. Age relaxations apply: 3 years for OBC NCL, 5 years for SC/ST, 10 years for PwBD, 5 additional years for ex-servicemen.

**Is a Chartered Accountant (CA) eligible for SEBI Grade A?**
Yes. CAs are eligible under the General stream as CA is treated as equivalent to a Bachelor's degree with 60 percent marks. Their subject knowledge in Finance, Companies Act, and Audit gives them an advantage in Phase 2.

**What is the salary of SEBI Grade A officer in 2026?**
Total monthly emoluments at entry level in Mumbai are approximately Rs. 1.35 to Rs. 1.45 lakh gross, with net in-hand of Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.15 lakh after NPS and tax deductions. Total annual CTC including all perks and allowances is approximately Rs. 20 to Rs. 24 lakh.

**How is the SEBI Grade A final merit calculated?**
Final merit is based on Phase 2 marks (85 percent weightage) plus Interview marks (15 percent weightage). Phase 1 is qualifying only and marks do not count in the final merit.

**Is there negative marking in SEBI Grade A Phase 1?**
Yes. One-fourth of the marks allotted for a correct answer are deducted for each wrong answer. Skipping a question you do not know costs less than a wrong guess.

**Which stream has the highest selection chance in SEBI Grade A?**
Niche streams (Legal, IT, Research) have selection ratios closer to 1:500, compared to about 1:2,000 for General. If your degree matches a niche stream, apply through it directly.

**Can I appear for both SEBI Grade A and RBI Grade B in the same cycle?**
Yes. Both notification and exam windows do not overlap. Most General stream candidates prepare for both since Phase 1 syllabi are about 80 percent common.

**Is SEBI Grade A better than IBPS PO or SBI PO?**
On pay, SEBI Grade A entry salary is about 2x IBPS PO in-hand. Career ceiling at Executive Director level is above the highest scale in commercial banking. On competition, SEBI Grade A is harder (selection ratio around 1:2,000 for General vs 1:200 to 1:400 for SBI PO), but the payoff scales accordingly.

**Where is the SEBI Grade A interview held?**
The interview is held at SEBI headquarters in Mumbai (Bandra Kurla Complex). Some cycles allow video conference interviews for outstation candidates. The interview is 30 to 45 minutes and involves 3 to 5 panel members.

## Sources

- Securities and Exchange Board of India official portal: [sebi.gov.in](https://www.sebi.gov.in)
- SEBI recruitment page: sebi.gov.in/careers.html (link goes live during the notification window)
- Reference for career progression and pay structure: SEBI Annual Report 2024

content:
## BSNL JTO 2026: the exam is BSNL's own, not GATE

BSNL is recruiting 100 Junior Telecom Officers in the Telecom stream from the open market, under a notification issued on 26 May 2026. The computer based test is on 23 August 2026, which is ten days away at the time of writing.

Applications ran from 4 June to 3 July 2026 and are closed.

One point needs settling immediately, because coverage of this recruitment is genuinely contradictory. Selection is through a computer based test conducted by BSNL. It is not through GATE, and it is not a merit-list exercise without an examination, both of which have been reported.

The confusion is understandable rather than careless. BSNL has recruited Junior Telecom Officers through different routes in different cycles: some through GATE scores, some through its own written or computer based examination. So a candidate reading material from an earlier cycle, or a site that has not updated, will find a genuinely different process described. For the 2026 Telecom stream recruitment, the CBT is the route.

If you applied, the CBT on 23 August is your live stage and the admit card is what to watch for on the BSNL portal.

## Key details

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Notification | 26 May 2026 |
| Vacancies | 100, Telecom stream, open market |
| Applications | 4 June to 3 July 2026, closed |
| Computer based test | 23 August 2026 |
| Selection stages | CBT, then Document Verification, then Medical Examination |
| Age | 20 to 30 years |
| Pay scale | IDA E-1, Rs 16,400 to Rs 40,500 |

Vacancies are distributed across BSNL's circles, so the posting you are competing for depends on the circle you applied against rather than a single national pool.

## Selection process

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| Computer Based Test | Decides merit |
| Document Verification | Eligibility check |
| Medical Examination | Fitness confirmation |

The CBT is the only stage that ranks you. Document verification and the medical are qualifying: they confirm you are who and what you claimed, and that you meet the fitness standard, but they do not add to your position.

That structure means the examination on 23 August determines the outcome, and the two stages after it are administrative gates rather than further competition.

## Eligibility

On education, the requirement is a bachelor's degree in Telecommunication, Electronics, Radio, Computer, Electrical, Information Technology or Instrumentation engineering, or an M.Sc in Electronics or Computer Science.

That is a reasonably wide list within the electronics and computing family, and it is worth checking your degree nomenclature against it precisely, since branch names vary between universities and document verification is where a mismatch surfaces.

On age, the band is 20 to 30 years, with relaxation of 5 years for SC and ST candidates, 3 years for OBC candidates and 10 years for candidates with disabilities.

## What a Junior Telecom Officer actually does

Worth setting out, because the title is opaque from outside the organisation.

A JTO is an executive-grade entry position in BSNL's technical cadre. The work covers the operation and maintenance of telecom infrastructure: exchanges and switching systems, transmission networks including optical fibre, broadband and internet services, mobile network elements, and increasingly the data centre and enterprise service side of the business.

In practice a JTO supervises technical teams, handles fault resolution and network uptime for an assigned area, manages installation and commissioning work, and deals with the planning and reporting that goes with running infrastructure. There is a substantial field component in most postings, particularly in the operations and maintenance roles.

Postings follow the circle structure, and BSNL operates across the country including in rural and remote areas where it is often the incumbent or only fixed-line and broadband provider. Transfer within a circle is normal, and inter-circle transfer is possible but not routine.

## Pay: why IDA is not the same as a government pay level

This is the part most worth understanding before joining, and it is where a comparison with a central government post goes wrong if done casually.

BSNL is a public sector undertaking, not a government department. Its employees are not civil servants on the 7th Pay Commission matrix. They are PSU employees on an Industrial Dearness Allowance pay scale.

The JTO post sits at IDA Pay Scale E-1, running from Rs 16,400 to Rs 40,500, with an annual increment of 3 per cent of basic pay. On top of basic pay come Industrial Dearness Allowance, house rent allowance, perks and medical benefits. Reported in-hand pay at entry falls in the region of Rs 45,000 to Rs 55,000 a month depending on allowances and posting.

Three differences from a government post matter.

The dearness allowance mechanism differs. IDA is revised quarterly on an industrial index, where the central government's DA for civil servants is revised half-yearly on a different basis. The two move differently, and over years the divergence is real.

Pay revision happens differently. Central government pay is revised through Pay Commissions applying across the service. PSU pay is revised through periodic wage negotiation and government approval specific to the enterprise, and it depends in part on the enterprise's financial position.

The E-1 designation marks this as executive grade. A JTO is an officer-level entrant rather than a clerical or technician-grade one, which is why the entry qualification is an engineering degree and why progression runs through executive grades.

## Career progression

| Grade | Post |
|---|---|
| E-1 | Junior Telecom Officer |
| E-2 | Sub Divisional Engineer (SDE) |
| E-3 and above | Divisional Engineer and higher executive grades |

Progression runs through BSNL's internal promotion process, based on service, performance and available vacancies in the higher grades, with departmental examinations applying at some stages.

A JTO who progresses through the executive grades can reach senior management within the organisation over a career, and the technical experience is also portable: telecom network experience transfers to private telecom operators, equipment vendors, network integrators and the enterprise connectivity market, where an ex-BSNL engineer with operations experience is a recognised profile.

## Something to weigh honestly before joining

Since this is a career decision rather than only an examination, one factual point belongs on the page.

BSNL is a public sector enterprise whose financial position has required government support, and revival packages have been extended to it. That is a matter of public record rather than speculation, and it is relevant context for anyone weighing a long career there against alternatives.

What it does not mean is that the job is not worth taking. BSNL remains a substantial national operator with a large network, a strategic role including in rural connectivity and government communications, and executive-grade employment with the benefits that carries. Government support has in practice been forthcoming.

What it does mean is that the decision deserves the same clear eyes as any other. A candidate comparing this against a central government post on the 7th CPC matrix, or against a private telecom role, should compare the pay mechanism, the revision process and the organisational position rather than only the headline in-hand figure. Those are different propositions, and which is better depends on what you want.

## Preparing for the 23 August CBT

With ten days left, the work is consolidation rather than fresh study.

The examination tests the technical stream at degree level alongside general components, so the bulk of the marks sit in your own engineering subjects. Concentrate revision there rather than on general aptitude, which carries less weight.

For the telecom and electronics core, revise communication systems, digital electronics, networks, signals and systems, microprocessors, electromagnetics and transmission, and the data communication and networking material, at the depth of an undergraduate degree rather than beyond it.

Work previous papers where available, since BSNL's question style in its own examinations is reasonably consistent across cycles and past papers tell you the level better than any syllabus description.

Practise under a clock. A computer based technical paper rewards pace, and candidates who have revised thoroughly but not practised at speed routinely leave questions unattempted.

Confirm the admit card details when it is released, particularly the centre and reporting time, and carry the printed admit card with the photo identity document matching your application.

## Circle-wise vacancies and why your choice matters

Because the 100 posts are distributed across BSNL's circles rather than pooled nationally, the circle you applied against is the field you compete in, and the practical consequences are larger than the number of posts suggests.

A circle with a handful of vacancies and many applicants produces a high cutoff. A circle with comparable vacancies and fewer applicants produces a lower one. With only 100 posts nationally, individual circles may carry very few vacancies each, which makes the variation between them pronounced rather than marginal.

The posting consequence is equally real. BSNL circles cover the whole country including the North East, the hill states and remote districts, and a JTO appointed to a circle will generally serve within it. Transfer within a circle is routine; moving between circles is possible but not something to assume.

So the circle choice made at application time is a decision about where you will live and work, not only about statistical odds. For candidates who applied on the basis of vacancy numbers alone without considering the posting geography, that is worth knowing before results rather than after an appointment letter arrives.

For a future cycle, weigh the two together: your realistic chance in a circle against your willingness to live there for years. A marginally better chance in a circle you would struggle to settle in is not a good trade.

## What happens after the CBT

Document verification follows for shortlisted candidates. Assemble the papers now rather than after the result: degree certificate and mark sheets, proof of date of birth, category certificate in the prescribed format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, PwD certificate where applicable, and identity documents matching the application.

The degree nomenclature check matters here specifically. Because eligibility is defined by a list of branches, a candidate whose degree is titled slightly differently from the listed branches should be ready to establish equivalence, ideally with supporting documentation from the university.

The medical examination confirms fitness for the post. Given the field component in operations roles, which can involve exchange sites, tower locations and cable routes, the standard is a working fitness standard rather than a nominal one, so it is worth a basic check with a doctor rather than assuming.

## What the CBT covers

Since the technical stream carries the bulk of the marks, it is worth setting out what that means in practice.

The paper draws on the undergraduate telecom and electronics curriculum. The areas that recur across BSNL's own examinations are communication systems covering analogue and digital modulation, sampling and multiplexing; digital electronics including logic families, combinational and sequential circuits and memory; signals and systems; networks and network theorems; electromagnetic theory and transmission lines; antennas and wave propagation; microprocessors and microcontrollers; control systems; and the data communication and computer networking material covering protocols, the OSI and TCP/IP models, switching and routing.

Telecom-specific material carries particular weight given the stream: exchange and switching systems, optical fibre communication, mobile and cellular systems, and broadband technologies.

Alongside the technical portion, expect general components covering general awareness, reasoning and quantitative aptitude at a modest level. These are worth attempting properly but not worth displacing technical revision, since the technical share dominates.

The depth expected is that of an undergraduate degree rather than a postgraduate one. A candidate who has retained their degree material and revises systematically is well placed; a candidate attempting to learn topics from scratch in the final days is not, which is why consolidation beats new study at this stage.

## BSNL JTO compared with other engineering government routes

An engineering graduate targeting government or public sector employment has several routes, and they differ in more than the employer.

| Route | Employer type | Pay basis | Selection |
|---|---|---|---|
| BSNL JTO | Public sector undertaking | IDA pay scale, E-1 executive grade | BSNL CBT |
| [RRB ALP](/sarkari-naukri/rrb-alp-2026) and Technician | Government department (Railways) | 7th CPC pay matrix | RRB CBT plus aptitude and medical |
| SSC Junior Engineer | Government department | 7th CPC pay matrix | SSC written examination |
| [UPSC Engineering Services](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-ese-2026) | Government, Group A | 7th CPC pay matrix, gazetted | Prelims, mains and interview |
| Other PSU recruitment | Public sector undertakings | IDA pay scales | Often GATE-based |

Two distinctions matter when comparing. Government departments pay on the 7th CPC matrix with DA revised half-yearly and revisions through Pay Commissions, whereas PSUs pay on IDA scales with quarterly DA revision and enterprise-specific wage settlements. And UPSC Engineering Services is a gazetted Group A entry, a materially different level from an E-1 PSU post or a Junior Engineer position.

Many PSU recruitments use GATE scores, which is worth knowing for an engineering graduate planning a year: a good GATE score opens a set of PSU applications simultaneously, whereas BSNL's own CBT in this cycle is specific to this recruitment. Sitting GATE remains sensible even for a candidate primarily targeting BSNL, since it widens the option set considerably.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is BSNL JTO 2026 recruitment through GATE?**
No. Selection for the 2026 Telecom stream recruitment is through a computer based test conducted by BSNL, on 23 August 2026, followed by document verification and a medical examination. The confusion arises because BSNL has used different routes in different cycles, including GATE scores in some years and its own examination in others, so material from an earlier cycle describes a genuinely different process.

The computer based test is on 23 August 2026. The notification was issued on 26 May 2026 and applications ran from 4 June to 3 July 2026, so the recruitment is now at the examination stage and the admit card is what to watch for on the BSNL portal.

100 posts in the Telecom stream, recruited from the open market and distributed across BSNL's circles. Because vacancies are circle-wise, the pool you compete against depends on the circle you applied for rather than being a single national list.

**What is the BSNL JTO selection process?**
Three stages: a computer based test, which is the only stage that decides merit; document verification, which checks eligibility; and a medical examination confirming fitness. The two stages after the CBT are qualifying gates rather than further competition, so the examination on 23 August determines the outcome.

A bachelor's degree in Telecommunication, Electronics, Radio, Computer, Electrical, Information Technology or Instrumentation engineering, or an M.Sc in Electronics or Computer Science. Since branch nomenclature varies between universities, check your degree title against the listed branches carefully, because a mismatch surfaces at document verification and may need equivalence established.

**What is the age limit for BSNL JTO 2026?**

**What is the BSNL JTO salary?**
The post is at IDA Pay Scale E-1, from Rs 16,400 to Rs 40,500, with an annual increment of 3 per cent of basic pay, plus Industrial Dearness Allowance, house rent allowance, perks and medical benefits. Reported in-hand pay at entry is around Rs 45,000 to Rs 55,000 a month depending on allowances and posting.

PSU pay revision also happens through periodic wage negotiation specific to the enterprise rather than through Pay Commissions applying across the service.

Yes. The E-1 designation places it in the executive grade, which is why the entry requirement is an engineering degree and why progression runs through executive grades: E-2 as Sub Divisional Engineer, then E-3 as Divisional Engineer and upward through the higher executive grades.

content:
## UPSC IES ISS 2026: Indian Economic Service and Indian Statistical Service recruitment

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) conducts the combined Indian Economic Service (IES) and Indian Statistical Service (ISS) examination once a year to recruit Grade A officers into two of India's most specialised civil services. The IES supplies economics-trained officers to ministries like Finance, Commerce, Planning, and NITI Aayog. The ISS supplies statistically trained officers to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and the Reserve Bank of India. The 2026 notification is expected in September 2026 with the written exam in June or July 2027. Total vacancies typically range from 30 to 60 across both services combined.

This is a niche exam. Fewer than 6,000 candidates appear for both services combined in a typical year. That is roughly the same size as a single UPSC CSE Mains cohort. Selection ratios are far better than UPSC CSE (about 1:150 for IES and 1:100 for ISS versus 1:800 for CSE), while the starting salary and posting quality match Grade A civil service standards.

## Important dates for UPSC IES ISS 2026

| Event | Date (expected) |
|---|---|
| Official notification | September 2026 |
| Registration opens | September 2026 |
| Last date to apply | October 2026 |
| Admit card release | May or June 2027 |
| Written examination | June or July 2027 |
| Written result | September 2027 |
| Personal interview | November or December 2027 |
| Final result | January or February 2028 |

Confirm every date against upsc.gov.in when the official notification is released. Dates above reflect the typical IES/ISS cycle timing from 2023, 2024, and 2025 recruitments.

## IES and ISS: what they are and where officers work

### Indian Economic Service (IES)

IES officers work as economists inside the central government. Typical postings and functions:

- Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs, Department of Expenditure, Department of Revenue)
- Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce, DPIIT)
- NITI Aayog (policy research and evaluation)
- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (economic analysis wing)
- Reserve Bank of India deputations (occasionally)
- Department of Public Enterprises
- Other ministries needing in-house economic analysis capacity

The role is analytical and advisory. IES officers write policy briefs, evaluate schemes, model economic outcomes, and support senior civil servants and ministers with economic reasoning behind decisions.

### Indian Statistical Service (ISS)

ISS officers work as statisticians across ministries that produce or consume large-scale data. Typical postings:

- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (National Statistical Office, Central Statistics Office)
- National Sample Survey Office
- Registrar General of India (Census Commissioner's office)
- Ministry of Agriculture (agricultural statistics)
- Ministry of Labour (labour bureau and employment statistics)
- Reserve Bank of India deputations
- International Statistical Institute affiliations

The role is technical and data-heavy. ISS officers design surveys, run statistical estimation for national aggregates (GDP, CPI, employment), and increasingly work on modern data-analytics workflows adopted by government departments.

## Vacancies for IES ISS 2026

Vacancy distribution varies by cycle. Using recent years as a reference:

| Year | IES vacancies | ISS vacancies | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 25 | 26 | 51 |
| 2024 | 22 | 26 | 48 |
| 2025 | 20 | 27 | 47 |

Expect 2026 vacancies to fall in the 40 to 60 range. Selection is category-wise as per government reservation rules: UR, EWS, OBC NCL, SC, ST, PwBD.

## Eligibility for UPSC IES ISS 2026

### Age

Age 21 to 30 years as on August 1 of the notification year (August 1, 2026 for the 2026 cycle). Age relaxation applies:

- OBC NCL: up to 33 years
- SC and ST: up to 35 years
- PwBD (UR): up to 40 years
- PwBD (OBC): up to 43 years
- PwBD (SC or ST): up to 45 years
- Ex-servicemen: 5 years additional per rules

### Education

Eligibility is service-specific. A candidate cannot apply for both services in the same year.

For **IES**, a Master's degree in Economics, Applied Economics, Business Economics, or Econometrics from a recognised university is required. Interdisciplinary economics degrees are accepted if the university officially classifies them as Economics degrees.

For **ISS**, a Bachelor's degree with Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, or Applied Statistics as one of the subjects, OR a Master's degree in Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, or Applied Statistics from a recognised university.

Candidates in the final year of qualifying degree can apply provisionally but must submit their degree certificate by the deadline in the notification.

### Nationality

Indian citizens, plus Nepalese and Bhutanese subjects, Tibetan refugees who came to India before January 1, 1962, and persons of Indian origin who migrated from certain listed countries with intent to settle in India. The last two categories need a Government of India eligibility certificate.

## Application fee for UPSC IES ISS 2026

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC, EWS (Male) | Rs. 200 |
| SC, ST, PwBD, Women (all categories) | Nil |

Payment is online via UPI, net banking, debit card, or credit card, or offline via SBI Bank Challan.

## How to apply for UPSC IES ISS 2026 step by step

Applications go through the UPSC One Time Registration (OTR) portal at upsconline.nic.in only.

1. Visit upsconline.nic.in and complete UPSC OTR if not already done. OTR is a one-time process; the same OTR ID works across all UPSC exams.
2. Log in to the OTR portal and open the IES/ISS 2026 examination form.
3. Choose the service (IES or ISS) and fill personal details, qualification details, and centre preferences.
4. Upload photograph, signature, and photo identification (as per size and format specifications in the notification).
5. Pay the fee online or via SBI Bank Challan.
6. Submit and download the confirmation page. Print two copies for records.

The withdrawal window opens for a few days after the last date. If you decide not to appear, use it to save the record.

## UPSC IES ISS 2026 exam pattern

The examination has two stages: a written examination worth 1000 marks and a personal interview worth 200 marks. Total is 1200 marks.

### Written examination (1000 marks, 6 papers over 3 days)

Two papers are common to both services. Four papers are service-specific.

Common papers:

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | General English | 100 | 3 hours |
| II | General Studies | 100 | 3 hours |

Service-specific papers for IES:

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| III | General Economics I | 200 | 3 hours |
| IV | General Economics II | 200 | 3 hours |
| V | General Economics III | 200 | 3 hours |
| VI | Indian Economics | 200 | 3 hours |

Service-specific papers for ISS:

| Paper | Subject | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| III | Statistics I (Objective) | 200 | 2 hours |
| IV | Statistics II (Objective) | 200 | 2 hours |
| V | Statistics III (Descriptive) | 200 | 3 hours |
| VI | Statistics IV (Descriptive) | 200 | 3 hours |

All descriptive papers are in English only. There is no compulsory Indian language paper.

### Personal interview (200 marks)

Candidates who clear the written cutoff are called for a personal interview at UPSC headquarters in Delhi (Dholpur House). The panel typically includes 4 to 5 members. Interview weightage is 200 out of 1200 total marks, roughly 16.7 percent.

Final merit is the sum of written and interview marks.

## Syllabus focus for IES and ISS

### IES syllabus focus areas (Papers III to VI)

Paper III (General Economics I): microeconomics (consumer theory, producer theory, market structures), macroeconomics (national income, IS-LM, monetary and fiscal policy), international trade theory, growth models.

Paper IV (General Economics II): public finance, environmental economics, welfare economics, development economics, monetary theory, banking and finance.

Paper V (General Economics III): quantitative methods (statistics, econometrics), Indian economic history from 1950, industrial economics, labour economics.

Paper VI (Indian Economics): Indian macroeconomic performance since 1991, structural reforms, agricultural policy, industrial policy, poverty and inequality, current five-year and multi-year economic strategies, budget analysis for the last 3 years.

### ISS syllabus focus areas (Papers III to VI)

Paper III (Statistics I, Objective): probability, distributions, statistical inference, hypothesis testing.

Paper IV (Statistics II, Objective): linear models, sampling, design of experiments, statistical computing basics.

Paper V (Statistics III, Descriptive): applied statistics including time series, index numbers, official statistics.

Paper VI (Statistics IV, Descriptive): choice of one specialisation from Operations Research, Econometrics, Sampling Techniques, Demography, Actuarial Statistics, or Statistical Computing.

## Salary and service structure for IES ISS 2026

IES and ISS officers are placed in the Junior Time Scale (Grade A) on joining:

| Component | Approximate value |
|---|---|
| Basic Pay (Level 10, 7th CPC) | Rs. 56,100 per month |
| Dearness Allowance (about 55% of basic) | Rs. 30,855 |
| House Rent Allowance | Rs. 15,000 to Rs. 27,000 (varies by city) |
| Transport Allowance | Rs. 3,600 to Rs. 7,200 |
| Other allowances | Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 5,000 |
| **Gross monthly (Delhi posting)** | **Rs. 1.05 lakh to Rs. 1.20 lakh** |

Net in-hand after NPS, tax, and other deductions is approximately Rs. 80,000 to Rs. 95,000 at Junior Time Scale.

Beyond salary, officers receive:

- Government accommodation in Delhi or the state of posting, at nominal licence fee
- Government vehicle for official duty at Senior Time Scale (Grade B) and above
- Full medical coverage under CGHS for self and family
- Leave Travel Concession every 2 years
- Contribution to NPS
- Study leave and deputation opportunities including international training

Total annual CTC at entry level is approximately Rs. 15 to Rs. 18 lakh including all monetary and non-monetary perks.

## Career progression in IES and ISS

Both services follow the standard central civil service progression:

Junior Time Scale (Grade A) then Senior Time Scale (Grade B), Junior Administrative Grade (Grade C), Selection Grade (Grade D), Senior Administrative Grade (Grade E), Higher Administrative Grade, and finally Apex Scale (Secretary in Government of India).

Typical timing: Junior to Senior Time Scale in 4 years, then approximately 4 to 6 years per subsequent scale. Officers who reach Higher Administrative Grade or Apex Scale can head departments like the National Statistical Office or serve as Chief Economic Adviser in ministries. Compensation at Apex Scale exceeds Rs. 2.5 lakh per month base plus perks.

## Preparation strategy for UPSC IES ISS 2026

### General English (Paper I)

Focus on essay writing, precis, and comprehension. This paper is qualifying-heavy in terms of impact on your ranking because most candidates score in a tight 45 to 55 range. Practice at least 2 essays and 3 precis per week for the last 3 months.

### General Studies (Paper II)

Overlaps significantly with UPSC CSE Prelims General Studies. Any standard CSE Prelims prep material (Manorama Yearbook, Laxmikanth Polity, Bipan Chandra History) is sufficient. Do not over-prepare this paper; focus your best hours on subject papers.

### IES subject papers (III to VI)

The four IES papers are the ranking decider. Standard reference books:

- Microeconomics: Varian, or Snyder and Nicholson
- Macroeconomics: Blanchard, or Mankiw
- Public Finance: Musgrave and Musgrave
- International Trade: Krugman and Obstfeld
- Development Economics: Todaro and Smith
- Indian Economics: Uma Kapila, or the Economic Survey of the last 3 years
- Econometrics: Gujarati

Solve 10 years of previous year papers. UPSC repeats question types and even specific concepts every 4 to 5 years in the IES syllabus.

### ISS subject papers (III to VI)

Statistics-focused prep, with the two objective papers (III, IV) closer in style to CSIR NET Statistics, and the two descriptive papers (V, VI) requiring problem-solving demonstrations.

- Probability and inference: Rohatgi and Saleh, or S.C. Gupta and V.K. Kapoor
- Linear models and sampling: Cochran, or Kish
- Applied statistics: Croxton, Cowden, and Klein
- For Paper VI specialisation: choose based on your comfort. Operations Research (Taha) and Econometrics (Gujarati) are the most-picked electives.

### Interview

The IES/ISS interview panel probes depth in your chosen service's core area far more than UPSC CSE panels do. Prepare for questions like "Explain the current stance of RBI's monetary policy" (IES) or "Design a sampling plan for measuring urban unemployment in Delhi" (ISS). Vague answers do not survive the follow-up.

## UPSC IES ISS vs UPSC CSE: which one to target

Both are Grade A civil service entries. Choose based on your academic strength, career interest, and competition tolerance.

| Feature | UPSC IES / ISS | UPSC CSE |
|---|---|---|
| Selection ratio | 1:100 to 1:150 | 1:800 to 1:1,000 |
| Vacancies (typical) | 40 to 60 combined | 1,000 to 1,100 |
| Written exam total | 1,000 marks | 1,750 marks |
| Number of papers | 6 | 9 (including 4 optional) |
| Interview weightage | ~17 percent | ~15 percent |
| Optional subject choice | Only for ISS Paper VI | Yes, 1 of 26 subjects |
| Qualification required | Master's in Economics or Statistics | Any bachelor's degree |
| Age limit (General) | 30 years | 32 years |
| Attempt limit (General) | 6 | 6 |
| Postings | Ministries and agencies dealing with economics or data | Full spectrum of IAS/IPS/IFS/IRS and 20+ services |
| Entry pay (Level 10) | Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.20 lakh gross | Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.20 lakh gross |
| Suitable if | Master's in Economics or Statistics; interest in analytical or research-heavy roles | Any degree; interest in field administration or policy leadership |

For candidates who already hold a Master's in Economics or Statistics from a strong programme, IES/ISS is often the higher-expected-value path because competition is lower and the ceiling is comparable at Apex Scale.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Attempting IES with only a Bachelor's in Economics. Eligibility for IES requires a Master's; a Bachelor's alone does not qualify.
- Underestimating Paper I (English). Candidates who score 60+ in English gain 5 to 10 ranks on the merit list versus the median.
- Skipping Indian Economics (Paper VI) preparation because it "should come naturally". This paper has the highest year-on-year change in content and needs the last 3 years' Economic Survey memorised.
- For ISS, choosing an unfamiliar Paper VI specialisation. Pick the elective you did in your Master's or one you have prepared for over 6 months.
- Treating the interview as a formality. IES/ISS panels test depth aggressively; a shallow subject knowledge shows quickly.

## Frequently asked questions

**When will the UPSC IES ISS 2026 notification be released?**
The 2026 notification is expected in September 2026, with the written exam in June or July 2027. Confirm dates on upsc.gov.in once the official notification is released.

**Is there negative marking in IES ISS papers?**
Yes, for the two ISS objective papers (Paper III and Paper IV). Descriptive papers do not have negative marking. Common English and General Studies papers do not have negative marking either.

**Can I appear for both IES and ISS in the same year?**
No. Candidates must choose one service (IES or ISS) at the time of application. Applying for both in the same cycle is not allowed.

**What is the salary of an IES or ISS officer at entry level?**
Junior Time Scale (Grade A) officers receive a gross monthly package of Rs. 1.05 to Rs. 1.20 lakh in Delhi, with net in-hand of Rs. 80,000 to Rs. 95,000 after NPS and tax. Total annual CTC including allowances and perks is Rs. 15 to Rs. 18 lakh.

**Can a Statistics graduate (Bachelor's) apply for ISS?**
Yes, provided your Bachelor's had Statistics, Mathematical Statistics, or Applied Statistics as one of the subjects. Master's in Statistics is not mandatory for ISS eligibility.

**Which is easier, IES or ISS?**
Neither is objectively easier. IES has slightly fewer applicants per vacancy (about 1:100 vs 1:150 for IES vs ISS ratios in recent years). Difficulty depends on your academic background. A candidate with a strong Statistics Master's finds ISS more approachable; a candidate with an Economics Master's finds IES more approachable.

**What is the attempt limit for UPSC IES ISS?**
6 attempts for General category, 9 for OBC NCL, unlimited for SC and ST candidates until the age limit is reached.

**How much time is needed to prepare for IES ISS from scratch?**
For a Master's holder in the relevant subject, 8 to 12 months of dedicated preparation is typical. For candidates fresh from a Bachelor's programme with Statistics coursework, 12 to 18 months is a realistic timeline.

**Is coaching necessary for UPSC IES ISS?**
No. The exam has a small candidate pool and most successful candidates prepare through self-study using standard subject textbooks and previous year papers. Coaching is available in Delhi for IES specifically and is useful for the Indian Economics paper if you are not already engaged with policy content.

**Can IES or ISS officers switch to IAS later?**
Yes, through the Combined Services Examination (CSE) if within the age limit. Some officers move via lateral entry to central-services deputations. Direct switching between services is rare and requires re-clearing UPSC CSE.

## Sources

- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation: [mospi.gov.in](https://www.mospi.gov.in)
