content:
## Indian Army Agniveer 2026: the honest picture

Indian Army Agniveer recruitment enrols young men and women into the Army for a four-year tenure under the Agnipath scheme. The single most important thing to understand, and the thing most other pages blur, is that this is a four-year engagement with a monthly Agnipath package and a Seva Nidhi payout, not a regular soldier's pay scale with dearness allowance and a pension. Getting this right changes how you should judge the offer.

Recruitment happens through the Army's central portal joinindianarmy.nic.in, in categories that run from Agniveer General Duty to Technical, Clerk, and Tradesman posts. For the 2026 cycle, around 25,000 or more vacancies have been reported across sites, with registration having opened in February 2026, but treat the exact 2026 vacancy count and dates as reported figures to confirm on the official portal, since the Army updates them per cycle. This guide is built on the confirmed Agnipath structure and the most recent cycle as a baseline, and it covers the categories, the physical standards, the exam, the package math in plain terms, and what actually happens after four years.

## Important dates for Army Agniveer 2026

| Event | Date (as reported, verify on the portal) |
|---|---|
| Registration opened | 13 February 2026 |
| Registration last date | Around 1 April 2026, reportedly extended to 10 April 2026 |
| Online Common Entrance Exam (CEE) | 1 to 15 June 2026 window (tentative) |
| Recruitment rally (physical and medical) | After the CEE result |

Because the Army revises these each cycle and the deadline was reportedly extended, confirm the current dates on joinindianarmy.nic.in rather than relying on a single figure.

## Agniveer categories

The Army recruits Agniveers in several categories, each with its own education requirement.

| Category | For candidates with |
|---|---|
| Agniveer General Duty (GD) | Class 10 |
| Agniveer Technical | Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, Maths, and English, or an ITI |
| Agniveer Clerk / Store Keeper Technical | Class 12 in any stream |
| Agniveer Tradesman (10th pass) | Class 10 |
| Agniveer Tradesman (8th pass) | Class 8 |

There are also specialist streams such as Sepoy Pharma, Technical Nursing Assistant, and Women Military Police, each with its own eligibility. The Women Military Police entry is the route through which women are recruited as Agniveers in the Army, so a woman candidate looking for an Agniveer post should watch for that specific category when a cycle opens, since it has its own vacancies and standards.

## Vacancy details

Around 25,000 or more Agniveer vacancies have been reported for the 2026 cycle across recruitment sites, distributed by category and region. The Army does not always publish a single fixed number in advance, and it recruits in large numbers each year, so treat the reported figure as indicative and check the official notification for the confirmed category-wise and region-wise split.

## Eligibility by category

The education requirement is the main gate, and it varies by category.

| Category | Education requirement |
|---|---|
| General Duty | Class 10 with at least 45 percent aggregate and 33 percent in each subject |
| Technical | Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry, Maths, and English, at least 50 percent aggregate and 40 percent in each subject, or a relevant ITI |
| Clerk / Store Keeper Technical | Class 12 in any stream with at least 60 percent aggregate and 50 percent in each subject |
| Tradesman (10th) | Class 10 with 33 percent in each subject |
| Tradesman (8th) | Class 8 with 33 percent in each subject |

## Age limit

The Agnipath scheme sets the age band at 17.5 to 21 years. For the 2026 cycle the birth-date window has been reported around 1 October 2005 to 1 April 2009, though sources vary slightly, so confirm it against the official notification. There is no age relaxation for any category under the scheme.

## Physical standards

Physical standards vary by region and category. As an indicative guide for General Duty, the requirements are below, and the exact chart is in the notification.

| Standard | Requirement (indicative) |
|---|---|
| Height (general) | 170 cm |
| Height (Garhwali, Kumaoni) | 163 cm |
| Height (North-East) | 160 cm |
| Height (Gorkhas) | 157 cm |
| Chest | 77 cm unexpanded, with 5 cm expansion |
| Weight | Proportionate to height and age |

Clerk and Store Keeper Technical posts have a slightly lower height requirement. Confirm the figures for your region and category on the official chart.

## Physical Fitness Test marking

The Physical Fitness Test at the rally carries marks for the run and the beam, and it includes qualifying events.

The 1.6 km run is a 60-mark event: finishing in up to 5 minutes 30 seconds scores the full 60 marks, and 5 minutes 31 seconds to 5 minutes 45 seconds scores 48 marks. Beyond 5 minutes 45 seconds a candidate is disqualified.

The pull-ups on the beam are a 40-mark event: 10 pull-ups score 40 marks, 9 score 33, 8 score 27, 7 score 21, and 6 score 16. A minimum of 6 pull-ups is needed to qualify.

The 9-foot ditch jump and the zig-zag balance are qualifying, pass or fail, and carry no marks. So the run and the beam together decide the physical score, while the ditch and balance simply have to be cleared. Because these events reward months of training rather than last-minute effort, candidates who clear the written exam should already be running and building upper-body strength well before the rally, since a strong exam score is wasted if the run or the beam falls short on the day.

## Application fee

The application fee for Army Agniveer has been reported at around Rs 250 for the candidate, with part of the cost borne by the Army. Payment is online through the recruitment portal. Confirm the exact fee in the notification, since it is set per cycle.

## Selection process

The selection sequence changed in 2023, and the current order puts the written exam first, which many older pages still get wrong.

1. Online Common Entrance Exam (CEE): a computer-based test, held first.
2. Recruitment Rally: candidates shortlisted from the CEE are called for the Physical Fitness Test, which is the run, beam, ditch, and balance, plus the Physical Measurement Test for height, chest, and weight, and then the medical examination.
3. Document verification, the merit list, and enrolment.

So you sit the online exam first, and only shortlisted candidates go to the rally for the physical and medical stages. This is the opposite of the pre-2023 order, where the physical came first.

## CEE exam pattern

The Common Entrance Exam is a one-hour computer-based test, and its structure varies by category, with a penalty of 0.5 marks for each wrong answer in the main categories.

| Category | Questions | Marks | Subjects |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Duty | 50 | 100 | General Knowledge, General Science, Maths, Reasoning |
| Technical | 50 | 200 | General Knowledge, Physics, Maths, Chemistry |
| Clerk / SKT | 50 | 200 | General Knowledge, General Science, Maths, Computer, English |
| Tradesman (10th) | 30 | 90 | General Knowledge, General Science, Maths |
| Tradesman (8th) | 20 | 60 | General Knowledge, General Science |

Some sources list the General Duty paper as 45 questions for 90 marks, so confirm the exact count in the notification. Clerk and Store Keeper Technical candidates must clear a minimum mark in the English section specifically.

## Syllabus

General Knowledge covers current affairs, history, geography, and general awareness. General Science covers physics, chemistry, and biology at the school level. Maths covers arithmetic, algebra, and geometry to the level of the category's education requirement. The Technical paper goes deeper into Physics, Chemistry, and Maths, and the Clerk paper carries a substantial English section. The overall standard matches the education level of each category, so General Duty stays around Class 10 and Technical around Class 12.

## The Agnipath package and Seva Nidhi

This is the section to read carefully, because it is where the Agniveer offer differs most from a regular soldier's pay, and where other pages mislead by calling it a salary.

An Agniveer receives a monthly Agnipath package, not a pay scale with dearness allowance. Of that package, the Agniveer takes home about 70 percent, and about 30 percent goes into a Seva Nidhi corpus, which the government matches with an equal contribution.

| Year | Monthly package | Seva Nidhi (self, ~30%) | In-hand (~70%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rs 30,000 | Rs 9,000 | Rs 21,000 |
| 2 | Rs 33,000 | Rs 9,900 | Rs 23,100 |
| 3 | Rs 36,500 | Rs 10,950 | Rs 25,550 |
| 4 | Rs 40,000 | Rs 12,000 | Rs 28,000 |

Over the four years, the Agniveer's own contributions total about Rs 5.02 lakh, and the government's matching contribution adds another Rs 5.02 lakh, so the Seva Nidhi holds about Rs 10.04 lakh in contributions. With the interest that accrues, the payout at the end of four years is commonly cited at about Rs 11.71 lakh. So the honest way to state it is: about Rs 10.04 lakh in contributions, and about Rs 11.71 lakh including interest. This Seva Nidhi payout is fully exempt from income tax under the applicable provision.

On top of the package, every Agniveer gets a non-contributory life insurance cover of Rs 48 lakh for the four-year term. In the case of death attributable to service, the family receives an additional ex-gratia along with the insurance, the Seva Nidhi, and the pay for the unserved period, and disability is compensated by percentage. There is no pension and no gratuity for the Agniveers who are not retained.

## What happens after four years

This is the question that worries most candidates, and it deserves a clear answer. At the end of the four-year tenure, up to 25 percent of each batch is retained into the regular Army cadre, based on merit, medical fitness, and the organisation's need, and their subsequent service counts as a fresh regular engagement with the normal pay and pension. The remaining roughly 75 percent leave the service. Those who leave take with them the tax-free Seva Nidhi payout of about Rs 11.71 lakh, a skill certificate recognising the training and experience they gained, and, under various government and state schemes, priority or age relaxation in recruitment to central armed police forces and state police. So the four years are not a dead end for those who exit, but they are also not a guaranteed permanent career, and a candidate should weigh the offer with that reality in mind.

## Agniveer versus a regular soldier

To make the difference concrete, here is how an Agniveer compares with a regular soldier under the older terms.

| Factor | Agniveer | Regular soldier (older terms) |
|---|---|---|
| Tenure | 4 years | Full service career |
| Pay | Agnipath package | Regular pay scale with DA |
| Pension | None (unless retained) | Yes |
| Exit benefit | Seva Nidhi about Rs 11.71 lakh, tax-free | Pension and gratuity |
| Insurance | Rs 48 lakh for the term | Service insurance |
| Permanency | 25 percent retained | Permanent |

The Agniveer route offers a shorter, defined engagement with a lump-sum exit benefit and a path to a regular career for a quarter of each batch. A candidate who wants the certainty of a full career and a pension should understand that only retention offers that under the current scheme.

## A preparation plan for Army Agniveer

Preparation runs on two tracks that both matter, because the exam and the physical each filter candidates. For the written CEE, study the subjects of your category to the level of its education requirement, using previous years' papers to build speed under the one-hour limit and to get used to the 0.5 negative marking. For the physical, train for the run and the beam well in advance, since the 1.6 km run in 5 minutes 30 seconds and 10 pull-ups are what score the marks, and fitness of that level takes months to build, not weeks. Because the exam now comes first and only shortlisted candidates reach the rally, clearing the CEE with a strong score is the immediate priority, but a candidate who neglects the physical loses the seat they earned on paper. Balancing both from the start is what carries a candidate through to enrolment.

## Army Agniveer or Navy Agniveer

The Agnipath scheme runs across all three services, and candidates often ask whether to try the Army or the [Navy Agniveer](/sarkari-naukri/indian-navy-agniveer-2026) route. The package, the four-year tenure, the Seva Nidhi, and the 25 percent retention are the same across services, so the money and the structure do not differ. What differs is the nature of the service and the entry requirements. The Army recruits the largest numbers and across the widest range of categories, from General Duty to Tradesman, and its work is land-based across regiments and units. The Navy recruits fewer, mainly through the Senior Secondary Recruit and Matric Recruit entries, and its service is sea and shore based, with trades like Chef and Steward alongside the general entry. A candidate open to either can apply to both when the cycles are live, since the eligibility overlaps for many, and the choice then comes down to the kind of service life they want.

## Common misconceptions to clear

A few beliefs about Agniveer recruitment are worth correcting. The first is that the monthly package is a take-home salary; in fact about 30 percent goes to the Seva Nidhi, so the in-hand is around 70 percent. The second is that the physical test comes first; since 2023 the online exam comes first, and only shortlisted candidates reach the rally. The third is that every Agniveer becomes a permanent soldier; only up to 25 percent are retained. The fourth is that leaving after four years means leaving empty-handed; in fact the exiting Agniveer carries a tax-free Seva Nidhi of about Rs 11.71 lakh, a skill certificate, and preference in several other recruitments. Clearing these four up front lets a candidate judge the offer accurately.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the rally.

1. Your Class 8, 10, or 12 certificate and mark sheets, as your category requires, and an ITI certificate for the Technical trade route.
2. A domicile or residence certificate, which also supports any regional height relaxation.
3. A category certificate where applicable.
4. A recent photograph, signature, and a valid photo ID matching your application.
5. Character and other certificates as listed in the notification.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Agniveer a permanent job?**
No. Agniveer is a four-year tenure under the Agnipath scheme. At the end of four years, up to 25 percent of each batch is retained into the regular Army cadre based on merit, medical fitness, and organisational need, while the remaining roughly 75 percent leave with the Seva Nidhi payout and a skill certificate.

**What is the in-hand salary of an Army Agniveer?**
An Agniveer takes home about Rs 21,000 a month in the first year, rising to about Rs 28,000 in the fourth year. This is roughly 70 percent of the Agnipath package, since about 30 percent goes into the Seva Nidhi corpus. It is a package, not a pay scale with dearness allowance.

**How much Seva Nidhi does an Agniveer get after 4 years?**
The Seva Nidhi holds about Rs 10.04 lakh in contributions, made up of the Agniveer's roughly Rs 5.02 lakh and an equal government match. With accrued interest, the payout at the end of four years is commonly cited at about Rs 11.71 lakh, and it is exempt from income tax.

**Do Army Agniveers get a pension?**
No. Agniveers who are not retained after four years do not receive a pension or gratuity. They receive the tax-free Seva Nidhi payout of about Rs 11.71 lakh, a skill certificate, and priority or age relaxation in some other recruitments. Only the roughly 25 percent retained into the regular cadre earn pension over a full career.

**What is the age limit for Army Agniveer 2026?**
The Agnipath scheme sets the age band at 17.5 to 21 years, with no relaxation for any category. For the 2026 cycle the birth-date window has been reported around 1 October 2005 to 1 April 2009, so confirm it against the official notification.

**What is the running time for Army Agniveer?**
The 1.6 km run is a 60-mark event. Finishing in up to 5 minutes 30 seconds scores the full 60 marks, and 5 minutes 31 seconds to 5 minutes 45 seconds scores 48 marks. Beyond 5 minutes 45 seconds a candidate is disqualified.

**How many pull-ups are needed for Army Agniveer?**
A minimum of 6 pull-ups on the beam is needed to qualify, scoring 16 marks. The marks rise with the count: 10 pull-ups score the full 40 marks, 9 score 33, 8 score 27, and 7 score 21.

**Is there negative marking in the Agniveer CEE?**
Yes. The Common Entrance Exam deducts 0.5 marks for each wrong answer in the main categories. The exam now comes first in the selection sequence, and only shortlisted candidates are called to the recruitment rally for the physical and medical stages.

**What happens after 4 years as an Agniveer?**
About 75 percent of each batch leaves after four years with the tax-free Seva Nidhi payout of around Rs 11.71 lakh, a skill certificate, and priority in some other recruitments. Up to 25 percent are retained into the regular Army cadre with normal pay and a pension over a full career.

content:
## NDA & NA 2026 at a glance

The UPSC National Defence Academy and Naval Academy Examination, NDA & NA, is the main route into the armed forces straight after Class 12, leading to a commission as an officer in the Army, Navy, or Air Force. UPSC conducts it twice a year, as NDA I and NDA II. As of late July 2026, NDA I 2026 is a completed cycle and NDA II 2026 is the live one: it was notified on 20 May 2026, and its written exam is scheduled for 13 September 2026, for 394 vacancies.

Two things make this exam stand out. It is one of the few officer entries open right after Class 12, at an age of 16.5 to 19.5, and, since a Supreme Court ruling, it is open to women across all wings. This guide covers the two cycles, the women-eligibility position clearly, the written exam and the five-day SSB interview, and the honest difference between the stipend during training and the pay after commissioning.

Here is where the live cycle stands: NDA II 2026 applications closed in June 2026, and the written exam is on 13 September 2026, followed by the SSB interview for those who qualify. NDA I 2027 would be the next fresh cycle after this. So this page is a full guide to the exam and the path to a commission, with NDA I 2026 as a baseline reference.

## Important dates for NDA & NA 2026

| Event | NDA II 2026 (live) | NDA I 2026 (baseline) |
|---|---|---|
| Notification | 20 May 2026 | 10 December 2025 |
| Written exam | 13 September 2026 | 12 April 2026 |
| Course | NDA 158th and 120th Naval Academy Course | NDA 157th and 119th Naval Academy Course |

## Vacancy details

NDA II 2026 has 394 vacancies, of which 370 are for male candidates and 24 for female candidates. The commonly reported service-wise split is Army 208, Air Force 120, Navy 42, and Naval Academy 24, though the exact split is set in the notification, so confirm it there. The Naval Academy figure is the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme intake.

## Women in the NDA

This is a point competitors often state flatly or bury, so it is worth explaining clearly. Following a Supreme Court order in 2021, unmarried women became eligible for the NDA, and the first women cadets were admitted from the 2022 intake. Women are now eligible across all wings, that is the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy, subject to the same age, education, and medical standards, with the physical standards set to female norms. In NDA II 2026, 24 of the 394 seats are earmarked for women. So a woman candidate who has passed or is appearing in Class 12, meets the age band, and satisfies the wing-specific subject requirement can sit the NDA exactly as a male candidate does.

## Eligibility for NDA & NA 2026

On age, you must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years, and unmarried. The exact birth-date window is set for each cycle in the notification, and there is no age relaxation for any category.

On education, you need to have passed or be appearing in Class 12. The subject requirement depends on the wing. For the Army wing, any stream is accepted, so Arts and Commerce candidates qualify. For the Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings, Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, that is the PCM combination, is mandatory. This distinction matters and many pages leave it vague: a candidate without PCM can still join the Army wing but not the Navy or Air Force.

On marital status, you must be unmarried, and you must remain unmarried until you complete training.

## Physical and medical standards

Candidates must meet the physical and medical standards for a cadet, which are set out in the notification. The minimum height is around 157 cm for the Army and Navy and higher for the Air Force, with relaxations for candidates from Gorkha, North-Eastern, Garhwal, and Kumaon regions. Vision standards are stricter for the Air Force, where spectacles are not permitted for the flying branch, and procedures like LASIK or radial keratotomy are disqualifying. Candidates should read the medical standards carefully before applying, since a medical disqualification later is a hard setback.

## Selection process

NDA selection has two stages that together carry 1800 marks.

1. Written examination: 900 marks. This shortlists candidates for the SSB.
2. Services Selection Board (SSB) interview: 900 marks, a five-day assessment.

The final merit is built from the written exam and the SSB together, so both carry equal weight, and a candidate must clear the SSB, not just the written exam, to be selected.

## Written exam pattern

The written exam has two papers on the same day, both objective and bilingual, with different negative marking.

| Paper | Content | Questions | Marks | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | Mathematics | 120 | 300 | 2.5 hours |
| Paper 2 | General Ability Test (GAT) | 150 | 600 | 2.5 hours |

The General Ability Test is split into English for 200 marks and General Knowledge for 400 marks. Each question carries 2.5 marks. The negative marking differs by paper: Mathematics deducts about 0.83 marks per wrong answer, and the General Ability Test deducts about 1.33 marks per wrong answer. So a wrong guess in the GAT is costlier than in Maths, which shapes attempt strategy.

## Syllabus

Mathematics covers algebra, matrices and determinants, trigonometry, analytical geometry in two and three dimensions, differential and integral calculus, differential equations, vector algebra, and statistics and probability, with trigonometry, algebra, and calculus forming the bulk. The General Ability Test covers English grammar, vocabulary, and comprehension, and General Knowledge across Physics, Chemistry, General Science, History, Geography, and current affairs. The standard is broadly that of Class 11 and 12, drawing largely on the NCERT textbooks.

## The five-day SSB interview

The SSB interview is where many written-qualified candidates fall, because it tests officer-like qualities rather than knowledge, and it runs over five days.

Day one is screening, with an officer intelligence rating test and a picture perception and discussion test, after which some candidates are sent home. Day two is the psychology round, with a thematic apperception test, a word association test, a situation reaction test, and a self-description. Days three and four are the group testing officer tasks, including group discussions, group planning, progressive group tasks, and command tasks, alongside the personal interview. Day five is the conference, where the board takes its final call. The SSB assesses qualities like reasoning, decision-making, initiative, and the ability to work in and lead a group, so preparation for it is different from exam study and rewards mock SSBs and self-awareness.

## What the NDA cutoff has actually been

UPSC publishes the cutoff marks after each cycle closes, and the numbers move a lot from year to year, which is why a single "expected cutoff" figure from a coaching site is worth very little. These are the official UPSC cutoffs for recent NDA I cycles.

| Cycle | Written cutoff (out of 900) | Final cutoff (out of 1800) |
|---|---|---|
| NDA I 2025 | 334 | 699 |
| NDA I 2024 | 291 | 654 |
| NDA I 2023 | 301 | 664 |
| NDA I 2022 | 360 | 720 |
| NDA I 2021 | 343 | 709 |
| NDA I 2020 | 355 | 723 |

Two things stand out from that table. The written cutoff has swung between 291 and 360 marks in six cycles, a spread of 69 marks, which tracks paper difficulty rather than any trend you can plan around. And the gap between the written cutoff and the final cutoff sits at roughly 360 to 370 marks in every year, which tells you what the SSB adds: a candidate who scrapes through the written exam still needs a solid SSB performance to make the final list.

Alongside the aggregate cutoff, UPSC applies a minimum qualifying standard of 25 per cent in each subject. A candidate who clears the aggregate but falls below 25 per cent in Mathematics or in the General Ability Test is not evaluated further, so lopsided preparation that abandons one paper does not work here.

A practical target: aim for 400 or more in the written exam rather than the 300 to 350 band. That builds a cushion against a hard paper and against an average SSB day.

## Stipend during training versus pay after commissioning

This is where honesty matters, because other pages blur a cadet's training stipend with an officer's salary. During the roughly three years at the NDA and the further year at the service academy, cadets do not draw a full officer salary; their food, accommodation, uniforms, and medical care are provided, and a stipend applies in the final pre-commission training year, commonly cited at around Rs 56,100 a month. That figure is the pre-commission stipend, not a multi-year salary.

On being commissioned as a Lieutenant or the equivalent, an officer enters Pay Level 10 with a basic pay of Rs 56,100, plus Military Service Pay of Rs 15,500 and dearness allowance, which brings the in-hand to roughly Rs 1,00,000 to Rs 1,25,000 a month, alongside subsidised housing, rations, and other service benefits. The pay then grows through the officer ranks over a career. So the accurate picture is a modest stipend during training and a strong officer package after commissioning, not a large salary from day one.

## What happens after selection: the training path

Selection into the NDA starts a four-year training path, not a posting. Cadets from all three services train together for three years at the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla near Pune, then move to their service academy for about a year of specialised training.

| Wing | Service academy after NDA | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Army | Indian Military Academy (IMA) | Dehradun |
| Navy | Indian Naval Academy (INA) | Ezhimala |
| Air Force | Air Force Academy (AFA) | Dundigal, Hyderabad |

During the three years at Khadakwasla, cadets also read for a bachelor's degree affiliated to Jawaharlal Nehru University, in one of BA, BSc, or BSc Computer Science, and the degree is awarded at the passing out parade. So a cadet who completes NDA training leaves with a recognised graduate degree as well as a military commission, which matters if a career ever moves outside the services.

Candidates who take the Naval Academy route through the 10+2 Cadet Entry Scheme go directly to INA Ezhimala rather than through Khadakwasla, and read for a BTech there.

The commission comes at the end of the service academy year, not at the end of the NDA years. That is the point at which the stipend becomes an officer's pay.

## Career progression after commissioning

An officer commissioned through the NDA enters as a Lieutenant in the Army, or a Sub Lieutenant in the Navy and a Flying Officer in the Air Force, and moves up through defined pay levels under the 7th Pay Commission. Military Service Pay of Rs 15,500 a month applies at every one of these ranks, on top of basic pay and dearness allowance.

| Army rank | Navy equivalent | Air Force equivalent | Pay level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lieutenant | Sub Lieutenant | Flying Officer | Level 10 |
| Captain | Lieutenant | Flight Lieutenant | Level 10B |
| Major | Lieutenant Commander | Squadron Leader | Level 11 |
| Lieutenant Colonel | Commander | Wing Commander | Level 12A |
| Colonel | Captain | Group Captain | Level 13 |
| Brigadier | Commodore | Air Commodore | Level 13A |
| Major General | Rear Admiral | Air Vice Marshal | Level 14 |

Promotion to Captain and Major is time-bound, at roughly two and six years of service, so an NDA entrant reaches Major in their late twenties. Above Lieutenant Colonel, promotion turns selective and depends on vacancies, annual reports, and courses. Beyond pay, the package includes subsidised accommodation, ration entitlements, medical cover for the officer and dependants under ECHS after retirement, group insurance, and a pension, which is the part of the deal that separates a permanent commission from the four-year Agniveer route covered on our [Indian Army Agniveer](/sarkari-naukri/indian-army-agniveer-2026) page.

## NDA versus CDS versus CAPF

Candidates aiming at an officer career often weigh NDA against the [UPSC CDS](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-cds-ii-2026) route after graduation and the [CAPF Assistant Commandant](/sarkari-naukri/upsc-capf-ac-2026) route into the paramilitary. This comparison sets out the difference.

| Factor | NDA | CDS | CAPF AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry after | Class 12 | Graduation | Graduation |
| Age | 16.5 to 19.5 | About 19 to 25 | 20 to 25 |
| Force | Army, Navy, Air Force | Army, Navy, Air Force | Central armed police forces |
| Women eligible | Yes, all wings | Yes, via specified entries | Yes |
| Selection | Written plus SSB | Written plus SSB | Written plus physical plus interview |

NDA is the earliest officer entry, straight after Class 12. CDS is the graduate route into the armed forces. CAPF AC leads into the paramilitary forces. A candidate who is still in Class 12 and set on the armed forces should target NDA, while graduates would look at CDS or CAPF AC.

## A preparation plan for NDA

NDA rewards a steady build across Maths and the General Ability Test alongside SSB readiness. For Maths, revise the Class 11 and 12 syllabus thoroughly, since trigonometry, algebra, and calculus dominate, and practise under the negative-marking scheme. For the GAT, build English through reading and grammar practice, and General Knowledge through NCERT science and social science plus a daily current-affairs habit, keeping in mind the heavier negative marking that punishes loose guessing. Just as important, prepare for the SSB in parallel, since it carries half the marks and cannot be crammed; mock interviews, group tasks, and honest self-reflection build the officer-like qualities the board looks for. The candidates who convert NDA are those who treated the SSB as seriously as the written exam.

## Books and resources for NDA preparation

The syllabus sits at Class 11 and 12 level, so the NCERT textbooks do most of the work and specialised NDA books fill the gaps in practice and pattern.

| Section | What to use |
|---|---|
| Mathematics | NCERT Class 11 and 12 Maths, then Pathfinder for NDA and NA (Arihant) or R S Aggarwal for practice |
| English | Objective General English by S P Bakshi, plus daily newspaper reading for comprehension |
| General Knowledge | NCERT Science and Social Science for Classes 9 to 12, Lucent's General Knowledge for revision |
| Current affairs | A monthly current affairs compilation, or a daily newspaper habit over 6 to 8 months |
| Previous papers | UPSC NDA question papers of the last 8 to 10 cycles, available free on upsc.gov.in |
| SSB | Let Us Crack SSB Interview, plus mock SSB sessions if you can access them |

Previous years' papers do more than any single book. UPSC repeats question types heavily in the General Ability Test, and working through 8 to 10 past papers under timed conditions teaches the negative-marking calculus better than reading about it.

## Mistakes that cost NDA candidates

A few errors show up cycle after cycle, and every one of them is avoidable.

1. Applying for the wrong wing. A candidate without Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics who marks Navy or Air Force preferences is rejected at document verification, after months of preparation.
2. Ignoring the medical standards until the end. Vision requirements for the flying branch disqualify a large number of otherwise strong candidates, and refractive surgery like LASIK is disqualifying for the Air Force. Read the medical standards before you apply, not after you clear the written exam.
3. Guessing freely in the General Ability Test. At about 1.33 marks deducted per wrong answer against 2.5 for a correct one, loose guessing across 30 uncertain questions can cost more than it gains.
4. Treating the SSB as an afterthought. It carries 900 of the 1800 marks, and the gap between the written and final cutoffs shows exactly how much it decides.
5. Missing the age window. The 16.5 to 19.5 band is narrow and has no relaxation for any category, so a candidate typically gets only two or three attempts in total.
6. Letting one paper slide. The 25 per cent per-subject minimum means a strong Maths score cannot rescue a weak General Ability Test.

## How to apply for NDA

Applications go through the UPSC online portal, and the process is the same in every cycle.

1. Complete the One Time Registration on upsconline.nic.in if you have not already. This is a separate step from the application itself and is reused across UPSC exams.
2. Open the NDA and NA application when the notification goes live and fill in personal, educational, and communication details exactly as they appear on your Class 10 certificate.
3. Choose your wing preferences in order, keeping the PCM requirement in mind for Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy.
4. Pick your exam centre. Centres fill on a first-apply basis, so applying early gives you a better chance of a nearby centre.
5. Upload your photograph and signature in the specified format, along with a photo ID.
6. Pay the fee of Rs 100. Women candidates and SC and ST candidates pay nothing.
7. Submit, then save the PDF and the registration number. UPSC opens a short correction window after the deadline for limited edits.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the SSB.

1. Your Class 10 and Class 12 certificates and mark sheets, with the wing-specific subjects.
2. Proof of date of birth, usually your Class 10 certificate.
3. A recent photograph, signature, and a valid photo ID matching your application.
4. Documents for any regional height relaxation and other certificates as listed in the notification.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can girls apply for NDA in 2026?**
Yes. Following a Supreme Court order in 2021, unmarried women are eligible for the NDA across all wings, that is the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy, with the first women cadets admitted from the 2022 intake. In NDA II 2026, 24 of the 394 seats are earmarked for women.

**What is the NDA 2026 exam date?**
The NDA II 2026 written exam is scheduled for 13 September 2026. The earlier NDA I 2026 written exam was held on 12 April 2026. UPSC conducts the NDA and NA examination twice a year, as NDA I and NDA II.

**Is PCM compulsory for NDA?**
It depends on the wing. Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics are mandatory for the Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings. The Army wing accepts any stream, so an Arts or Commerce candidate can join the Army wing without PCM but not the Navy or Air Force.

**What is the age limit for NDA 2026?**
Candidates must be between 16.5 and 19.5 years and unmarried, with the exact birth-date window set for each cycle in the notification. There is no age relaxation for any category.

**Do NDA cadets get a salary during training?**
Not a full salary. Cadets get free food, accommodation, uniforms, and medical care during training, and a stipend of around Rs 56,100 a month applies in the final pre-commission training year. A full officer package, with basic pay, Military Service Pay, and allowances, begins only on commissioning.

**What is the total marks of the NDA exam?**
The NDA selection carries 1800 marks in total: the written exam is 900 marks (Mathematics 300 plus General Ability Test 600), and the SSB interview is 900 marks. The final merit is built from both together.

**Is there negative marking in NDA?**
Yes. The Mathematics paper deducts about 0.83 marks for each wrong answer, and the General Ability Test deducts about 1.33 marks per wrong answer. Because the GAT penalty is heavier, blind guessing there is costlier than in Maths.

**Can I join NDA after 12th with Arts or Commerce?**
Yes, but only the Army wing. The Army wing accepts any stream, so Arts and Commerce candidates qualify. The Navy, Air Force, and Naval Academy wings require Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

**What is the difference between NDA and CDS?**
NDA is the officer entry straight after Class 12, at 16.5 to 19.5 years, while CDS is the graduate route into the armed forces at about 19 to 25 years. Both use a written exam plus the SSB interview, but NDA is the earlier entry and CDS is for graduates.

content:
## LIC AAO 2026-27: complete guide

If you want a high-paying, permanent central government job with one of the most iconic organisations in India, LIC AAO deserves to be near the top of your list. The Life Insurance Corporation of India recruits Assistant Administrative Officers every year or two, and the pay is genuinely outstanding: **Rs. 1.26 lakh per month gross** in metro cities at joining, with Rs. 1.07 lakh in-hand after deductions. For a graduate-level government job, that is hard to beat.

The last cycle (32nd Batch) had **841 vacancies** across Generalist, Specialist, and Assistant Engineer streams. Selection ratio was roughly 1 in 500 for Generalist and 1 in 150 to 1 in 200 for niche Specialist streams (CA, CS, Actuarial, Legal), which makes Specialist posts the highest-probability path if you have the qualification.

The **LIC AAO 2026-27 notification is expected in August to September 2026**, based on the pattern of the 32nd Batch which was announced on August 16, 2025. Watch [licindia.in](https://licindia.in) Careers page.

---

## What does an LIC AAO do day to day?

An AAO (Assistant Administrative Officer) is a Grade II officer at LIC. It is the entry-level officer position at India's largest insurance company, which is also a central public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Finance.

Depending on your specialisation and posting, you could be working in policy administration and underwriting, claims settlement, customer service at a branch office, accounts and finance, legal matters (for Legal specialists), or actuarial functions (for Actuarial specialists).

After successfully completing your one-year probation, you become an Administrative Officer (AO). From there, the promotion path moves upward to Assistant Divisional Manager, Divisional Manager, Senior Divisional Manager, Zonal Manager, Executive Director, and eventually Managing Director.

LIC's officer cadre is smaller than public sector banking (LIC has roughly 12,000 officers across all grades versus SBI's 90,000-plus), which means promotions are competitive but also more visible. Officers with Actuarial or CA qualifications typically reach senior management faster than pure Generalist entrants.

---

## Vacancy history and 2026-27 expected split

| Cycle | Year | Total | Generalist | Insurance Specialist | CA / CS / Legal / Actuarial | Assistant Engineer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 31st Batch | 2019 | 590 | 350 | 150 | 40 | 50 |
| 32nd Batch | 2023 | 300 | 150 | 100 | 30 | 20 |
| 32nd Batch (extended) | 2025 | **841** | 350 | 310 | 100 | 81 |
| **33rd Batch (expected)** | **2026-27** | **~800 to 900** | **~350** | **~300** | **~100** | **~80** |

LIC does not run AAO recruitment annually. Cycles are triggered when cadre vacancies build up to justify a fresh batch. The 2025 cycle was the largest in over a decade, which suggests the 2026-27 cycle may be closer to the 2019 volume (roughly 500 to 700) if it follows the historical pattern.

The **Generalist stream is where 40% of vacancies sit** and where most graduates without specialised qualifications compete. Insurance Specialist requires an Associate or Fellow membership of Insurance Institute of India (III) which many candidates do not have, making it a relatively narrow competition pool despite the 300+ vacancy count.

---

## Post streams and eligibility

### AAO Generalist

Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university. No minimum percentage. Age: 21 to 30 years.

This is the default entry route for most candidates. Arts, Science, Commerce, and Engineering candidates are all eligible without any additional professional qualification.

### AAO Insurance Specialist

Bachelor's degree plus Associate or Fellow of Insurance Institute of India (AIII or FIII). Age: 21 to 32 years.

The Insurance Specialist post has a mandatory 5-year posting at a mofussil (rural or semi-urban) branch after joining. This is a firm requirement, not a preference. Candidates who prefer metro postings should apply for Generalist instead.

### AAO Chartered Accountant (CA)

Bachelor's degree plus ICAI membership as a Chartered Accountant. Age: 21 to 32 years.

CA-qualified AAOs are typically posted at Divisional Offices, Zonal Offices, or Central Office in Mumbai, handling audit, investment accounts, tax matters, and financial reporting. Career progression to Divisional Manager (Finance) is faster than Generalist by 2 to 3 years.

### AAO Company Secretary (CS)

Bachelor's degree plus ICSI membership as a Company Secretary. Age: 21 to 32 years.

CS-qualified AAOs handle board compliance, secretarial matters, regulatory filings with IRDAI, and corporate governance. Postings are almost exclusively at Central Office and Zonal Offices.

### AAO Legal

LLB degree plus minimum 2 years of enrolment with the Bar Council of India. Age: 21 to 32 years.

Legal AAOs handle claim disputes, litigation, contract vetting, policy holder complaints, and IRDAI regulatory matters. Postings at Regional Offices and larger Divisional Offices.

### AAO Actuarial

Bachelor's degree plus specified papers cleared from the Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI). Minimum requirement is Core Technical and 2 Core Applications papers. Age: 21 to 32 years.

Actuarial is the highest-paid and fastest-promoting stream inside LIC. LIC's actuarial department in Mumbai handles product pricing, reserves valuation, mortality studies, and IRDAI regulatory submissions. Progression to Chief Actuary role in 15 to 20 years is standard for consistent performers.

### Assistant Engineer (Civil / Electrical)

B.Tech or B.E. in Civil or Electrical Engineering plus 3 years of relevant work experience. Age: 21 to 30 years.

Assistant Engineers handle LIC's building projects (LIC owns 300+ office buildings and 12,000+ staff quarters across India), maintenance, and infrastructure procurement. Postings at Regional Offices and property-heavy Divisional Offices.

### Age relaxation

Standard relaxation applies: SC / ST 5 years, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years, PwBD (General) 10 years, PwBD (OBC) 13 years, PwBD (SC/ST) 15 years, and existing confirmed LIC employees get 5 additional years over their applicable category limit.

---

## Important dates (expected 2026-27 based on 2025 cycle)

| Event | Expected date |
|---|---|
| Notification release | August 2026 |
| Application opens | August 2026 |
| Last date to apply | September 2026 |
| Prelims admit card | Early October 2026 |
| Prelims exam | October 2026 |
| Prelims result | November 2026 |
| Mains admit card | November 2026 |
| Mains exam | November to December 2026 |
| Mains result | January 2027 |
| Interview | February to March 2027 |
| Final result | April 2027 |
| Pre-recruitment medical | May 2027 |
| Joining | June to July 2027 |

All dates are expected based on LIC's previous cycle (32nd Batch, 2025). Official dates are published only on licindia.in. Do not rely on third-party exam portals for confirmed dates.

---

## Application fee

Rs. 700 plus applicable GST for General, OBC, and EWS candidates. Nil for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates. Fee is paid online through the IBPS-managed portal via UPI, net banking, or debit / credit card. No offline mode is accepted.

---

## How to apply: step-by-step

1. **Watch [licindia.in](https://licindia.in) Careers page from August 2026.** LIC does not send notification alerts. The link goes live on the day of the notification release.
2. **Click the official recruitment link.** You will be redirected to the IBPS-managed application portal at [ibpsonline.ibps.in](https://ibpsonline.ibps.in). LIC does not run its own recruitment portal for AAO.
3. **Register with a valid email ID and mobile number.** Both are verified via OTP. Save the registration credentials because the same login is used for admit card download, result check, and interview call letter.
4. **Fill in personal, educational, and work details.** For Specialist posts, upload your professional qualification certificate (CA membership, ICSI membership, Bar Council enrolment, IAI papers cleared, or B.Tech mark sheet plus 3-year work experience letter).
5. **Upload photo and signature.** Photo: passport-size, JPEG, under 200 KB, white background. Signature: black ink on white paper, JPEG, under 50 KB. Signature is verified again during document verification at interview stage.
6. **Pay the fee online** via UPI, net banking, or debit / credit card. Fee is Rs. 700 plus GST for General / OBC / EWS. SC / ST / PwBD candidates skip this step.
7. **Download and save the fee payment receipt and application confirmation.** Keep a printed copy along with the application form.
8. **Download admit card** from ibpsonline.ibps.in approximately 10 days before Prelims. Same portal is used for Mains admit card and interview call letter.

Never apply through any third-party link or website. Only use the link provided on the official licindia.in Careers page.

---

## Selection process: 4 stages

### Stage 1: Preliminary Examination (qualifying only)

A 60-minute online test with 100 questions. This is purely a screening test. Prelims marks play **no role** in the final merit list. You only need to clear the sectional and overall cutoffs to reach Mains.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reasoning Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 minutes |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 35 | 35 | 20 minutes |
| English Language | 30 | 30 | 20 minutes |
| **Total** | **100** | **100** | **60 minutes** |

Negative marking is 0.25 marks per wrong answer. Sectional cutoffs typically fall between 8 to 12 marks out of 30 to 35, and overall cutoff falls between 55 to 65 out of 100 depending on category and cycle difficulty.

### Stage 2: Main Examination (the real merit test)

The Mains is what determines your rank. It has two components conducted on the same day.

**Objective Paper: 300 marks, 120 minutes**

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reasoning and Numerical Ability | 30 | 90 | 40 minutes |
| General Knowledge and Current Affairs | 30 | 60 | 20 minutes |
| Insurance and Financial Market Awareness | 30 | 60 | 20 minutes |
| English Language with Comprehension | 30 | 90 | 40 minutes |
| **Total** | **120** | **300** | **120 minutes** |

Negative marking is 0.25 marks per wrong answer. Insurance and Financial Market Awareness is the section that separates strong candidates from average ones because most SSC or bank aspirants have never studied insurance formally.

**Descriptive Paper: 25 marks, 30 minutes**

Essay writing and letter writing in English. You need to score at least the qualifying marks (typically 8 to 10 out of 25 based on category) to be considered for the interview shortlist. This paper is evaluated separately from the objective paper.

### Stage 3: Personal Interview

Candidates who qualify Mains are called for a personal interview at LIC Zonal Offices. Interview panel typically has 3 to 5 LIC senior officers plus one external subject expert.

Final merit is calculated as: Mains objective (300) + Mains descriptive (25) + Interview (60) = 385 marks total. Prelims marks are not counted.

The interview covers your understanding of insurance, current affairs, basic finance, your qualification-relevant subject (CA for CA candidates, actuarial concepts for Actuarial candidates), and your suitability for LIC's culture. Communication in English is expected but not to a UPSC standard.

### Stage 4: Pre-recruitment medical examination

Before you get your appointment letter, LIC conducts a standard medical fitness examination at an empanelled hospital. This is mandatory and cannot be skipped. Vision, hearing, blood pressure, chest X-ray, and general fitness are checked. Colour blindness disqualifies candidates from certain Assistant Engineer posts but not from Generalist or Specialist streams.

---

## Salary: the biggest reason to target this exam

This is genuinely one of the best pay packages in the central government sector for a graduate-level exam.

| Pay component | Amount |
|---|---|
| Basic pay at joining | Rs. 88,635 per month |
| Pay scale | Rs. 88,635 to Rs. 1,69,025 |
| Dearness Allowance (currently ~46%) | Rs. 40,772 per month |
| House Rent Allowance (metro Tier A) | Rs. 8,864 per month (10% of basic) |
| City Compensatory Allowance | Rs. 900 per month |
| Transport Allowance | Rs. 3,600 per month |
| Special Allowance | Rs. 6,000 per month |
| Gross monthly (metro) | Rs. 1,26,000 to Rs. 1,32,000 |
| Deductions (PF, Insurance, Tax) | Rs. 18,000 to Rs. 25,000 |
| **Net in-hand (metro, after deductions)** | **Rs. 1,07,000 per month approximately** |

The gross figure includes Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance (varies by city tier: 10% for metro Tier A, 8% for Tier B, 6% for Tier C), City Compensatory Allowance, and transport allowance. Metro cities like Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad get the highest HRA slab.

To put the salary in context: an IAS officer starts at Rs. 56,100 basic pay. An LIC AAO starts at Rs. 88,635 basic. RBI Grade B starts at Rs. 55,200 basic (though RBI has higher DA-linked components). SEBI Grade A starts at Rs. 44,500 basic. LIC AAO is the highest starting basic pay of any graduate-level central government exam.

**Additional benefits:**

Pension is a defined benefit scheme (not NPS) for LIC employees, subject to service length. Gratuity is paid on retirement or resignation after 5 years. Medical coverage extends to self, spouse, and dependent parents with cashless treatment at empanelled hospitals. Leave Travel Concession (LTC) covers family travel every 4 years to anywhere in India. Staff home loan is available at concessional interest rates (typically 3 to 5 percentage points below market). Group insurance scheme covers Rs. 20 lakh life insurance during service. Performance-linked incentives can add 5 to 15% to annual gross depending on branch or department performance.

---

## Bond and service commitment

LIC has a mandatory service bond that every selected candidate must sign before joining.

Minimum service period is 4 years from the date of joining (including probation). Penalty for leaving before 4 years is Rs. 5,00,000 (five lakh rupees) plus applicable GST. The penalty is recoverable from the candidate or, in their absence, their legal heirs.

This is a firm commitment. If you are simultaneously preparing for UPSC, CAT, or other exams, factor this in before accepting the LIC AAO offer. Many CA-qualified AAOs later face this issue when they clear UPSC in year 2 or 3 of service.

---

## Career progression inside LIC

| Grade | Level | Typical years to reach | Approx basic pay |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assistant Administrative Officer (AAO) | Grade II | Entry (Year 1) | Rs. 88,635 |
| Administrative Officer (AO) | Grade III | 4 to 6 years | Rs. 1,05,000 |
| Assistant Divisional Manager (ADM) | Grade IV | 8 to 12 years | Rs. 1,25,000 |
| Divisional Manager (DM) | Grade V | 15 to 20 years | Rs. 1,45,000 |
| Senior Divisional Manager (SDM) | Grade VI | 20 to 25 years | Rs. 1,65,000 |
| Zonal Manager (ZM) | Grade VII | 25 to 30 years | Rs. 1,95,000 |
| Executive Director | Above Board | 28 to 32 years (rare) | Rs. 2,25,000+ |

Promotion beyond Divisional Manager requires clearing departmental promotion exams plus vacancy availability. Actuarial and CA-qualified officers typically reach ADM by year 8 to 10 due to the specialised cadre policy.

---

## Preparation strategy: 4 to 6 months

The LIC AAO exam is a 2-stage speed-plus-accuracy test with an Insurance Awareness twist that most bank PO aspirants underprepare for. The right prep sequence is Prelims-first (60 days), then Mains-focused (60 to 90 days), then Interview prep after Mains result (30 days).

### Prelims prep (60 days)

Reasoning Ability: Puzzles and seating arrangements are the highest-weight topic (roughly 15 to 20 marks out of 35). Solve 3 to 5 puzzles daily from books like R.S. Aggarwal Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning or M.K. Pandey Analytical Reasoning.

Quantitative Aptitude: Number series, Data Interpretation, and Arithmetic word problems dominate (roughly 20 to 25 marks out of 35). Books: R.S. Aggarwal Quantitative Aptitude or Arun Sharma How to Prepare for Quantitative Aptitude for CAT.

English Language: Reading comprehension, cloze test, and para jumbles dominate (roughly 15 to 20 marks out of 30). Books: Objective English by Hari Mohan Prasad or Wren and Martin High School English Grammar.

### Mains-specific prep (60 to 90 days after Prelims)

The Insurance and Financial Market Awareness section is unique to LIC AAO. This is where most candidates lose 20 to 30 marks that they cannot afford to lose. Focus areas:

- IRDAI regulations and role of the regulator
- Types of life insurance: term, endowment, ULIP, money-back, whole life
- LIC's flagship plans: Jeevan Labh, Jeevan Anand, Jeevan Umang, New Endowment Plan
- Insurance terminology: premium, sum assured, surrender value, bonus, maturity value, claim, nominee
- Government insurance schemes: PMJJBY, PMSBY, Ayushman Bharat
- Basic financial market awareness: stock market basics, mutual funds, RBI role and functions, inflation, monetary policy tools, banking regulation

Recommended books: Life Insurance Corporation of India by Nishit K. Sinha, Insurance Awareness by Ranjeet Kumar, or IC-33 study material from Insurance Institute of India.

General Knowledge and Current Affairs (Mains): Last 6 months of national and international news, government policies, RBI and IRDAI circulars, sports, awards, and important appointments. Sources: Yojana magazine, Manorama Yearbook 2026, Vision IAS current affairs monthly, and daily newspaper habit (The Hindu or Indian Express).

Descriptive paper (Mains): Practice writing one essay of 250 words and one formal letter of 150 words per day for the last month. Topics rotate around current affairs, insurance policy debates, and financial inclusion themes.

### Interview prep (30 days after Mains result)

Read LIC's annual report (available at licindia.in), study the latest IRDAI annual report, be able to explain 5 LIC flagship plans by heart with premium and benefit structure, prepare for questions on your bachelor's degree subject, and rehearse the 60-second personal introduction covering education, work experience, and reason for choosing LIC.

---

## LIC AAO vs SBI PO vs UPSC EPFO vs SEBI Grade A

| Parameter | LIC AAO | SBI PO | UPSC EPFO | SEBI Grade A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Notification cycle | Every 2 to 3 years | Annual | Annual (irregular) | Annual |
| Vacancies per cycle | 500 to 900 | 2,000 to 2,500 | 500 to 600 | 100 to 150 |
| Prelims + Mains + Interview | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Descriptive paper | Yes (Mains 25 marks) | Yes (Mains 50 marks) | No | Yes (Mains Paper 3) |
| Basic pay at joining | Rs. 88,635 | Rs. 48,480 | Rs. 47,600 | Rs. 44,500 |
| Gross monthly (metro) | Rs. 1,26,000 | Rs. 70,000 to 85,000 | Rs. 90,000 | Rs. 1,25,000 |
| Selection ratio | 1 in 500 Generalist | 1 in 500 | 1 in 950 | 1 in 2,000 |
| Service bond | 4 years, Rs. 5 lakh penalty | None | None | None |
| Age limit | 21 to 30 Generalist | 20 to 30 | 21 to 30 | 21 to 30 |
| Best for | Insurance and finance graduates wanting highest starting pay | Banking career growth | Labour law and pension specialisation | Capital markets and financial regulation |

LIC AAO has the highest basic pay but the smallest cadre (fewer promotion slots than SBI PO). UPSC EPFO has weaker starting pay but no bond and free access to CAPF and state police reservation trails. SEBI Grade A has the toughest selection ratio and requires 3 to 6 months of specialised capital markets prep on top of general banking-style Prelims and Mains.

---

## Common mistakes candidates make

1. **Applying under the wrong stream.** Insurance Specialist requires AIII or FIII membership, which many candidates confuse with "insurance awareness". If you do not have Insurance Institute of India certification, you are not eligible for Specialist. Apply Generalist.
2. **Underestimating the Insurance Awareness section in Mains.** Most bank PO aspirants scale to LIC AAO thinking their existing prep is sufficient. The Insurance section carries 60 marks and costs ranks; dedicated 4-week prep is mandatory.
3. **Ignoring the descriptive paper.** Failing the descriptive qualifying floor (typically 8 to 10 out of 25) drops you from the entire merit list regardless of objective marks. Practice at least 15 essays and 15 letters before Mains.
4. **Signing the 4-year bond without reading it.** The Rs. 5 lakh penalty is enforceable. Candidates who quit LIC in year 2 or 3 to join UPSC, CAT, or private sector have had the penalty recovered through salary certificates from the new employer.
5. **Not preparing for the mofussil posting condition for Insurance Specialists.** A 5-year mofussil posting is mandatory for Insurance Specialists. This is confirmed at appointment; candidates who accept and then request transfer within the 5-year window are denied.
6. **Assuming Prelims marks count.** Prelims is qualifying only. Some candidates over-invest in Prelims and neglect Mains prep, resulting in Prelims-cleared but Mains-poor performance.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**When will LIC AAO 2026-27 notification be released?**
The LIC AAO 2026-27 notification is expected in August to September 2026, based on the historical pattern of LIC's 32nd Batch which was released on August 16, 2025. The official notification is published only on licindia.in Careers page. Do not rely on third-party exam portals for confirmed dates. Applications typically remain open for 30 days from the notification date.

**What is the salary of LIC AAO in 2026?**
LIC AAO basic pay is Rs. 88,635 per month at joining. Gross monthly salary in metro cities including Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, City Compensatory Allowance, and transport allowance is approximately Rs. 1,26,000. Net in-hand after PF, tax, and insurance deductions is approximately Rs. 1,07,000 per month. This is the highest starting basic pay among all graduate-level central government recruitment exams.

**What is the age limit for LIC AAO 2026?**
Age limit is 21 to 30 years for Generalist and Assistant Engineer posts, and 21 to 32 years for all Specialist posts (CA, CS, Legal, Actuarial, Insurance Specialist). Age is calculated as on the date of the official notification. Standard age relaxation applies: SC/ST 5 years, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years, PwBD General 10 years.

**Is LIC AAO harder than SBI PO?**
LIC AAO is harder than SBI PO because of the additional Insurance and Financial Market Awareness section in Mains (60 marks), the descriptive paper qualifying floor, and the smaller vacancy pool leading to higher cutoffs. Prelims difficulty is roughly comparable to SBI PO Prelims. Selection ratio for LIC AAO Generalist is approximately 1 in 500 versus SBI PO's 1 in 500. Overall, expect 20 to 30% more prep time for LIC AAO than SBI PO.

**How many vacancies are expected in LIC AAO 2026-27?**
Approximately 800 to 900 total vacancies are expected across all streams, similar to the 2025 cycle (32nd Batch which had 841 vacancies). Expected split: 350 Generalist, 300 Insurance Specialist, 100 combined CA/CS/Legal/Actuarial, and 80 Assistant Engineer. Official numbers will be confirmed with the notification release.

**What is the bond for LIC AAO?**
LIC has a mandatory 4-year service bond starting from the date of joining (including probation). Penalty for leaving before 4 years is Rs. 5,00,000 plus applicable GST. The penalty is recoverable from the candidate or their legal heirs. Candidates simultaneously preparing for UPSC, CAT, or other exams should factor this before accepting the LIC AAO offer.

**Is the Insurance Awareness section really necessary?**
Yes. The Insurance and Financial Market Awareness section carries 60 out of 300 marks in the Mains objective paper. Candidates who score below 25 in this section rarely make the merit cutoff, regardless of how strong they are in Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, or English. Dedicated 4-week prep with IRDAI regulations, LIC flagship plans, and insurance terminology is mandatory.

**Can I apply for both LIC AAO Generalist and Specialist?**
No, you can apply for only one stream per cycle. If you have a CA, CS, or Legal qualification and meet the Specialist eligibility, applying for Specialist is strategically better because Specialist streams have selection ratios of 1 in 150 to 1 in 200 compared to Generalist's 1 in 500. However, Specialists face specific posting conditions (5-year mofussil for Insurance Specialist, Central Office postings for CS).

**What is the training period for LIC AAO?**
Selected candidates undergo a 4-week induction training programme at LIC's Management Development Centre in Mumbai, followed by 6 months of on-the-job training at the initially posted branch. Total probation is 1 year, extendable up to 2 years based on performance. Confirmation after successful probation makes you a permanent LIC employee.

**How is the final merit list prepared for LIC AAO?**
Final merit is calculated using Mains marks (325 total: 300 objective + 25 descriptive) plus Interview marks (60). Total merit ceiling is 385 marks. Prelims marks are qualifying only and do not count toward final rank. Candidates who fail either the descriptive qualifying floor or the interview cutoff are eliminated regardless of Mains objective performance.
