content:
## SSC JE 2026 status: what is confirmed and what is not

The SSC JE 2026 notification has not been released as of 27 July 2026. SSC Junior Engineer recruits Group B non-gazetted engineers in Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical streams for central government departments like CPWD and the Military Engineer Services. If you are searching for a firm 2026 date or vacancy count, treat every number you see on coaching pages as an estimate, because they contradict each other and none traces to an SSC notification yet.

Here is the honest position. The SSC Exam Calendar 2026-27 was released on 08 January 2026 and places the SSC JE notification later in 2026, but the exact application dates and the 2026 vacancy count are still open. This page is built on the confirmed SSC JE 2024 cycle as a working baseline, and every 2026-specific figure is flagged as expected rather than final. When the official notification drops, the numbers here will be updated.

For context, the SSC JE 2024 cycle notified 1,731 posts across the three engineering disciplines. Some pages project 3,000 or more posts for 2026, but that is unverified marketing, so plan against the 1,731 baseline until SSC says otherwise.

## Expected timeline for SSC JE 2026

| Event | Status |
|---|---|
| SSC Exam Calendar 2026-27 released | 08 January 2026 (confirmed) |
| Notification release | Expected later in 2026 (tentative, per the SSC calendar) |
| Application window | To be announced with the notification |
| Paper 1 (CBT) | Tentative, later 2026 |
| Paper 2 (CBT) | After Paper 1 result |

Do not fill in a hard date from a coaching page. SSC publishes the real schedule only in the notification PDF on ssc.gov.in, and that is the single source to trust.

## Vacancy details (2024 baseline)

The 2024 cycle spread 1,731 posts across three disciplines. SSC JE has no Quantity Surveying and Contract discipline in recent cycles, so the live streams are Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical only.

| Discipline | 2024 baseline vacancies |
|---|---|
| Civil | Largest share |
| Electrical | Moderate share |
| Mechanical | Moderate share |
| Total (2024) | 1,731 |

The department-wise split shifts every cycle with user demand, so read the 2026 breakup from the official notification when it appears rather than assuming the 2024 distribution repeats exactly.

## Participating departments

SSC JE fills posts across roughly nine central organisations, and the mix of disciplines differs by department.

| Department | Disciplines recruited |
|---|---|
| Central Public Works Department (CPWD) | Civil, Electrical |
| Central Water Commission (CWC) | Civil, Mechanical |
| Military Engineer Services (MES) | Civil, Electrical, Mechanical |
| Border Roads Organisation (BRO) | Civil, Electrical, Mechanical |
| Farakka Barrage Project | Civil, Electrical |
| Brahmaputra Board | Civil |
| National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) | Civil |
| Central Water and Power Research Station | Electrical |
| Directorate of Quality Assurance (Naval) | Mechanical, Electrical |

## Eligibility: where a diploma is enough

This is the part candidates most often get wrong. The qualification bar genuinely varies by department, and a three-year diploma is enough for several posts.

| Department | Minimum qualification |
|---|---|
| CPWD (Civil, Electrical) | Diploma in the relevant engineering discipline |
| CWC (Civil) | Three-year diploma in Civil Engineering |
| CWC (Mechanical) | Degree or diploma in Mechanical Engineering |
| MES | Degree, or three-year diploma plus 2 years' experience |
| BRO | Degree, or three-year diploma plus 2 years' experience |

The rule to remember is simple. A three-year diploma is enough for several posts, notably in CPWD and CWC Civil. Some posts, especially in BRO and MES, need either a degree or a diploma backed by two years of relevant experience. Read the department column of the notification against your own qualification before you apply.

## Age limit and relaxation

Most SSC JE posts set an upper age of 30 years, while some CPWD posts allow up to 32 years. The exact limit is post-specific and printed in the notification. Standard relaxation applies: 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, 10 years for PwBD, and 3 years for ex-servicemen over and above the upper limit.

## Application fee

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC | Rs 100 |
| SC, ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen | Nil |
| All women candidates | Nil |

Payment is online through BHIM UPI, net banking, or a card.

## Selection process

SSC JE selection runs through two computer based papers followed by verification stages.

1. Paper 1 (CBT): objective, common to all candidates.
2. Paper 2 (CBT): a single-discipline technical paper.
3. Document verification.
4. Medical examination.

The final merit is built from the combined Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks. There is no interview.

## Paper 1 exam pattern

Paper 1 is a 200-mark objective test of two hours, with a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 50 | 50 |
| General Awareness | 50 | 50 |
| General Engineering (Civil or Electrical or Mechanical) | 100 | 100 |
| Total | 200 | 200 |

You attempt the General Engineering section only in the discipline you applied for, so a Civil applicant answers Civil questions and never sees the Electrical or Mechanical sets. Paper 1 is the screening stage that decides who moves on to the technical Paper 2, and it is common to both the degree and diploma holders who apply.

## Paper 2 exam pattern

Paper 2 is a 300-mark discipline paper of two hours, and it now runs in computer based mode. Watch the negative marking here.

| Feature | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total marks | 300 |
| Discipline | Civil and Structural, or Electrical, or Mechanical |
| Duration | 2 hours |
| Negative marking | 1 mark per wrong answer |

That negative-marking gap matters. Paper 1 penalises a quarter mark per error, but Paper 2 penalises a full mark, so blind guessing in the technical paper is far more costly. Many candidates who clear Paper 1 comfortably lose ground in Paper 2 by over-attempting.

## Syllabus

General Intelligence and Reasoning covers analogies, similarities and differences, space visualisation, problem solving, decision making, visual memory, relationship concepts, and arithmetical reasoning. General Awareness covers current events, India and its neighbours, history, culture, geography, the economic scene, general polity, and scientific research. The General Engineering section, and Paper 2, follow the standard diploma-and-degree syllabus for the chosen discipline: for Civil this spans building materials, estimating and costing, surveying, soil mechanics, hydraulics, irrigation, transportation and environmental engineering, theory of structures, concrete technology, and RCC and steel design; for Electrical it spans basic concepts, circuit and magnetic circuit law, AC fundamentals, measurement, electrical machines, generation, transmission and distribution, and basic electronics; for Mechanical it spans theory of machines, strength of materials, thermodynamics, IC engines, fluid mechanics, boilers, air compressors, and refrigeration and air-conditioning.

## SSC JE 2026 salary

SSC JE posts sit at Pay Level 6 of the 7th Pay Commission, with a basic pay of Rs 35,400 and a scale of Rs 35,400 to Rs 1,12,400. With dearness allowance at 60 percent of basic pay effective 1 January 2026, per the Finance Ministry order, the in-hand pay works out well above the basic.

Take a worked example in a metro (X-class city). On a basic of Rs 35,400, dearness allowance at 60 percent adds Rs 21,240, house rent allowance at the metro rate of 27 percent adds about Rs 9,558, and transport allowance with DA adds roughly Rs 5,400. That is a gross near Rs 71,600, and after the National Pension System contribution and other deductions the in-hand lands close to Rs 62,000 a month. In a Y-class city the HRA drops to about 18 percent and the in-hand settles a little lower. Many competitor pages still show a stale 17 to 50 percent DA, which undercounts the real figure.

## SSC JE 2024 cut-off (reference)

Cut-offs vary by discipline, and Electrical and Mechanical usually close higher than Civil. As a reference from the SSC JE 2024 Paper 1 result, the unreserved cut-off sat near 122.93 for Civil and near 132.07 for Electrical and Mechanical.

| Category | Civil (2024) | Electrical / Mechanical (2024) |
|---|---|---|
| Unreserved | about 122.93 | about 132.07 |
| OBC | about 116.82 | slightly below UR |
| EWS | about 109.20 | varies |
| SC | about 101.85 | varies |
| ST | about 97.83 | varies |

Treat these as a planning band for 2026 and read the exact figures from the SSC JE 2026 result when it is published.

## SSC JE compared with state JE recruitments

Beyond the railways, many candidates also weigh SSC JE against state public works and irrigation JE posts run by state boards and PSCs. The trade-offs are real. SSC JE gives an all-India Group B posting across central departments, which can mean transfers far from home but a wider promotion field. State JE posts, run by bodies like the state PWD or subordinate service commissions, usually keep you within one state and its language zone, which suits candidates who want to stay close to home. Pay is broadly similar at Level 6 in most states, but the exam cycles are less predictable, and the number of posts swings sharply from year to year. If mobility does not bother you and you want an annual, well-defined exam, SSC JE is the steadier target. If staying in your home state matters more than a national posting, a state JE recruitment may fit better.

## Why the diploma-versus-degree detail matters so much

Most confusion around SSC JE comes down to one question: can I apply with only a diploma? The honest answer is that it depends on the department, and getting this wrong wastes an attempt. A large share of SSC JE posts, especially in CPWD and the Central Water Commission's Civil wing, accept a three-year diploma with no degree required. That makes SSC JE one of the most valuable central government routes open to diploma holders, since comparable engineer posts elsewhere often demand a full degree. The catch is the field-heavy departments. BRO and several MES posts want either a degree or a diploma backed by two years of relevant work experience, because the roles carry more site responsibility. So before applying, match your exact qualification and experience against the department column of the notification, post by post, rather than assuming one blanket rule covers the whole recruitment.

## SSC JE vs RRB JE

Candidates eligible for SSC JE often weigh it against the Railway RRB JE. This comparison sets out the real differences.

| Factor | SSC JE | RRB JE |
|---|---|---|
| Conducting body | Staff Selection Commission | Railway Recruitment Board |
| Pay Level | Level 6 (Rs 35,400 to 1,12,400) | Level 6 (same scale) |
| Group | Group B | Group C |
| Departments | CPWD, MES, CWC, BRO and others | Indian Railways only |
| Exam cycle | Annual | Irregular |
| Work nature | Site and office, desk-heavy in some departments | Field and maintenance heavy |

SSC JE suits candidates who want a Group B posting across central engineering departments. RRB JE suits those set on a railway career with more field and maintenance work.

## What the job looks like by discipline

The department you join shapes your posting far more than the discipline label. A Civil JE in CPWD supervises construction and maintenance of central government buildings, roads, and public works, splitting time between site inspection and office estimation. A Civil or Mechanical JE in the Central Water Commission works on dams, barrages, and river projects, often at field stations along major rivers. An Electrical JE in CPWD or MES handles the electrical installations, wiring, and load planning of government establishments. MES and BRO postings lean toward defence infrastructure and border roads, which means field-heavy work in tougher locations, and that is partly why those posts allow the diploma-plus-experience route. Reading the duty profile of each department before you rank preferences saves you from a posting that does not fit the life you want.

## Career growth and promotions

SSC JE is an entry into a technical service with a defined ladder, not a terminal post. A Junior Engineer is typically promoted to Assistant Engineer over a career, with departmental exams and seniority both playing a part, and further movement into executive engineer grades is possible in the larger departments like CPWD and MES. Alongside pay progression, government engineers get medical cover, pension benefits under the applicable scheme, and job security that private-sector site engineering rarely matches. For diploma holders in particular, SSC JE is one of the few routes into a Group B gazetted-track career without first completing a degree.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready before the application window opens, since the SSC portal times out if you leave the form to search for files.

1. A recent passport-size photograph and a scanned signature in the SSC-specified format.
2. Your engineering degree or diploma certificate and mark sheets for the qualification and date-of-birth details.
3. An experience certificate, if you apply for a post that needs a diploma plus two years' experience.
4. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) where you claim relaxation.
5. Aadhaar or another government photo ID for the One Time Registration.

## A preparation plan that fits SSC JE

The exam splits neatly into a shared part and a technical part, and your plan should respect that. General Intelligence and Reasoning and General Awareness are common with other SSC exams, so previous SSC papers are the most efficient practice, and General Awareness rewards a steady daily current affairs habit rather than last-week cramming. The General Engineering section in Paper 1 and the full Paper 2 rest on diploma-level fundamentals, so the highest-return work is revising your core discipline subjects until the standard problems become quick. Once your basics are firm, move to previous years' Paper 2 sets under timed conditions, and pay close attention to the harsher Paper 2 negative marking while deciding which questions to leave. A common and avoidable mistake is treating Paper 2 like Paper 1 and guessing freely, which turns a strong technical candidate into a borderline one. Accuracy in the technical paper, not raw attempt count, is what separates selected candidates.

## A note on the numbers you see online

Because the notification is not out, the internet is full of confident-looking SSC JE 2026 vacancy counts and dates that disagree with each other. One page says 3,000 posts, another says the notification is out in one month, a third in another. None of these is sourced to SSC. The only figures worth planning against today are the confirmed 2024 baseline of 1,731 posts across Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical, and the SSC Exam Calendar 2026-27 released on 08 January 2026. Everything else waits for the official notification PDF.

## How to apply and prepare

When the notification opens, apply through the SSC OTR portal at ssc.gov.in, fill the form with your discipline and post preferences, upload a photo and signature, pay the Rs 100 fee if applicable, and submit before the deadline. On preparation, the reasoning and general awareness sections are shared with other SSC exams, so previous SSC papers are the best practice material. The technical papers reward diploma-level fundamentals over exam tricks, so build your discipline basics first and then move to previous years' Paper 2 sets, keeping the harsher Paper 2 negative marking in mind while deciding what to attempt.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is the SSC JE 2026 notification out?**
No. As of 27 July 2026 the SSC JE 2026 notification has not been released. The SSC Exam Calendar 2026-27, released on 08 January 2026, places it later in 2026, and the exact dates and vacancy count will come with the official notification on ssc.gov.in.

**Can a diploma holder apply for SSC JE?**
Yes. A three-year diploma in the relevant engineering discipline is enough for several posts, notably in CPWD and CWC Civil. Some posts in BRO and MES need a degree, or a diploma plus two years of experience.

**How many disciplines are in SSC JE?**
SSC JE has three disciplines in recent cycles: Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical. There is no Quantity Surveying and Contract discipline in the current SSC JE recruitment.

**What is the SSC JE in-hand salary in 2026?**
An SSC JE at Pay Level 6 with a basic of Rs 35,400 takes home about Rs 62,000 a month in a metro, at the 60 percent dearness allowance effective 1 January 2026, after HRA, transport allowance, and deductions.

**How many vacancies will SSC JE 2026 have?**
The 2026 vacancy count is not yet announced. The SSC JE 2024 cycle notified 1,731 posts across Civil, Electrical, and Mechanical, and that figure is the working baseline until the 2026 notification is released.

**Is there an interview in SSC JE?**
No. SSC JE selection is Paper 1, then Paper 2, then document verification and a medical examination. The final merit rests on the combined Paper 1 and Paper 2 marks.

**What is the age limit for SSC JE 2026?**
Most SSC JE posts set an upper age of 30 years, with some CPWD posts allowing up to 32, before relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

**Which is harder, Paper 1 or Paper 2 negative marking?**
Paper 2 is harsher on errors. Paper 1 deducts 0.25 marks per wrong answer, while Paper 2 deducts a full 1 mark, so guessing in the technical paper is far more costly than in Paper 1.

content:
## APPSC Group 2 at a glance

APPSC Group 2 2026 is the Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission's recruitment cycle for 783 non-gazetted and lower-gazetted posts across the Andhra Pradesh state administration, revenue, secretariat, municipal, cooperative, and welfare departments. The exam is conducted jointly for Group 2 (posts that include an interview) and Group 2A (posts filled by written exam only).

The commission notified the 2026 cycle in January 2026 with the online application window running February 15, 2026 to March 15, 2026 on psc.ap.gov.in. The Preliminary screening test is scheduled for June 21, 2026, Mains in September and October 2026, and Interview (Group 2 posts) in December 2026.

Around 5 to 6 lakh candidates typically apply per Group 2 cycle in Andhra Pradesh, giving a 1 in 700 selection ratio for the 783 vacancies. That places Group 2 harder than the parallel Group 3 (ministerial cadre) but easier than the elite APPSC Group 1 exam which recruits Deputy Collectors. Assistant Section Officer at the AP Secretariat and Revenue Divisional Officer are the two most sought-after posts within the Group 2 cadre.

## Posts recruited under APPSC Group 2

The 783 vacancies span 12 post categories in the Secretariat, Revenue, Municipality, Cooperative, and Welfare departments. Group 2A and Group 2 differ mainly in the interview requirement.

| Post | Department | Typical initial posting |
|---|---|---|
| Assistant Section Officer (ASO) | AP Secretariat | Vijayawada Secretariat and Amaravati offices |
| Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) | Revenue | Revenue divisional headquarters within a district |
| Mandal Revenue Officer (MRO) | Revenue | Mandal revenue office |
| Mandal Revenue Inspector | Revenue | Mandal revenue inspection circle |
| Municipal Commissioner Grade III | Municipal Administration (CDMA) | Municipal corporation or municipality |
| Assistant Registrar (Cooperative) | Cooperative | District cooperative office |
| District Backward Classes Welfare Officer | BC Welfare | District BC welfare cell |
| Assistant Commercial Tax Officer | Commercial Taxes | Circle commercial tax office |
| Assistant Section Officer (Legislature) | AP Legislature Secretariat | Legislative Assembly office in Amaravati |
| Extension Officer (Cooperative) | Cooperative | Cooperative society extension office |
| Assistant Labour Officer | Labour | District labour office |
| Junior Assistant across departments | Various | Department-specific postings |

Assistant Section Officer at the Secretariat and RDO are the highest-preferred posts because they carry direct policy exposure and faster progression to higher cadre levels. Mandal Revenue Inspector and Assistant Labour Officer have lighter competition and are useful entry paths for candidates with limited attempts left.

## Who qualifies for APPSC Group 2

APPSC Group 2 has five eligibility conditions that must be satisfied on July 1, 2026.

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Nationality | Indian citizen |
| Age | 18 to 42 years for General category on July 1, 2026 |
| Education | Bachelor's degree from a UGC-recognised university, any stream |
| Nativity | Andhra Pradesh nativity certificate required at document verification |
| Language | Telugu proficiency tested in Mains Paper IV |

Age relaxations follow AP state government norms. Backward Classes (BC) candidates get 5 years extra (up to 47). Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe candidates get 10 years extra (up to 52). Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) get 10 years extra over the applicable category limit. Ex-servicemen relaxations follow AP defence services norms. Serving AP government employees may claim up to 5 years extra subject to continuous service and departmental clearance.

AP nativity is a hard requirement for reserved category benefits and post allocation. Nativity is proved through birth certificate, school records showing continuous 4 years in AP schools, or a nativity certificate issued by the Tahsildar. Candidates whose parents held AP nativity but who studied outside the state should apply for the Tahsildar-issued nativity certificate at least 60 days before applying.

Telugu proficiency for the Mains Paper IV is tested at intermediate level. Candidates who did not study Telugu as a subject at school should start preparing for the Paper IV syllabus at least 6 months before the Mains exam. The commission has clarified that Paper IV is a merit-determining paper and cannot be substituted with another language.

## Application fee and how to apply on psc.ap.gov.in

The commission charges Rs. 250 for General and OBC candidates and Rs. 120 for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates. Fee is paid online only through Net Banking, UPI, or credit and debit card. There is no offline demand draft option since the 2020 digital transition.

1. Open psc.ap.gov.in on Chrome, Firefox, or Edge. Older browsers may fail at the OTP verification screen.
2. Click One Time Registration (OTR). Every APPSC applicant needs an OTR profile that stays valid for all future APPSC exams.
3. Enter your name, date of birth, mobile number, email, and Aadhaar number exactly as they appear on your 10th class certificate.
4. Verify mobile OTP and email OTP. Both are needed.
5. Complete the personal details page including caste category, nativity status, and PwBD certification if applicable.
6. Fill educational qualifications with your graduation degree, university name, roll number, year of passing, and class or percentage.
7. Upload photograph (JPEG, 20 to 50 KB, taken within the last 3 months) and signature (JPEG, 10 to 20 KB, on white background).
8. Log in to your OTR account, select APPSC Group 2 2026 from the current notifications, fill the exam-specific form including post preferences in order of preference, and pay the fee.
9. Submit and download the Confirmation Page. Print two copies for your records.

Common errors and how to fix them. If the mobile OTP does not arrive, telecom spam filters may be blocking APPSC SMS. Wait 5 minutes and retry, or switch to a different mobile. If your photograph gets rejected for size, use online image compressors to reach the 20 to 50 KB band. If your nativity status shows a mismatch, upload the Tahsildar-issued nativity certificate at the document verification stage. Post preference order is locked at submission and cannot be changed later, so decide your priority list before starting the form.

## Selection process: three stages

APPSC uses a three-stage selection process. The Preliminary Examination is a screening filter, the Mains is the merit-determining written test, and the Interview applies only to Group 2 (not Group 2A) posts.

Stage 1 is the Preliminary Examination scheduled for June 21, 2026. This is a single-paper objective test on General Studies and Mental Ability.

| Paper | Marks | Duration | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Studies and Mental Ability | 150 | 2 hours 30 minutes | Multiple choice, no negative marking |

Prelims is qualifying only. Marks are not counted toward the final merit list. Candidates need to score above the category cutoff to advance to Mains. Typically 15 times the number of Mains slots are shortlisted from Prelims, so around 11,750 candidates will qualify for Mains in this cycle.

Stage 2 is the Main Examination, a four-paper descriptive test with 600 total merit marks. All four papers count toward the merit list.

| Paper | Topic | Marks | Included in merit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper I | Essay and English | 150 | Yes |
| Paper II | General Studies I: History, Polity, Economy | 150 | Yes |
| Paper III | General Studies II: Science, Technology, Environment, Current Affairs | 150 | Yes |
| Paper IV | Telugu (language paper) | 150 | Yes |
| Total merit marks | | 600 | |

Stage 3 is the Interview or Personality Test for Group 2 posts only. Group 2A posts (Municipal Commissioner Grade III, Extension Officer, Assistant Labour Officer, and a subset of ASO cadres) are filled based on Mains score alone. The Interview carries 75 marks. Total maximum for Group 2 posts is 600 (Mains) + 75 (Interview) = 675.

## Detailed syllabus and recommended books

APPSC Group 2 syllabus overlaps with the parallel APPSC Group 1 exam and with UPSC Civil Services on core General Studies, but Andhra Pradesh history, geography, economy, and current affairs are the differentiators.

Prelims General Studies covers eight areas. Indian History (Ancient, Medieval, Modern, with focus on AP's role in Satavahana, Ikshvaku, Eastern Chalukya, Vijayanagara, and Nizam periods). Indian Polity (Constitution, Panchayati Raj in AP, state-level administration, AP Reorganisation Act 2014). Indian Economy (five-year plans, AP economy, Polavaram Project). Geography (physical, economic, and AP physical geography including rivers Godavari, Krishna, Pennar). Science and Technology (general awareness, ISRO Sriharikota, pharma sector). General Awareness (schemes, sports, awards). AP-specific General Knowledge (AP formation history 1953 and 1956, post-bifurcation reorganisation 2014, three-capitals debate, chief ministers, state schemes, census data). Mental Ability (arithmetic reasoning, data interpretation, logical reasoning, decision making).

Recommended books for Prelims. Bipin Chandra "India's Struggle for Independence" for modern history. Ram Sharan Sharma "Ancient India" with supplementary reading on Satavahana and Eastern Chalukya dynasties. Laxmikanth "Indian Polity" for constitutional topics. NCERT Class 11 and 12 for economics and geography basics. TMH Lucent Andhra Pradesh Yearbook or AP State Reference Book for AP-specific facts. AP Reorganisation Act 2014 text (available on ap.gov.in) for post-bifurcation legal and financial arrangements. R S Agarwal or M K Pandey for Mental Ability.

Mains Paper II (GS I) focuses on Indian and AP-specific History, Indian Polity, and Indian and AP Economy. Mains Paper III (GS II) focuses on Science and Technology, Environment, and Current Affairs (both national and AP). Both merit papers reward structured answers with introduction, body, and conclusion. Practise writing at least 5 answers per week during the last 3 months before Mains.

Telugu Paper IV covers essay writing, précis writing, grammar, and comprehension in formal Telugu. Recommended books include the AP Intermediate Telugu textbook, "Telugu Vyakaranam" by G N Reddy, and previous year Telugu papers from APPSC and TSPSC (Telangana has a parallel Telugu paper with similar difficulty). Candidates without Telugu-medium schooling should aim for 60 to 70 percent on this paper, which is achievable with 4 to 6 months of structured practice.

## Salary breakdown and career progression

APPSC Group 2 posts fall under the AP Revised Pay Scales 2022, adopted from the recommendations of the AP Pay Revision Commission.

| Post | Pay Level | Basic pay | Gross monthly | In-hand monthly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Assistant Section Officer (Secretariat) | Level 15 | Rs. 40,270 | Rs. 62,000 to Rs. 72,000 | Rs. 52,000 to Rs. 60,000 |
| Revenue Divisional Officer | Level 14 | Rs. 38,890 | Rs. 60,000 to Rs. 70,000 | Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 58,000 |
| Municipal Commissioner Grade III | Level 14 | Rs. 38,890 | Rs. 60,000 to Rs. 70,000 | Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 58,000 |
| Assistant Commercial Tax Officer | Level 14 | Rs. 38,890 | Rs. 58,000 to Rs. 68,000 | Rs. 48,000 to Rs. 56,000 |
| Mandal Revenue Inspector | Level 13 | Rs. 37,100 | Rs. 55,000 to Rs. 65,000 | Rs. 45,000 to Rs. 53,000 |

Gross pay includes Dearness Allowance (currently 32 percent of basic under AP norms), House Rent Allowance (20 percent for Amaravati, Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, and Guntur, 14 percent for other municipal areas, 6 percent elsewhere), Transport Allowance (Rs. 3,600 to Rs. 7,000 per month based on city class), and AP-specific allowances.

Career progression for an Assistant Section Officer at the Secretariat typically moves through Section Officer, Assistant Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Joint Secretary, and Special Secretary in the Secretariat cadre over 25 to 30 years. Reaching Principal Secretary (Level 25 apex scale) requires selection into the elite AP Special Officers cadre or IAS deputation.

Revenue Divisional Officer progression moves through Deputy Collector (through internal promotion after 8 to 10 years), Joint Collector, Additional District Collector, and District Collector. IAS deputation is possible for a small fraction of high-performing RDOs after clearing a Union Public Service Commission promotion process, typically after 15 to 20 years in state service.

Municipal Commissioner Grade III progression moves through Grade II, Grade I, and Special Grade Commissioner over 15 to 20 years, with the potential to reach the Municipal Administration and Urban Development directorate at senior levels.

## Six to twelve month prep timeline

Month 1-2: Complete NCERT History (Class 6-12) with supplementary reading on Satavahana, Eastern Chalukya, and Vijayanagara for AP-specific content. Read Laxmikanth for polity and start daily current affairs from Eenadu, Deccan Chronicle, or The Hindu with AP-specific focus.

Month 3-4: Deep-dive into Indian and AP Geography (physical and economic, especially Godavari-Krishna river basin, Vizag industrial belt, Rayalaseema geography) and Economy (Indian and AP, including Polavaram, agriculture, and industry). Start Telugu Paper IV preparation in parallel; aim for 1 hour per day on Telugu essay and grammar. Write 3 answers per week on GS topics.

Month 5-6: Solve APPSC Group 2 previous year papers from 2016 to 2023 (10 sets minimum). Take at least 5 full-length Prelims mock tests. Focus revision on AP-specific chapters and weak GS areas. Start Mental Ability daily practice (30 questions per day).

Month 7-8: Prelims focused mode. Daily current affairs revision, mock tests every 3 days, and detailed AP GK sweep (chief ministers of AP, YSR-era schemes, Jagan Mohan Reddy schemes, budget highlights, new districts formation, capital dispute status). Prelims on June 21, 2026 sits at the end of this window.

Month 9-12 (post-Prelims): Full Mains preparation mode. Answer writing practice for GS Papers II and III. Telugu Paper IV daily practice with essay writing on AP-current-affairs topics. Interview preparation from Month 11 onwards for candidates confident of Mains qualification.

Candidates with prior UPSC preparation can compress the plan to 6 months by focusing on AP-specific content and Telugu Paper IV, since UPSC prep covers the core GS syllabus adequately. Candidates with prior APPSC Group 1 preparation can compress it to 4 to 5 months since the Group 1 and Group 2 syllabi overlap by around 70 percent.

## Common mistakes candidates make

Seven mistakes account for most APPSC Group 2 rejections across cycles.

Under-preparing AP-specific General Knowledge. Standard UPSC preparation material has minimal AP coverage. APPSC Group 2 Prelims and Mains have 15 to 20 questions each on AP directly (chief ministers, YSR and Jagan schemes, budget, new districts, three-capitals policy, Polavaram, tribal welfare). Missing this is the single biggest score gap.

Ignoring Telugu Paper IV until the last minute. Paper IV carries 150 merit marks and cannot be substituted. Candidates who begin Telugu preparation only 2 months before Mains score 40 to 50 percent on this paper, which drops final rank by 200 to 300 positions.

Wrong post preference order. The commission allocates posts based on merit rank and the preference order given in the application form. Putting Junior Assistant as first preference when the real target is Assistant Section Officer is a common mistake that gets locked at application and cannot be changed later.

Missing the nativity certificate at document verification. Candidates who claim BC, SC, ST reservation or claim AP nativity for post preference must present the Tahsildar-issued nativity certificate at document verification. Missing this document triggers a downgrade to General category or full disqualification.

Skipping the Mental Ability section during Prelims prep. Mental Ability carries around 25 percent of Prelims marks. Candidates focused only on GS often score badly on Mental Ability and fail the Prelims cutoff by a small margin.

Under-answering in Mains. Descriptive papers reward structured answers with introduction, body with sub-points, and conclusion. Wall-of-text or bullet-only answers lose marks compared to structured essays. Practise answer writing weekly from Month 4 onwards.

Ignoring AP current affairs. National current affairs are covered by every candidate. AP-specific current affairs (state budget, new schemes, chief minister announcements, court judgments on the three-capitals issue) differentiate serious candidates. Read Eenadu or Deccan Chronicle daily.

## APPSC Group 2 vs APPSC Group 1 vs UPSC Civil Services

APPSC Group 2 and APPSC Group 1 target different cadre levels within the AP state administration, while UPSC Civil Services recruits into central services and All India Services. This comparison helps candidates decide the right primary target.

| Feature | APPSC Group 2 2026 | APPSC Group 1 (latest cycle) | UPSC Civil Services 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vacancies | 783 | Around 100 to 150 | 1,056 |
| Selection ratio | 1 in 700 | 1 in 3,500 | 1 in 800 |
| Age (General) | 18 to 42 | 18 to 42 | 21 to 32 |
| Attempts limit | No cap, only age ceiling | No cap, only age ceiling | 6 for General, 9 for OBC, unlimited for SC/ST |
| Prelims marks | 150 (qualifying only) | 240 (2 papers, qualifying + eligibility) | 400 |
| Mains marks | 600 merit (4 papers) | 750 merit (5 papers plus optional) | 1,750 merit |
| Interview marks | 75 (Group 2 posts only) | 100 | 275 |
| Total merit ceiling | 675 (Group 2), 600 (Group 2A) | 850 | 2,025 |
| Salary entry | Level 13 to 15 (Rs. 37,100 to 40,270) | Level 20 (Rs. 56,100 basic) | Level 10 (Rs. 56,100 basic) |
| Career ceiling | Principal Secretary rare | Chief Secretary AP possible | Cabinet Secretary direct |
| Home state posting | Guaranteed | Guaranteed | Depends on cadre allocation |
| Prep time typical | 6 to 12 months | 12 to 24 months | 12 to 24 months |
| Syllabus overlap with UPSC | 55 percent | 70 percent | Baseline |

APPSC Group 2 is the right primary target for candidates with AP nativity ties who want a solid state government career with lower competition than Group 1 and shorter preparation timelines than UPSC. APPSC Group 1 is the right target for candidates aiming at the elite Andhra Pradesh administrative service with Deputy Collector-level entry. UPSC is the right target for candidates aiming at national-level cadres with higher career ceilings. Many candidates prepare for all three in parallel because the syllabus overlap allows shared study effort.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who is eligible for APPSC Group 2 2026?**
Indian citizens aged 18 to 42 (General category) with a Bachelor's degree from a UGC-recognised university and AP nativity certification. BC candidates get 5 years extra (up to 47), SC and ST candidates get 10 years extra (up to 52), and PwBD get 10 years over the applicable limit.

**How many vacancies are in APPSC Group 2 2026?**
783 vacancies across 12 post categories including Assistant Section Officer at the Secretariat, Revenue Divisional Officer, Mandal Revenue Officer and Inspector, Municipal Commissioner Grade III, Assistant Registrar (Cooperative), and Assistant Commercial Tax Officer.

**What is the last date to apply for APPSC Group 2 2026?**
March 15, 2026. The online application window opens February 15, 2026 on psc.ap.gov.in. The Preliminary screening test is scheduled for June 21, 2026.

**Is AP nativity mandatory for APPSC Group 2?**
Yes for post allocation and reservation benefits. Non-AP candidates can apply but cannot claim BC, SC, ST reservation and cannot get posts reserved for AP nativity holders. A Tahsildar-issued nativity certificate is verified at the document verification stage.

**How much is the application fee?**
Rs. 250 for General and OBC candidates. Rs. 120 for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates. Payment is online only through Net Banking, UPI, or credit and debit card. There is no offline payment option.

**What is the exam pattern for APPSC Group 2 2026?**
Three stages. Prelims is one 150-mark General Studies and Mental Ability paper (qualifying only). Mains is four papers of 150 marks each (Essay and English, GS I, GS II, Telugu), totalling 600 merit marks. Interview is 75 marks for Group 2 posts only.

**What is the salary of an APPSC Group 2 Assistant Section Officer?**
Pay Level 15 in AP Revised Pay Scales 2022, basic pay Rs. 40,270. Gross monthly Rs. 62,000 to Rs. 72,000 including DA, HRA, and other allowances. In-hand around Rs. 52,000 to Rs. 60,000 after standard deductions.

**Is Telugu Paper IV compulsory?**
Yes for all Group 2 and Group 2A applicants. Telugu Paper IV carries 150 merit marks in Mains and cannot be substituted with any other language. Candidates without Telugu-medium schooling need at least 6 months of structured Telugu preparation.

**How many attempts can I make for APPSC Group 2?**
No cap on total attempts. Only the upper age limit (42 for General, 47 for BC, 52 for SC and ST) applies. You can appear as many times as the age ceiling allows.

**Should I prepare for APPSC Group 2 alongside APPSC Group 1?**
Yes if you have AP nativity and 12 to 24 months of preparation runway. The Group 2 and Group 1 syllabi overlap by around 70 percent. Group 2 becomes a strong fallback if you clear Prelims for both, and the shared preparation time is far more efficient than serial attempts.

content:
## UPSSSC Lower PCS 2026: main exam on 23 August

The Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission is recruiting for its Combined Lower Subordinate Services Examination at graduate level under Advertisement 07-Exam/2026, and the main examination is on 23 August 2026 from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon.

That is eleven days away at the time of writing.

Applications ran from 29 May 2026 and closed on 25 June 2026 after an extension from the original date of 18 June. Vacancy figures have been reported at various points as around 2,285, then 2,516 following an increase, and 2,587, so the position is best described as roughly 2,500 posts with the exact figure confirmed in the commission's own notices rather than in secondary reporting.

Around 1,00,492 candidates were shortlisted for the main examination on the basis of their normalised PET 2025 scores. Against roughly 2,587 vacancies, that is about 39 candidates per post at the mains stage, which is the honest competition position.

## The PET gateway, and why it matters more than this exam

This is the structural feature that defines UPSSSC recruitment and it is where candidates most often misunderstand the process.

UPSSSC does not run each recruitment as a standalone examination open to all graduates. It runs a common Preliminary Eligibility Test, the PET, and a valid PET score is the precondition for applying to any UPSSSC recruitment. Without one you cannot apply, however well qualified you are.

For this recruitment, the PET 2025 score is what was required. Candidates holding a valid PET 2025 scorecard could apply; those without one could not, and no amount of preparation for the main examination changes that.

Three consequences follow, and they matter for planning a UPSSSC career rather than just this attempt.

The PET is the real bottleneck. Around a lakh candidates were shortlisted here from a PET field that is far larger, so the PET determines who reaches the door and this examination determines who gets through it.

Your PET score has a validity period, and within that window it opens every UPSSSC recruitment advertised. A good PET score is therefore an asset across multiple recruitments rather than a single one, which is why it deserves serious preparation in its own right.

If you do not currently hold a valid PET score, the practical step is to prepare for and sit the next PET rather than tracking individual recruitment notifications you cannot apply to. That is the sequencing candidates get wrong most often.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Advertisement | 07-Exam/2026 |
| Applications opened | 29 May 2026 |
| Applications closed | 25 June 2026, extended from 18 June |
| Main examination | 23 August 2026, 10:00 am to 12:00 noon |
| Shortlisted for mains | About 1,00,492 candidates on normalised PET 2025 scores |

The two-hour window for the main paper is worth noting. This is a compact examination rather than a long one, which places a premium on pace.

## What the posts are

Combined Lower Subordinate Services covers a range of Group C posts across Uttar Pradesh government departments, filled through a single examination rather than separately.

The posts recruited under this heading typically include supply inspector, excise constable-level and inspector posts, marketing inspector, revenue-side positions, cane supervisor, and a variety of assistant and inspector roles across departments such as food and civil supplies, excise, revenue, cane development, panchayati raj and others.

Because the advertisement covers multiple posts across departments, candidates express post preferences and allocation follows merit, preference and vacancy position. The exact post list, department-wise vacancy distribution and any post-specific eligibility conditions are set out in the advertisement, and that is the document to read rather than a general description.

One practical point: some posts within such combined recruitments carry additional requirements or tests, such as a physical standard for field-facing roles or a specific subject qualification. Check whether any post you have preferenced carries such a condition, since it applies in addition to the general eligibility.

## Main examination pattern

The main examination is a written paper of two hours, held on 23 August 2026 from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon.

The subject coverage for UPSSSC graduate-level main examinations generally spans Hindi language and grammar, general knowledge with substantial weight on Uttar Pradesh, general intelligence and reasoning, current affairs, and elementary arithmetic, with the exact section-wise composition and marks distribution fixed in the advertisement for the cycle.

Because the commission sets the paper structure per recruitment and it has varied between advertisements, the authoritative source for your paper is the advertisement and any subsequent notice on upsssc.gov.in rather than a general description of UPSSSC papers.

What is consistent across UPSSSC examinations is the emphasis on Uttar Pradesh material. State geography, districts and divisions, rivers, agriculture, industries, historical sites, culture, administration, and current state schemes and appointments recur reliably. This is the highest-yield portion of the syllabus and the part where candidates from the state hold an advantage that out-of-state candidates rarely close.

## Preparing in the remaining days

With eleven days to the paper, the work is revision and practice rather than new study.

Concentrate on Uttar Pradesh general knowledge. It is the largest predictable block in the paper and the material is finite: districts, rivers, parks, tribes, festivals, historical sites, state schemes and recent state-level developments can be revised to near-completeness in the time available, which is not true of any other section.

Revise current affairs of roughly the past year, with attention to Uttar Pradesh specifically alongside national developments.

Practise reasoning and arithmetic under timed conditions rather than reading theory. Both are trainable and both reward pace on a two-hour paper.

Work Hindi language and grammar deliberately if your schooling was in another medium. Sandhi, samas, tatsam and tadbhav, idioms, and error correction are rule-based and respond to focused revision quickly.

Take at least two full papers under the two-hour clock in the final week, and use the analysis to fix time allocation rather than only to count marks.

## What happens after the main examination

Following the main examination, the process continues through document verification and, for posts that require it, additional stages such as a skill test or physical standards, before the final merit list and appointment.

Final merit for most UPSSSC recruitments rests on the main examination score, with the PET serving as a screening stage whose marks do not carry into the final ranking. Confirm that for this recruitment in the advertisement, since the commission specifies the merit basis there.

Document verification is where candidatures are lost on paperwork rather than performance. Assemble your documents now rather than after the result: educational certificates, proof of date of birth, category certificate in the Uttar Pradesh format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, domicile documents, and identity documents matching your application. A discrepancy between a name or date across documents is a common and avoidable problem.

## Salary and what these posts pay

Group C posts recruited through this examination sit in the Uttar Pradesh state pay structure, with the specific pay level varying by post.

Entry pay for graduate-level Group C posts in the state services generally falls in the range associated with pay levels in the lower-middle band of the state matrix, with dearness allowance, house rent allowance depending on the classification of the posting city, and other admissible allowances on top of basic pay. The advertisement states the pay scale for each post, and that is the figure to rely on rather than a general estimate, since the posts covered here differ.

Beyond pay, these are permanent state government posts carrying the leave, medical and pension entitlements applicable to Uttar Pradesh government employees, along with promotion prospects within the departmental hierarchy.

## Career progression

Group C posts in the state services progress through departmental promotion, and the pace depends on the department and the vacancy position in the higher grades.

Alongside promotion, a serving employee who holds a graduate degree and remains within the age band can appear for higher recruitments, including the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission examinations for gazetted posts and other UPSSSC recruitments at higher levels. Many candidates use a Group C post as a stable base from which to prepare for those, since the working hours in most such roles allow it and the position provides income security during preparation.

Our [UPPSC PCS](/sarkari-naukri/uppsc-pcs-2026) page covers the state's gazetted-level route for candidates considering that progression.

It is worth being clear about the distinction between the two, since the names invite confusion. This recruitment is Lower Subordinate Services, conducted by UPSSSC for Group C posts, gated by the PET. UPPSC PCS is the Provincial Civil Services examination conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission for gazetted posts including Deputy Collector and Deputy Superintendent of Police, with its own preliminary, mains and interview structure and no PET requirement. They are different examinations, different commissions and different levels of the state service, despite both containing the letters PCS.

A candidate whose target is the gazetted service should be preparing for UPPSC rather than UPSSSC, and the general studies base overlaps enough that a serving Group C employee can work towards it while employed.

## Parallel options worth applying to

Because UPSSSC recruitments are advertised irregularly and gated by PET validity, a graduate targeting government employment should keep other applications running rather than waiting on one commission.

Central graduate-level recruitment runs on its own calendar and needs no state-specific gateway: [SSC CGL](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-cgl-2026) for central government posts, [RRB NTPC](/sarkari-naukri/rrb-ntpc-2026) for graduate railway posts, and the banking examinations including [IBPS PO](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-po-2026) and [IBPS Clerk](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-clerk-2026).

The preparation base overlaps substantially. Reasoning, arithmetic, English or Hindi language and general awareness serve all of them, and only the state-specific general knowledge is particular to UPSSSC. A candidate who has prepared Uttar Pradesh general knowledge thoroughly for UPSSSC has done work that does not transfer, but everything else does.

The practical approach is to treat the UP-specific material as the addition rather than the foundation, and to apply to every central and state recruitment your qualification permits in a given year rather than concentrating on one.

## How to apply in the next cycle

Applications for this recruitment are closed. For a future UPSSSC recruitment, the sequence is what matters.

1. Sit the Preliminary Eligibility Test and obtain a valid PET score. Without this you cannot apply to any UPSSSC recruitment, so it is the first step rather than a parallel one.
2. Register on upsssc.gov.in and complete the one-time registration, which the commission reuses across its recruitments.
3. Watch for advertisements you are eligible for and apply within the window, quoting your valid PET score.
4. Fill personal, educational and category details exactly as on your certificates, since these feed both eligibility and reservation.
5. Enter post preferences carefully, as allocation follows merit and preference together.
6. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format and pay the fee.
7. Submit, save the application, and download the admit card when released.

## Understanding the PET properly

Since the PET governs access to every UPSSSC recruitment, it deserves more than a passing mention for anyone planning a UP state government career.

The Preliminary Eligibility Test is a screening examination conducted for graduate-level and intermediate-level candidates separately, producing a score that remains valid for a defined period. During that validity, the score is quoted on applications to UPSSSC recruitments as they are advertised.

The design intent is administrative. UPSSSC advertises many recruitments across many departments, and running a separate preliminary stage for each would be enormously expensive and slow. A single common screening test, with a score reused across advertisements, replaces that.

For a candidate the implication is a change of strategy. Rather than preparing intensively for whichever recruitment happens to be advertised, the sensible approach is to prepare seriously for the PET once, secure a strong normalised score, and then apply to every advertisement your qualification permits during the validity window. A candidate with a strong PET score and a modest number of applications is worse placed than one with the same score and many.

The PET syllabus covers ground that overlaps heavily with the mains: Indian history and the national movement, geography, economy, polity and administration, general science, elementary arithmetic, general Hindi, reasoning, current affairs and, importantly, Uttar Pradesh-specific general knowledge. That overlap means PET preparation is not separate from mains preparation; it is the foundation of it.

Normalisation applies to PET scores, since the test runs across shifts, so your usable score is the normalised one rather than your raw marks.

## Common mistakes in UPSSSC applications

Not holding a valid PET score and preparing for the mains anyway. This is the most consequential error, since the application is simply not possible, and it is entirely avoidable by checking the requirement before starting.

Treating the PET as a formality. It determines who reaches the mains across every recruitment, so a mediocre PET score constrains an entire validity period rather than one attempt.

Filling post preferences casually. Allocation follows merit and preference together, so an order that does not reflect what you actually want can produce a posting in a department you would not have chosen.

Ignoring post-specific conditions. Some posts in a combined recruitment carry physical standards or subject requirements, and a candidate who preferences one without meeting them loses the allocation at verification.

Neglecting the Uttar Pradesh portion of general knowledge. It is the most reliably recurring and highest-yield section in UPSSSC papers, and candidates who prepare only national-level material give away marks that are freely available.

Assembling documents after the result. Document verification is where candidatures are lost on paperwork, and category or domicile certificates in the wrong format take weeks to correct.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the UPSSSC Lower PCS 2026 main exam?**
The main examination is on 23 August 2026 from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon, under Advertisement 07-Exam/2026 for the Combined Lower Subordinate Services Examination at graduate level. Applications ran from 29 May 2026 and closed on 25 June 2026 after an extension from 18 June.

**How many vacancies are in UPSSSC Lower PCS 2026?**
Roughly 2,500. Figures have been reported at various points as around 2,285, then 2,516 following an increase, and 2,587, so the exact number should be confirmed from the commission's own notices rather than secondary reporting. Around 1,00,492 candidates were shortlisted for the mains, which works out to about 39 candidates per post.

**What is the PET and why do I need it for UPSSSC recruitments?**
The Preliminary Eligibility Test is UPSSSC's common screening examination, and a valid PET score is the precondition for applying to any UPSSSC recruitment. Without one you cannot apply regardless of your qualifications. For this recruitment the PET 2025 score was required. The PET is therefore the real bottleneck in UPSSSC recruitment, and a good score opens every recruitment advertised during its validity period.

**Can I apply for UPSSSC Lower PCS without a PET score?**
No. A valid PET scorecard is mandatory to apply. If you do not hold one, the correct step is to prepare for and sit the next PET rather than tracking recruitment notifications you cannot apply to, which is the sequencing candidates most often get wrong.

**Do PET marks count in the final merit?**
For most UPSSSC recruitments the PET is a screening stage whose marks do not carry into the final ranking, with final merit resting on the main examination score. Confirm the position for this specific recruitment in the advertisement, since the commission specifies the merit basis there.

**What is the UPSSSC Lower PCS main exam pattern?**
A written paper of two hours on 23 August 2026. Subject coverage for UPSSSC graduate-level mains generally spans Hindi language and grammar, general knowledge with substantial Uttar Pradesh weight, general intelligence and reasoning, current affairs and elementary arithmetic. The exact section-wise composition and marks are fixed in the advertisement, which has varied between recruitments, so read that rather than a general description.

**Which posts are covered under Combined Lower Subordinate Services?**
A range of Group C posts across Uttar Pradesh government departments, typically including supply inspector, excise-side posts, marketing inspector, revenue positions, cane supervisor and various assistant and inspector roles in departments such as food and civil supplies, excise, revenue, cane development and panchayati raj. The exact list and department-wise distribution is in the advertisement, and some posts carry additional requirements such as physical standards.

**What should I study in the last week before the exam?**
Uttar Pradesh general knowledge above all, since it is the largest predictable block and the material is finite enough to revise to near-completeness in the time available. Then current affairs of the past year with attention to state-level developments, then timed practice on reasoning and arithmetic rather than theory reading, and focused revision of Hindi grammar rules if your schooling was in another medium.

**How competitive is UPSSSC Lower PCS 2026?**
About 1,00,492 candidates were shortlisted for roughly 2,587 vacancies, which is approximately 39 candidates per post at the main examination stage. That is demanding but considerably better than the ratios in the largest all-India recruitments, and the Uttar Pradesh general knowledge weighting means well-prepared candidates from the state are competing against a field where that advantage is common rather than rare.

**What is the salary for UPSSSC Lower PCS posts?**
These are Group C posts in the Uttar Pradesh state pay structure, with the specific pay level varying by post, plus dearness allowance, house rent allowance by city classification and other admissible allowances. The advertisement states the pay scale for each post individually and that is the figure to rely on, since the posts covered under this recruitment differ from one another.

**What happens after the main examination?**
Document verification, and for posts requiring it additional stages such as a skill test or physical standards, before the final merit list and appointment. Document verification is where candidatures are commonly lost on paperwork rather than performance, so assemble educational certificates, date of birth proof, category certificate in the Uttar Pradesh format, domicile documents and matching identity documents now rather than after the result.

**Can I move to a higher post after joining?**
Yes, through departmental promotion, at a pace depending on the department and vacancies in higher grades. Separately, a serving employee holding a graduate degree and within the age band can sit higher recruitments including the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission examinations for gazetted posts. Many candidates use a Group C post as a stable base from which to prepare for those, since it provides income security during preparation.

content:
## SBI SO 2026: what it really is

SBI Specialist Cadre Officer recruitment is not a single exam the way SBI PO is. The State Bank of India, through its Central Recruitment and Promotion Department (CRPD), runs several independent Specialist Cadre Officer advertisements through the year, each for a different set of specialist roles, and each with its own vacancy count, eligibility, selection method, and dates. Advertisements are numbered in the form CRPD/SCO/[year]/[serial]. So there is no common SBI SO exam date or single vacancy number, and any page that gives you one is oversimplifying.

This is the single biggest confusion around SBI SO, and getting it right saves you from chasing a notification that does not match your qualification. If you are a lawyer, a chartered accountant, an IT auditor, or a doctor, the SBI SO advertisement that matters to you is the one for your specialism, not a generic SBI SO exam.

One practical note first: SBI has moved its careers portal to sbi.bank.in. The current advertisements and application links live at sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings, while the CRPD contact email remains crpd@sbi.co.in. Many other sites still point you to the old sbi.co.in address, which now redirects.

## Regular versus contractual posts

SBI hires specialists on two very different footings, and the difference decides your pay, security, and career path.

Regular basis posts are permanent SBI officer-cadre roles, graded on SBI's own scales such as Junior Management Grade Scale I and Middle Management Grade Scale II and III. They come with probation, the full allowance structure, provident fund, pension contribution, and the same promotion ladder as other SBI officers. These are governed by SBI service rules, not by a central government pay commission.

Contractual basis posts are fixed-term hires, usually for about five years and renewable on performance, paid a consolidated cost to company rather than a regular pay scale, and outside the pension structure. SBI uses the contractual route mostly for wealth management, senior IT and digital roles, and some specialist verticals. The pay can be high, but the security and long-term benefits differ from a regular post.

Knowing which basis an advertisement is for is the first thing to check, because it changes what the job is worth over a career and whether it comes with a pension at the end of it.

## Role families SBI recruits as SO

Across its advertisements, SBI hires specialists in these broad families.

| Role family | Typical basis | Example posts |
|---|---|---|
| Law | Regular | Assistant Manager and Deputy Manager (Law) |
| Finance and audit | Regular | Chartered Accountant, IS Audit officers |
| Information technology | Regular and contractual | IT, data, and digital specialists |
| Medical | Regular | Bank Medical Officer |
| Wealth management | Contractual | Relationship managers, customer relationship executives |

Historically SBI has also run advertisements for risk, credit, marketing, human resources, and systems roles, so the exact families open in any year depend on the bank's needs. This is why two people can both be preparing for SBI SO yet be chasing completely different advertisements with nothing in common except the employer.

## Confirmed 2026 advertisements

These are the Specialist Cadre Officer advertisements confirmed for the 2026-27 recruitment year. Vacancy counts are stated per advertisement, as SBI publishes them, rather than as one combined figure.

| Advertisement | Role | Basis | Vacancies |
|---|---|---|---|
| CRPD/SCO/2026-27/02 | Law (Assistant and Deputy Manager) | Regular | 49 |
| CRPD/SCO/2026-27/03 | Bank Medical Officer | Regular | 35 |
| CRPD/SCO/2025-26/27 | IS Audit and Chartered Accountant | Regular and contract | 116 (reported) |
| CRPD/SCO/2025-26/17 | Wealth management (relationship roles) | Contractual | reported figures vary |

The widely quoted "84 vacancies SBI SCO 2026" figure is simply the Law advertisement (49) plus the Bank Medical Officer advertisement (35), both opened on 24 June 2026. The IS Audit and Chartered Accountant and wealth management counts come from secondary sources, so treat those as reported and confirm them against the official advertisement before relying on them.

## The Law advertisement in detail

The Law advertisement, CRPD/SCO/2026-27/02 dated 24 June 2026, is the one with the fullest confirmed detail, and it is a useful model for how a regular SBI SO advertisement works.

It has 49 vacancies: 20 for Assistant Manager (Law) in Junior Management Grade Scale I, and 29 for Deputy Manager (Law) in Middle Management Grade Scale II, including two backlog posts. The cut-off date for age, qualification, and experience is 31 May 2026.

On age, Assistant Manager needs 25 to 32 years and Deputy Manager needs 25 to 35 years for the unreserved category, with standard relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates. On qualification, both need a law degree from a recognised Indian university. On experience as an enrolled advocate, Assistant Manager needs 2 years and Deputy Manager needs 4 years of practice, whether at the bar, as a law officer in a scheduled commercial bank, or a combination; internships and teaching do not count.

The application fee is Rs 750 for General, EWS, and OBC candidates, and nil for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates. The application window ran from 24 June to 14 July 2026.

## Selection varies by advertisement

A common error on other sites is the flat claim that SBI SO selection is only shortlisting plus interview with no written exam. That is wrong for some advertisements. The correct picture is that selection depends on the advertisement.

The Law advertisement, for example, has an online written test followed by an interview. Its written test carries an objective portion, where reasoning and English are qualifying and professional knowledge counts for merit, plus a descriptive portion of law subjects, with the written test tentatively in August 2026. The final merit for the Law posts is weighted 70 percent to the written test and 30 percent to the interview.

Other advertisements, such as the Bank Medical Officer post, are shortlisting based, where SBI screens applications against the eligibility bar and calls qualified candidates directly for an interview. So before you prepare, read your specific advertisement to know whether you face a written test or a shortlisting.

## Eligibility depends on the post

Because each advertisement targets a different specialism, eligibility varies. A Law post needs a law degree and years of advocacy experience. A Chartered Accountant post needs the CA qualification and post-qualification audit or finance experience. An IS Audit post needs an engineering or computer degree with information security experience. A Bank Medical Officer post needs an MBBS. Almost all regular SO posts, unlike SBI PO, require relevant work experience, so freshers are generally not eligible except where an advertisement specifically allows it.

## Application fee

Across recent regular advertisements the fee has been Rs 750 for General, EWS, and OBC candidates and nil for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates, paid online. Always confirm the fee in the specific advertisement, since it can vary.

## SBI SO salary and pay scales

Regular SBI SO posts are paid on SBI's own officer pay scales, not the central government pay commission, so the dearness allowance follows SBI's bipartite settlement. The two scales most SO posts start on are Junior Management Grade Scale I, with a basic scale of Rs 48,480 to Rs 85,920, and Middle Management Grade Scale II, with a basic scale of Rs 64,820 to Rs 93,960. On top of basic pay come dearness allowance, house rent allowance, city compensatory allowance, provident fund, pension contribution, and medical and leave benefits, so the in-hand and cost to company are well above the basic figures.

Contractual posts, by contrast, are paid a consolidated cost to company set in the advertisement, often with performance incentives, and they sit outside the regular scale and pension. Senior contractual specialist roles can carry a high cost to company, but you should read the exact figure and the contract terms in the specific advertisement rather than a general range.

## SBI SO versus SBI PO

Candidates sometimes weigh SBI SO against [SBI PO](/sarkari-naukri/sbi-po-2026). They are quite different routes.

| Factor | SBI SO | SBI PO |
|---|---|---|
| Nature | Specialist roles by qualification | Generalist officer |
| Entry | Multiple role-wise advertisements | One annual exam |
| Experience | Usually required | Not required |
| Selection | Varies (written test or shortlisting) plus interview | Prelims, mains, and Phase III |
| Career | Grows within the specialism | Broad branch and management track |

SBI PO suits a fresh graduate wanting a general banking career. SBI SO suits a qualified specialist, such as a lawyer or a chartered accountant, who wants to bring that expertise into the bank.

## How to track SBI SO openings

Because SBI SO advertisements appear through the year rather than on one fixed date, the practical skill is watching for the one that fits you. Check the SBI careers portal at sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings regularly, since new advertisements are posted there first, and the application windows are often short, running only two to three weeks. It helps to know your own eligibility profile in advance, meaning your qualification, your exact years of relevant experience, and the scale you would enter, so that when an advertisement for your specialism opens you can apply quickly rather than scrambling to gather documents. Setting a reminder to check the portal weekly is a simple habit that stops you missing a narrow window. Reputable exam-tracking sites can alert you too, but always confirm the details on the official portal, since secondary sites sometimes carry stale dates or vacancy numbers.

## SBI SO is not IBPS SO

One more disambiguation worth stating plainly. SBI SO is conducted by the State Bank of India for its own specialist posts. IBPS SO is a separate recruitment by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection for specialist officer posts across many public-sector banks, with its own exam and notification. They share the phrase Specialist Officer but are different organisations and different processes, so do not mix up their notifications.

## The IS Audit, CA, and wealth advertisements

Beyond the Law and Medical drives, two other 2026-27 recruitment-year advertisements are worth knowing, though their finer details come from secondary sources and should be confirmed against the official PDFs.

The IS Audit and Chartered Accountant advertisement, CRPD/SCO/2025-26/27, was reported to carry 116 posts across roles like Assistant Vice President and Deputy Manager in IS Audit, and Deputy Manager for Chartered Accountant internal audit. These posts need an engineering, computer, or CA qualification with post-qualification experience in audit, information security, or accounting, so freshers are not eligible. Some of the senior posts are contractual and carry a high cost to company, which is why they draw experienced professionals from outside banking.

The wealth management advertisement, CRPD/SCO/2025-26/17, covered relationship roles such as Vice President Wealth, Assistant Vice President Wealth, and Customer Relationship Executive, on a contractual basis with a five-year renewable term and performance-linked incentives. These roles manage high-net-worth clients and are paid a consolidated cost to company. Reported vacancy figures for the wealth drive vary widely across sites, so treat any single number as unconfirmed until you read the official advertisement.

## What a specialist officer actually does

A Specialist Cadre Officer brings a specific expertise into the bank rather than rotating through general branch work. A Law officer handles the bank's legal matters, from documentation and recovery cases to advising branches on compliance. A Chartered Accountant or IS Audit officer works on internal audit, financial controls, and information-security review. A Bank Medical Officer runs the bank's medical services for staff. A wealth relationship manager advises and services the bank's high-net-worth customers. Because the work is specialised, these officers are often posted at controlling offices, zonal offices, or specialised branches rather than every small branch, which is a different working life from a generalist officer.

## Career growth for specialist officers

A regular Specialist Cadre Officer grows within the officer hierarchy much like other SBI officers, moving from the entry scale into Middle Management and Senior Management grades over a career, while deepening the specialism they were hired for. The path tends to stay within the function, so a Law officer builds a legal career inside the bank and an audit officer builds an audit and controls career, rather than moving into general branch management. For an experienced professional, this is often the appeal: a stable, well-paid role that uses hard-won expertise, with the security and benefits of a public-sector bank. Contractual specialists, by contrast, are engaged for the term of the contract, and their continuation depends on renewal, so their path is shaped by performance and the bank's ongoing need for the role.

## Documents you will need

Because SO posts turn on qualification and experience, the documents matter more than in a generalist exam.

1. Your professional qualification certificates and mark sheets, such as the law degree, CA certificate, engineering degree, or MBBS.
2. Experience certificates that prove the exact years and nature of experience the advertisement demands.
3. For advocates, the Bar Council enrolment certificate and proof of practice.
4. A category certificate where you claim relaxation, and a PwBD certificate where applicable.
5. A recent photograph, signature, and a valid photo ID matching your application.

The experience proof is the item most applications stumble on, so make sure your certificates state the dates and role clearly, since vague letters are often rejected at verification.

## Preparing for a written-test advertisement

For advertisements that include an online written test, such as the Law post, the professional knowledge section is where the exam is won, because reasoning and English are only qualifying. That means your revision should centre on the core subjects of your specialism, at the depth a practising professional is expected to know, rather than on general aptitude. For the Law post, that spans constitutional, administrative, and financial-sector laws, procedural codes, the newer labour codes, and drafting. The descriptive portion rewards clear, well-structured answers written to the point within the word limit, so practising a few timed written answers in your subject is worth more than reading more theory. For shortlisting-based advertisements, there is no written test to prepare, so the effort goes into a strong application that clearly evidences your eligibility and into interview preparation on your specialism and on current banking topics.

## Why SBI SO is worth considering

For a qualified professional, an SBI Specialist Cadre Officer role offers something a generalist exam cannot: a job that pays for the expertise you already hold, in the country's largest bank, with the stability and benefits of a regular officer post. The entry is less of a lottery than SBI PO, because the field is limited to those with the specific qualification and experience, and a strong professional record counts. The trade-off is that openings appear as and when the bank needs a specialism, so you have to watch the careers portal and be ready to apply within a short window when your advertisement appears.

## How to apply for an SBI SO post

1. Open the SBI careers portal at sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings and find the advertisement for your specialism.
2. Read the full advertisement PDF for eligibility, experience, selection method, fee, and dates.
3. Register with a valid email and mobile number, then fill the application form.
4. Upload your photograph, signature, and the required qualification and experience documents.
5. Pay the fee online if your category is charged, and submit before the advertisement's last date.
6. Track the same portal for the written test call letter or the interview call, depending on your advertisement.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is there a single SBI SO exam every year?**
No. SBI SO is not one exam. The State Bank of India runs several separate Specialist Cadre Officer advertisements through the year, each for a different specialism, with its own vacancies, eligibility, selection method, and dates, numbered as CRPD/SCO/year/serial.

**What is the difference between SBI SO and SBI PO?**
SBI PO is a single annual exam for generalist Probationary Officers and needs no work experience. SBI SO is a set of role-wise advertisements for specialists such as lawyers, chartered accountants, IT auditors, and doctors, and most SO posts require relevant experience.

**Does SBI SO recruitment have a written exam or only an interview?**
It depends on the advertisement. The 2026 Law advertisement has an online written test plus an interview with 70 to 30 weightage, while the Bank Medical Officer advertisement is shortlisting based with an interview. Always check your specific advertisement.

**What is the difference between regular and contractual SBI SO posts?**
Regular posts are permanent SBI officer-cadre roles on SBI's own pay scales with pension and full benefits. Contractual posts are fixed-term hires, usually about five years and renewable, paid a consolidated cost to company and outside the pension structure.

**What is the SBI SO salary and pay scale?**
Regular SBI SO posts start on SBI's own scales, mainly Junior Management Grade Scale I (Rs 48,480 to Rs 85,920) and Middle Management Grade Scale II (Rs 64,820 to Rs 93,960), plus dearness and other allowances under the SBI settlement, not the central pay commission.

**What was the SBI SCO 84 vacancy 2026 recruitment?**
The 84-vacancy figure is the 2026 Law advertisement (49 posts) plus the Bank Medical Officer advertisement (35 posts), both opened on 24 June 2026. It is not a single combined SBI SO exam but two separate advertisements counted together.

**Where do I apply for SBI SO?**
Apply on the SBI careers portal at sbi.bank.in/web/careers/current-openings, which now hosts the current openings. Older references to sbi.co.in redirect to the new address. Read the specific advertisement PDF before applying.

**Is SBI SO the same as IBPS SO?**
No. SBI SO is conducted by the State Bank of India for its own posts. IBPS SO is a separate recruitment by the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection for specialist officers across many public-sector banks, with a different exam and notification.

**Stage 1: Computer Based Test.** A single objective paper covering mathematics, general intelligence and reasoning, general science, and general awareness including current affairs, with the technical component weighted according to the grade applied for.
